title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
河南鄉試錄序 〔亦閣〕
萬曆丙子河南復當賓興士
巡按御史趙〔煥〕寔監臨之先
是
上寤寐賢喆嘉慕古作人之道謂
科條未備而士習稍竊用
帷幄大臣言赫然下
===
璽書布功令廣厲學官郡國有司
靡不兢兢然奉
上德意冀得眞才以塞
明詔學官弟子亦靡不喁喁然引
領企踵冀攄所蘊蓄以自獻
蓋一時人文之盛視昔攺觀
云于時御史遵故事聘〔有敷〕
punctuated:
河南鄉試錄序〔亦閣〕
萬曆丙子，河南復當賓興士，巡按御史趙〔煥〕寔監臨之。先是，上寤寐賢喆，嘉慕古作人之道，謂科條未備而士習稍竊，用帷幄大臣言，赫然下璽書，布功令，廣厲學官。郡國有司靡不兢兢然奉上德意，冀得眞才以塞明詔；學官弟子亦靡不喁喁然引領企踵，冀攄所蘊蓄以自獻。蓋一時人文之盛，視昔攺觀云。于時，御史遵故事，聘〔有敷〕
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Henan Provincial Examination [Yige (?)]
In the bingzi year of the Wanli era (1576), it was once again time for Henan to recommend and promote scholars as honored guests, and the Regional Inspector, Censor Zhao [Huan] 趙煥, truly served as the Supervising Official for the examination. Prior to this, His Majesty had been longing day and night for men of worth and wisdom, admiring the ancient way of cultivating talent. Deeming that the examination regulations were not yet complete and that the habits of scholars had grown somewhat corrupt [? 稍竊, likely a misprint for 稍媮/稍靡], he acted upon the advice of the Grand Secretaries of the inner council and majestically issued an imperial edict under the imperial seal, promulgating the official statutes to broadly encourage and spur on the Confucian schools. Among the local authorities of the prefectures and counties, there were none who did not reverently and cautiously uphold His Majesty's virtuous intentions, hoping to obtain true talent in order to fulfill the brilliant decree; and among the students of the schools, there were likewise none who did not eagerly crane their necks and stand on tiptoe, hoping to pour forth what they had accumulated within to present themselves to the throne. Indeed, the flourishing of literary culture at this moment had taken on a new appearance compared to the past. At this time, the Censor followed precedent and invited me, [Youfu] …

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
暨教諭俞〔應星〕司考試學正
齊〔柯〕教諭林〔長清〕蔣〔養成〕王
〔同任〕朱〔廷輔〕余〔純然〕張〔汝翎〕
同考試提調則左布政使周
〔鑑〕左叅政吳〔國倫〕監試則按
察使鄭〔雲鎣〕僉事徐〔學詩〕暨
百執事皆就列受約束維慈
維春乃合提學副使趙〔奮〕所
===
簡士二千四百人有奇三試
之拔其儁八十人幷錄其文
貢于
廷〔有敷〕不佞以職事宜宣言于
首簡粵稽古昔郡國任土成
賦徵其名物以輸將于天府
punctuated: 暨教諭俞〔應星〕司考試，學正齊〔柯〕，教諭林〔長清〕、蔣〔養成〕、王〔同任〕、朱〔廷輔〕、余〔純然〕、張〔汝翎〕同考試。提調則左布政使周〔鑑〕、左叅政吳〔國倫〕，監試則按察使鄭〔雲鎣〕、僉事徐〔學詩〕，暨百執事皆就列受約束。維慈、維春乃合提學副使趙〔奮〕所簡士二千四百人有奇，三試之，拔其儁八十人，幷錄其文貢于廷。〔有敷〕不佞，以職事宜宣言于首簡。粵稽古昔，郡國任土成賦，徵其名物以輸將于天府，
translation_en: … along with County Director of Studies Yu Yingxing 俞應星 to serve as Examiners, and Department Director of Studies Qi Ke 齊柯, together with County Directors of Studies Lin Changqing 林長清, Jiang Yangcheng 蔣養成, Wang Tongren 王同任, Zhu Tingfu 朱廷輔, Yu Chunran 余純然, and Zhang Ruling 張汝翎, as Associate Examiners. Serving as Proctors were Left Administration Commissioner Zhou Jian 周鑑 and Left Administration Vice Commissioner Wu Guolun 吳國倫; serving as Surveillance Officials of the Examination were Surveillance Commissioner Zheng Yunying 鄭雲鎣 and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Xu Xueshi 徐學詩. Together with all the various functionaries, they took their places and accepted the regulations. Weici 維慈 and Weichun 維春 then gathered the more than two thousand four hundred scholars selected by Education Intendant Vice Commissioner Zhao Fen 趙奮 and tested them in three sessions, selecting the eighty most outstanding men among them and recording their essays to present as tribute to the Court. Inworthy as I, Youfu 有敷, am, by virtue of my official duties it is fitting that I set forth a prefatory statement on the opening pages. Examining antiquity, commanderies and principalities assessed the land to fix their revenues, levying their notable products in order to transport and present them to the imperial treasury, …

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
命之曰貢而諸侯造士于天
子亦曰貢蓋貢之言供也出
地之所有以供上用故咸謂
之貢往讀禹貢其述九州之
賦至詳別矣獨豫州得稱錯
上中及考班史古今人表則
伊尹傅說蘧瑗國僑甯俞之
倫又竝列于上中其他莫敢
===
望焉是數聖賢者固皆豫產
也豈非河嶽儲祥中和孕秀
故人物竝盛較然符合如此
乎夫高山景行先民是程者
哲人之逸軌也褎奇抱異秉
時飈奮者良士之芳猷也
punctuated: 命之曰「貢」，而諸侯造士于天子亦曰「貢」。蓋貢之言供也，出地之所有以供上用，故咸謂之貢。往讀《禹貢》，其述九州之賦，至詳別矣，獨豫州得稱錯上中。及考班史《古今人表》，則伊尹、傅說、蘧瑗、國僑、甯俞之倫，又竝列于上中，其他莫敢望焉。是數聖賢者，固皆豫產也。豈非河嶽儲祥，中和孕秀，故人物竝盛，較然符合如此乎？夫高山景行，先民是程者，哲人之逸軌也；褎奇抱異，秉時飈奮者，良士之芳猷也。
translation_en: …termed it “tribute” (gong 貢); and when the feudal lords presented cultivated scholars to the Son of Heaven, that too was called “tribute.” For “tribute” means “to supply” (gong 供): bringing forth what a region possesses in order to supply the sovereign’s use—hence both were called tribute. In the past, when I read the Tribute of Yu (Yu gong 禹貢), I saw that its account of the revenues of the Nine Provinces was most detailed and distinct, yet Yu Province (Yuzhou 豫州) alone was rated as upper-middle with admixtures of the first grade. And when I examined the “Table of Ancient and Modern Personalities” (Gu jin ren biao 古今人表) in Ban Gu’s History of the Former Han (Hanshu 漢書), figures the likes of Yi Yin 伊尹, Fu Yue 傅說, Qu Yuan 蘧瑗, Guo Qiao 國僑 (Zichan 子產), and Ning Yu 甯俞 were likewise all ranked in the upper-middle tier, such that others could scarcely hope to match them. Now, these several sages and worthies were all indeed natives of Yu Province! Is it not because the Yellow River and the Sacred Mount store up auspiciousness, and central harmony nurtures excellence, that both human talent and material products flourish together in such a clearly matching correspondence? Truly, to gaze upon the high mountain and walk the bright road, taking the ancients as one’s model—this is the lofty track of the wise; to cherish rare gifts and embrace extraordinary abilities, seizing the moment to rise like a whirlwind—this is the fragrant plan of the worthy scholar. …

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
主上統一聖真化隆縣寓
萬幾之暇輒
御經幄延儒碩講求治緒雅以親
賢籲俊為首務頃復盛
法駕
臨幸太學無論纁黌方領之士即
四夷陪臣質子莫不襲冠帶
===
稽首橋門以望下風英聲茂
實不崇朝而布八埏矣豫邇
畿輔為天下中文教先洽晨風
鬱北林巨魚縱大壑蓋其時
也茲所貢士得無有若伊傅
諸人者出供
上用以荅甚盛隆際哉古稱豫州
punctuated: 主上統一聖真，化隆縣寓。萬幾之暇，輒御經幄，延儒碩講求治緒，雅以親賢籲俊為首務。頃復盛法駕，臨幸太學。無論纁黌方領之士，即四夷陪臣、質子，莫不襲冠帶，稽首橋門，以望下風。英聲茂實，不崇朝而布八埏矣。豫邇畿輔，為天下中，文教先洽。晨風鬱北林，巨魚縱大壑，蓋其時也。茲所貢士，得無有若伊、傅諸人者出供上用，以荅甚盛隆際哉？古稱豫州
translation_en: The Reigning Sovereign unites the sagely and the authentic, and his transforming influence flourishes throughout the realm. In the leisure from his myriad affairs of state, he regularly attends the Classics Mat, inviting eminent Confucians to investigate the threads of governance, and consistently takes drawing near to the worthy and calling forth the outstanding as his foremost task. Recently, he again arrayed the Imperial Carriage in grandeur and graced the National University with an imperial visit. Not only the scholars of crimson-trimmed robes and square collars in the schools, but even the tributary envoys and hostage princes of the four barbarian quarters all donned caps and sashes and bowed their heads to the ground at the bridged gates to gaze upon his transformative influence from below. His illustrious renown and flourishing substance spread to the eight utmost borders before a single morning was out. Yu [Henan] lies near the Metropolitan Area and is the center of the world, so civilizing education imbues it first. When the morning falcon darts into the luxuriant northern woods and the great fish is loosed into the vast chasm—this is indeed the time! Among the scholars presented for tribute on this occasion, could there fail to be men like Yi Yin, Fu Yue, and those others mentioned above, who will come forth to serve the Sovereign's needs and answer to this most flourishing and exalted juncture? In antiquity it was said that the men and scholars of Yuzhou…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
人士常半天下要其實非侈
談也全豫幅隕千里編户之
民以百萬數而羣干釁校者
百不得一士占一藝以上以
萬數而待試有司者十不得
一操觚搦管昂首雲霄之會
以千數而推轂與計偕者又
===
二十而不得一士之與茲選
亦難矣智過千人爲豪才倍
萬人爲傑士拔于千萬人之
中而不以豪傑自命者非夫
也豪傑之士雖無聖人猶興
況
上以神聖臨之予有數固信諸士
punctuated: 人士常半天下，要其實非侈談也。全豫幅隕千里，編户之民以百萬數，而羣干釁校者百不得一；士占一藝以上以萬數，而待試有司者十不得一；操觚搦管、昂首雲霄之會以千數，而推轂與計偕者又二十而不得一。士之與茲選，亦難矣！智過千人爲豪，才倍萬人爲傑。士拔于千萬人之中，而不以豪傑自命者，非夫也。豪傑之士，雖無聖人猶興，況上以神聖臨之，予有數，固信諸士
translation_en: …men of talent regularly accounted for half of all those in the empire; considering the reality of it, this is no extravagant boast. The territory of all Henan spans a thousand li, and its registered households number in the millions, yet among them, those who gather to seek advancement in the schools are not one in a hundred; scholars who specialize in at least one Classic number in the tens of thousands, yet those who await examination by the authorities are not one in ten; those who grasp writing tablets and hold brushes, raising their heads toward the opportunity of soaring to the clouds, number in the thousands, yet those who are recommended to travel to the capital with the tribute accounts are again not one in twenty. For a scholar to be included in this selection is difficult indeed! One whose wisdom surpasses a thousand men is a hero (hao 豪); one whose talent doubles that of ten thousand men is a champion (jie 傑). When a scholar is selected from among thousands and tens of thousands of men, if he does not take it upon himself to be a hero and a champion, he is no true man. Scholars who are heroes and champions rise up even when there is no sage king; how much more so when His Majesty presides over them with divine sageliness! Having some share in this duty [?], I certainly trust that the scholars…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
之必能興也方士之未遇也
有司之欲知士急于士之求
知及其旣遇也有司之期待
士甚于士之自待顧語有之
薑桂因地而生不因地而辛
女因媒而嫁不因媒而貞有
司者固士之媒也敢遽謂士
===
之必貞哉葢言行之判久矣
古之觀人者九徵五視猶然
病其難廼今所據以知諸士
者言耳頊得徧閱諸士所爲
文信紬儒墨褒刺王伯綜古
今之變而晰道德之塗亦旣
斐然厭心矣使執此以往能
punctuated: 之必能興也。方士之未遇也，有司之欲知士，急于士之求知；及其旣遇也，有司之期待士，甚于士之自待。顧語有之：「薑桂因地而生，不因地而辛；女因媒而嫁，不因媒而貞。」有司者，固士之媒也，敢遽謂士之必貞哉？葢言行之判久矣。古之觀人者，九徵五視，猶然病其難，廼今所據以知諸士者，言耳。頊得徧閱諸士所爲文，信紬儒墨，褒刺王伯，綜古今之變，而晰道德之塗，亦旣斐然厭心矣。使執此以往，能
translation_en: … will surely be able to rise up. When a scholar has not yet met with recognition, the officials' desire to know the scholar is more urgent than the scholar's own quest to be known; and once he has met with recognition, the officials' expectations for the scholar are even greater than the scholar's expectations for himself. Yet there is a saying: "Ginger and cinnamon grow by reliance on the soil, but they are not pungent because of the soil; a woman marries through a matchmaker, but she is not chaste because of the matchmaker." The officials are indeed the matchmakers for the scholars—how could they rashly claim that the scholars will necessarily remain chaste? For words and deeds have long been separated. When the ancients observed men, even with the nine tests and five observations, they still worried about the difficulty of it; whereas today, all that we rely on to know you scholars is words alone. I, Xu [頊], have been able to read through the essays composed by all of you scholars: truly you draw out the threads of the Confucians and Mohists, praise the True Kings and censure the Hegemons, synthesize the transformations of past and present, and clearly discern the path of the Way and its Virtue—they are indeed brilliantly accomplished and satisfy the mind. If you hold fast to this as you go forward, and are able to…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
躡景伊傅賛軌豪傑期無愧
豫人士夫誰得而訾之假令
膠守舊聞無適于用竅言也
高自標許以眩俗駭聽而遠
于事情夸言也發匪由衷秉
人而效其捷券言也借六藝
市榮寵舉生平而弁髦之靜
言也有言若此雖工奚益即
===
諸士何以稱
上意剟于有司有司將安所傳其
皐邪豫有棠谿馮池良劒所
自出也設劒人竊其名以獻
而用無當于剸割則劒人必
蒙不共之罰〔有數〕之懼亦猶
punctuated: 躡景伊傅，賛軌豪傑，期無愧豫人士，夫誰得而訾之？假令膠守舊聞，無適于用，竅言也；高自標許，以眩俗駭聽，而遠于事情，夸言也；發匪由衷，秉人而效其捷，券言也；借六藝市榮寵，舉生平而弁髦之，靜言也。有言若此，雖工奚益？即諸士何以稱上意？剟于有司，有司將安所傳其皐邪？豫有棠谿、馮池，良劒所自出也。設劒人竊其名以獻，而用無當于剸割，則劒人必蒙不共之罰。〔有數〕之懼，亦猶
translation_en: …tread in the footsteps of Yi Yin and Fu Yue, and follow the path of heroes and outstanding men, aspiring to bring no shame upon the scholars and gentlemen of Henan—who then could criticize them? Suppose, however, that they stubbornly cling to old learning without adapting it to practical use: those are hollow words. Or set themselves up on high to dazzle the vulgar and startle listeners while remaining far removed from actual affairs: those are boastful words. Or utter what does not come from the heart, seizing upon others to imitate their quick success [?]: those are opportunistic [?] words. Or use the Six Arts to traffic in glory and favor, casting aside everything they have stood for all their lives like adiscarded cap: those are specious words. If their words are like these, even though they be skillfully crafted, of what benefit are they? How then could the scholars fulfill the Emperor's wishes? When the blame is laid [?] upon the authorities, how could the authorities shift their guilt elsewhere? In Henan there are Tangxi and Fengchi, whence fine swords come. Suppose a swordsmith were to steal their names in presenting a blade, yet in use it proved unfit for cutting and slicing; then the swordsmith would surely suffer the punishment for failing in his duty. What You Shu 〔有數〕 [?] fears is just…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
是矣諸士始登進譽諸吹劒
首者麾一吷耳懋之哉顧毋
以一吷而自滿也是役也巡
撫河南右僉都御史孟〔重〕風
猷夙登人士景從總理河道
右僉都御史傅〔希摯〕提督撫
治鄖陽右副都御史前王〔世〕
===
貞〔〕今徐〔學謨〕綏寧疆宇翼宣
文教監察御史印馬孫〔成名〕
巡鹽陳〔用賓〕雷〔嘉祥〕王〔曉〕振
揚法紀釐正士風布政使司
左參議凌〔琯〕孫〔光祜〕按察司
副使唐〔汝迪〕杜〔輅〕姜〔繼曾〕僉
事張〔應福〕趙〔思誠〕王〔錫命〕李
punctuated:
是矣。諸士始登進，譽諸吹劒首者，麾一吷耳。懋之哉！顧毋以一吷而自滿也。
是役也，巡撫河南右僉都御史孟〔重〕，風猷夙登，人士景從；總理河道右僉都御史傅〔希摯〕、提督撫治鄖陽右副都御史前王〔世〕貞〔〕、今徐〔學謨〕，綏寧疆宇，翼宣文教；監察御史印馬孫〔成名〕、巡鹽陳〔用賓〕、雷〔嘉祥〕、王〔曉〕，振揚法紀，釐正士風；布政使司左參議凌〔琯〕、孫〔光祜〕，按察司副使唐〔汝迪〕、杜〔輅〕、姜〔繼曾〕，僉事張〔應福〕、趙〔思誠〕、王〔錫命〕、李
translation_en:
… this. Now that the scholars are first ascending and advancing, if we compare them [譽, for 譬?] to blowing into the pommel of a sword, it is merely [麾, for 廑?] a faint wheeze. Strive hard! Do not be self-satisfied with a mere wheeze.

In this undertaking, Grand Coordinator of Henan and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Meng Zhong 孟重 had long set a high moral example and planning, so that scholars and people looked up to and followed him. Director-General of the Grand Canal and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Fu Xizhi 傅希摯, along with Superintendent and Grand Coordinator of Yunyang and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, formerly Wang Shizhen 王世貞 and currently Xu Xuemo 徐學謨, pacified the territories and assisted in spreading civilizing education. Investigating Censors: Horse-Stamping Censor Sun Chengming 孫成名, and Salt-Control Censors Chen Yongbin 陳用賓, Lei Jiaxiang 雷嘉祥, and Wang Xiao 王曉, roused and upheld the laws and discipline and rectified the literati ethos. Of the Provincial Administration Commission, Left Assistant Administration Commissioners Ling Guan 凌琯 and Sun Guanghu 孫光祜; of the Provincial Surveillance Commission, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Tang Rudi 唐汝迪, Du Lu 杜輅, and Jiang Jizeng 姜繼曾, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Zhang Yingfu 張應福, Zhao Sicheng 趙思誠, Wang Ximing 王錫命, Li…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
〔之茂〕聶〔廷璧〕都指揮使司署
都指揮僉事惠〔承恩〕朱〔家將〕
鄧〔都〕綜理庶務遠邇協恭右
參政吳〔文佳〕僉事徐〔汝翼〕署
都指揮僉事徐〔欽〕以入
賀行右參政楊〔樞〕副使田〔汝穎〕
僉事黃〔猷吉〕以督賦視邊治
===
河出其以
使事至者太常寺少卿賈〔三近〕
翰林院編脩劉〔楚先〕户科右
給事中李〔邦佐〕刑部郎中蔣
〔致大〕户部主事段〔邦寵〕中書
舍人蔡〔夢說〕行人司左司副
孫〔從龍〕行人孫〔健〕何〔汝登〕皆
punctuated: 〔之茂〕、聶〔廷璧〕，都指揮使司署都指揮僉事惠〔承恩〕、朱〔家將〕、鄧〔都〕，綜理庶務，遠邇協恭；右參政吳〔文佳〕、僉事徐〔汝翼〕、署都指揮僉事徐〔欽〕，以入賀行；右參政楊〔樞〕、副使田〔汝穎〕、僉事黃〔猷吉〕，以督賦、視邊、治河出；其以使事至者：太常寺少卿賈〔三近〕、翰林院編脩劉〔楚先〕、户科右給事中李〔邦佐〕、刑部郎中蔣〔致大〕、户部主事段〔邦寵〕、中書舍人蔡〔夢說〕、行人司左司副孫〔從龍〕、行人孫〔健〕、何〔汝登〕，皆
translation_en: … [Li] Zhimao 〔之茂〕, and Nie Tingbi 聶〔廷璧〕; and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners of the Regional Military Commission Hui Cheng'en 惠〔承恩〕, Zhu Jiajiang 朱〔家將〕, and Deng Du 鄧〔都〕, who managed the various administrative affairs and cooperated harmoniously near and far; Right Administration Vice Commissioner Wu Wenjia 吳〔文佳〕, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Xu Ruyi 徐〔汝翼〕, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Xu Qin 徐〔欽〕, who had departed to present congratulations at court; Right Administration Vice Commissioner Yang Shu 楊〔樞〕, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Tian Ruying 田〔汝穎〕, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Huang Youji 黃〔猷吉〕, who were away on duty overseeing tax collection, inspecting the frontier, and managing the Yellow River; as well as those who had arrived on imperial missions: Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Jia Sanjin 賈〔三近〕, Junior Compiler of the Hanlin Academy Liu Chuxian 劉〔楚先〕, Right Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Revenue Li Bangzuo 李〔邦佐〕, Director in the Ministry of Justice Jiang Zhida 蔣〔致大〕, Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue Duan Bangchong 段〔邦寵〕, Drafter in the Central Drafting Office Cai Mengshuo 蔡〔夢說〕, Left Deputy Director of the Messenger Office Sun Conglong 孫〔從龍〕, and Messengers Sun Jian 孫〔健〕 and He Rudeng 何〔汝登〕, all …

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
樂觀人文之盛故事得竝書
書之
山東濟南府長清縣儒學教
諭孫有叡謹序
punctuated:
樂觀人文之盛，故事得竝書，書之。

山東濟南府長清縣儒學教諭孫有叡謹序。
translation_en:
… delighted to witness the flourishing of refined culture; by precedent they may all be recorded together, and so I record them.

Respectfully prefaced by Sun Yourui 孫有叡, Instructor of the Confucian School of Changqing County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong.

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰我非生而知之者好古敏以求之者
也
君子之道四丘未能一焉所求乎子以事
父未能也所求乎臣以事君未能也所
求乎弟以事兄未能也所求乎朋友先
施之未能也庸德之行庸言之謹有所
不足不敢不勉有餘不敢盡言顧行行
顧言君子胡不慥慥爾
有布縷之征粟米之征力役之征君子用
其一緩其二
===
易
六三觀我生進退象曰觀我生進退未失
道也六四觀國之光利用賓于王象曰
觀國之光尚賓也九五觀我生君子无
咎象曰觀我生觀民也
聖人感人心而天下和平
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

「子曰：『我非生而知之者，好古，敏以求之者也。』」

「君子之道四，丘未能一焉：所求乎子，以事父，未能也；所求乎臣，以事君，未能也；所求乎弟，以事兄，未能也；所求乎朋友，先施之，未能也。庸德之行，庸言之謹；有所不足，不敢不勉，有餘不敢盡；言顧行，行顧言，君子胡不慥慥爾！」

「有布縷之征，粟米之征，力役之征。君子用其一，緩其二。」

易

「六三，觀我生，進退。象曰：『觀我生，進退』，未失道也。六四，觀國之光，利用賓于王。象曰：『觀國之光』，尚賓也。九五，觀我生，君子无咎。象曰：『觀我生』，觀民也。」

「聖人感人心而天下和平。」
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

"The Master said: 'I am not one who was born with knowledge; I am one who loves antiquity and is earnest in seeking it.'"

"There are four things in the Way of the noble man, none of which I, Qiu, have been able to achieve: to serve my father as I would require my son to serve me—that I have not yet been able to do; to serve my ruler as I would require my minister to serve me—that I have not yet been able to do; to serve my elder brother as I would require my younger brother to serve me—that I have not yet been able to do; to be the first to set an example in behaving toward friends as I would require them to behave toward me—that I have not yet been able to do. In practicing ordinary virtues and being careful in ordinary speech, where there is any deficiency, I dare not but exert myself; where there is any excess, I dare not go to the limit. When words correspond to actions and actions correspond to words, how could the noble man not be thoroughly genuine and sincere!"

"There are the exactions of cloth and silk, the exactions of grain and rice, and the exactions of corvée labor. A noble man employs one of these while deferring the other two."

Book of Changes (Yi)

"Six in the third place: Contemplating my own life, whether to advance or retreat. The Commentary on the Images says: 'Contemplating my own life, whether to advance or retreat'—one has not yet lost the Way. Six in the fourth place: Contemplating the glory of the state, it is beneficial to be a guest of the king. The Commentary on the Images says: 'Contemplating the glory of the state'—guests are esteemed. Nine in the fifth place: Contemplating my own life; for the noble man there is no blame. The Commentary on the Images says: 'Contemplating my own life' means contemplating the condition of the people."

"The sage moves the hearts of men, and all under Heaven comes to peace and harmony."

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
日新之謂盛德
君子知微知彰知柔知剛萬夫之望
書
欽哉愼乃有位敬脩其可願
王懋乃德視乃烈祖無時豫怠奉先思孝
接下思恭視遠惟明聽德惟聰
曰若稽古人之德矧曰其有能稽謀自
天
惟敬五刑以成三德
===
詩
蒹葭蒼蒼白露爲霜所謂伊人在水一方
遡洄從之道阻且長遡游從之宛在水
中央
有渰萋萋興雨祁祁雨我公田遂及我私
文王嘉止大邦有子
聖敬日躋昭假遲遲上帝是祗
春秋
叔孫州仇帥師墮郈　季孫斯仲孫何忌
punctuated:
日新之謂盛德。
君子知微知彰，知柔知剛，萬夫之望。

書：
欽哉，愼乃有位，敬脩其可願。
王懋乃德，視乃烈祖，無時豫怠。奉先思孝，接下思恭，視遠惟明，聽德惟聰。
曰若稽古，人之德，矧曰其有能稽謀自天。
惟敬五刑，以成三德。

詩：
蒹葭蒼蒼，白露爲霜。所謂伊人，在水一方。遡洄從之，道阻且長；遡游從之，宛在水中央。
有渰萋萋，興雨祁祁。雨我公田，遂及我私。
文王嘉止，大邦有子。
聖敬日躋，昭假遲遲，上帝是祗。

春秋：
叔孫州仇帥師墮郈；季孫斯、仲孫何忌
translation_en:
“Daily renewal is called abundant virtue.”
“The superior man knows the minute and knows the manifest, knows the soft and knows the hard: he is the one to whom ten thousand men look up.”

Book of Documents (Shu):
“Be reverent! Be cautious in the office you hold, and respectfully cultivate what is desirable.”
“May the king exert himself in his virtue and look to his meritorious ancestors, never at any time indulging in ease or idleness. In serving his predecessors, let him think of filial piety; in receiving his subordinates, let him think of courtesy; in looking afar, let him seek only clear vision; in listening to virtue, let him seek only acute hearing.”
“Examining into antiquity, even regarding the virtue of men, how much more so when it is said that one is able to examine and take counsel from Heaven!”
“Reverently attend to the five punishments, so as to complete the three virtues.”

Book of Odes (Shi):
“The reeds and rushes are deeply green, and the white dew is turned to frost. The person of whom I speak is on the other side of the water. I go up against the stream to follow him, but the way is difficult and long; I go down with the stream to follow him, and lo, he is right in the midst of the water.”
“The clouds gather densely, and the rain comes down gently. May it rain first on our public fields, and then reach our private ones.”
“King Wen approved of this, and in the great state there was the lady.”
“His sagely reverence advanced daily; his bright influence reached far and long, and he revered the Lord on High.”

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu):
“Shusun Zhouqiu led a force and dismantled Hou; Jisun Si and Zhongsun Heji…”

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
帥師墮費〔定公十有二年〕春齊國書帥
師伐我〔哀公十有一年〕
晉侯伐秦〔文公四年〕
楚屈完來盟于師盟于召陵〔僖公四年〕夏
四月己巳晉侯齊師宋師秦師及楚人
戰于城濮楚師敗績〔僖公二十有八年〕
晉欒書帥師救鄭〔成公六年〕夏五月甲
午遂滅偪陽〔襄公十年〕
公會晉侯齊侯宋公衛侯曹伯莒子邾子
杞伯救鄭〔成公七年〕
===
禮記
以百官之成質於天子百官齊戒受質
動則左史書之言則右史書之
致樂以治心則易直子諒之心油然生矣
易直子諒之心生則樂樂則安安則久
久則天天則神天則不言而信神則不
怒而威致樂以治心者也
悝拜稽首曰對揚以辟之勤大命施于烝
punctuated:
帥師墮費〔定公十有二年〕；春，齊國書帥師伐我〔哀公十有一年〕。
晉侯伐秦〔文公四年〕。
楚屈完來盟于師，盟于召陵〔僖公四年〕；夏四月己巳，晉侯、齊師、宋師、秦師及楚人戰于城濮，楚師敗績〔僖公二十有八年〕。
晉欒書帥師救鄭〔成公六年〕；夏五月甲午，遂滅偪陽〔襄公十年〕。
公會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、杞伯救鄭〔成公七年〕。

禮記
以百官之成質於天子，百官齊戒受質。
動則左史書之，言則右史書之。
致樂以治心，則易直子諒之心油然生矣。易直子諒之心生則樂，樂則安，安則久，久則天，天則神。天則不言而信，神則不怒而威，致樂以治心者也。
悝拜稽首曰：「對揚以辟之勤大命，施于烝
translation_en:
…led a force and dismantled the walls of Bi [Twelfth year of Duke Ding]; in spring, Guo Shu of Qi led a force and attacked us [Eleventh year of Duke Ai].
"The Marquis of Jin attacked Qin" [Fourth year of Duke Wen].
"Qu Wan of Chu came to make a covenant with the army, and made a covenant at Shaoling" [Fourth year of Duke Xi]; "In summer, in the fourth month, on the jisi day, the Marquis of Jin, the army of Qi, the army of Song, and the army of Qin fought with the men of Chu at Chengpu, and the army of Chu was utterly defeated" [Twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi].
"Luan Shu of Jin led a force to rescue Zheng" [Sixth year of Duke Cheng]; "In summer, in the fifth month, on the jiawu day, they thereupon extinguished Biyang" [Tenth year of Duke Xiang].
"The Duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, and the Earl of Qi to rescue Zheng" [Seventh year of Duke Cheng].

Record of Rites (Liji)
"With the completed accounts of the hundred officials, he presents them for verification to the Son of Heaven; the hundred officials fast and purify themselves to receive the verification."
"When he acted, the Scribe of the Left recorded it; when he spoke, the Scribe of the Right recorded it."
"When one thoroughly comprehends music to regulate the mind, then a mild, upright, affectionate, and sincere mind naturally arises. When a mild, upright, affectionate, and sincere mind arises, there is joy; with joy comes peace; with peace comes long continuance; with long continuance comes a heaven-like state; with a heaven-like state comes a spirit-like state. Being heaven-like, one is trusted without speaking; being spirit-like, one is awe-inspiring without anger. Such is the result of thoroughly comprehending music to regulate the mind."
"Kui bowed and knocked his head on the ground, saying: 'In response, I extol with [for 王, the King's?] diligent great mandate, inscribing it upon the sacrificial…'"…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
問虞夏之書渾渾商書灝灝周書噩噩夫
是三者何居或曰兢兢業業一日萬幾
四代之所以隆也豈以其敬戒相授守
言則為命書則為訓耶蓋嘗稽之虞作
布政之宮曰總章夏作簨簴之銘曰五
音聽治商作器用之銘曰自警三風十
愆曰警于有位周作十銘曰予一人所
聞以戒後世子孫茲其所為敬戒者蓋
萬世帝王之龜鑑也故曰聖人之言炳
若丹青匪文之也秦漢以來此道微矣
越數千年四代帝王之運再造我
===
國家
神聖繼作
典則具存而
存心省躬二錄與
敬一之箴五箴之註允我
祖宗傳心至語與典謨訓誥同文茲我
皇上
punctuated: 問：虞夏之書渾渾，商書灝灝，周書噩噩，夫是三者，何居？或曰：「兢兢業業，一日萬幾。」四代之所以隆也，豈以其敬戒相授守，言則為命，書則為訓耶？蓋嘗稽之，虞作布政之宮曰《總章》，夏作簨簴之銘曰《五音聽治》，商作器用之銘曰《自警》、《三風十愆》曰《警于有位》，周作十銘曰「予一人所聞，以戒後世子孫」。茲其所為敬戒者，蓋萬世帝王之龜鑑也。故曰：聖人之言，炳若丹青，匪文之也。秦漢以來，此道微矣。越數千年，四代帝王之運，再造我國家，神聖繼作，典則具存，而《存心》、《省躬》二錄，與《敬一》之箴、《五箴》之註，允我祖宗傳心至語，與典、謨、訓、誥同文。茲我皇上
translation_en: Question: The documents of Yu [Shun] and Xia are deep and simple, the documents of Shang are vast and boundless, and the documents of Zhou are solemn and rigorous—what is the reason for these three qualities? Someone said: "Cautious andreverent, attending to ten thousand affairs in a single day." Is not the reason why the Four Dynasties flourished that they transmitted and upheld reverence and caution to one another, so that when spoken their words became charges, and when written they became instructions? When we examine this, Yu built the palace for promulgating governance called the Zongzhang (Hall of General Regulation); Xia composed the inscription on the bell and drum stands concerning listening to governance through the five tones; Shang composed the inscriptions on daily vessels for self-admonition, and the "Three Vices and Ten Errors" to warn those in office; and Zhou composed the ten inscriptions, saying, "What I, the One Man, have heard, to admonish future generations of descendants." That by which they practiced reverence and caution serves indeed as a mirror for emperors and kings of ten thousand generations. Therefore it is said: The words of the sages shine as brightly as vermilion and blue, not merely because of their literary ornament. Since the Qin and Han dynasties, this Way has grown faint. After several thousand years, the destiny of the emperors and kings of the Four Dynasties has been recreated in our State. Divine sages have arisen in succession, and the canons and standards are fully preserved. Moreover, the two records Cunxin lu (Record of Preserving the Mind) and Xinggong lu (Record of Self-Examination), together with the Jingyi zhen (Admonition on Reverent Unity) and the commentaries on the Wuzhen (Five Admonitions), are truly the supreme words transmitting the mind of our Imperial Ancestors, sharing the same literary spirit as the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, and Announcements. Now Our August Sovereign…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
沖睿作聖
德邁周成
臨御以來
嘉言善政未易更僕舉大者
諭正人心數百言敷自皇極頊又於
講勸之暇
親書敬戒十二句
頒之政府以
詔四方夫言心聲也言心畫也諸士陳說古
===
今能矣有能奉
訓命而知
聖天子敬戒之心者乎其詳著于篇以鳴我
國家之盛
問郊祀大禮自古帝王隆之而其制至于
周大備今考周禮所載冬夏殊時圜方
異位與諸器數儀文莫不有精意存可
指而陳之與後世事不師古若咸陽四
時渭陽五帝與夫武德乾封太清景靈
punctuated:
沖睿作聖，德邁周成。臨御以來，嘉言善政，未易更僕，舉大者：諭正人心數百言，敷自皇極；頊又於講勸之暇，親書敬戒十二句，頒之政府，以詔四方。夫言，心聲也；言，心畫也。諸士陳說古今能矣，有能奉訓命而知聖天子敬戒之心者乎？其詳著于篇，以鳴我國家之盛。

問：郊祀大禮，自古帝王隆之，而其制至于周大備。今考《周禮》所載，冬夏殊時，圜方異位，與諸器數儀文，莫不有精意存，可指而陳之與？後世事不師古，若咸陽四時、渭陽五帝，與夫武德、乾封、太清、景靈，
translation_en:
…in his youthful wisdom becomes a sage, and his virtue surpasses that of King Cheng of Zhou. Since ascending the throne, his admirable words and benevolent governance cannot easily be counted even by changing attendants. To cite the greatest examples: his edict on rectifying people's minds, running to several hundred words, was promulgated from the Hall of Imperial Supremacy (Huangji dian); and recently [? 頊, for 頃], in his leisure from Classical Colloquia and expositions, he personally wrote out twelve lines on reverence and caution, bestowing them upon the Grand Secretariat to proclaim them to the four quarters. Now speech is the voice of the mind, and writing [? 言, for 書] is the picture of the mind. You gentlemen are already capable of setting forth accounts of antiquity and the present; is there anyone among you able to receive with reverence these instructive commands and understand the reverent and cautious mind of our sagely Son of Heaven? Write this out in detail in your essay, so as to proclaim the flourishing prosperity of our dynasty.

Question: The grand ritual of the suburban sacrifices has been held in high esteem by emperors and kings since antiquity, and its system reached full completeness in the Zhou dynasty. If we now examine what is recorded in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli)—the different seasons of winter and summer, the distinct sites of the Round Mound and Square Altar, along with the various ritual vessels, numbers, and ceremonial forms—there is none in which a subtle meaning does not reside; can you point these out and set them forth? In later ages, rulers did not model their affairs on antiquity: cases such as the Four Altars (sishi [? 四時, for 四畤]) near Xianyang and the Temple of the Five Emperors at Weiyang, as well as the practices of the Wude (618–626) and Qianfeng (666–668) eras and the Taiqing and Jingling palaces,…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
其說不經勿談矣卽其閒一二英主慕
古而興然分祭合祭竝配特配議論紛
特典制屢易其孰爲當與我
高皇帝稽古定制亦先分而後合卒以
祖宗竝配歲惟一舉至
肅皇帝復定分祭之禮建
大享殿而特配
聖祖歲凡四舉其分合繁簡之由可得聞其槩
與我
===
皇上嗣服之初肇舉
郊祀輔臣因進祀禮圖考具載
祖宗分祭合祭之規竝配特配之制與諸器數
儀文至詳且悉矣然謂合祀爲便竝配
爲順一舉爲宜俱昉
高皇帝定制行之而於
世廟之禮不嫌異同卽祠禮亦有不必盡泥者
何與玆俎豆之事也諸士其折衷以告
我毋諉曰其義難知
punctuated: 其說不經，勿談矣。卽其閒一二英主慕古而興，然分祭、合祭、竝配、特配，議論紛特，典制屢易，其孰爲當與？我高皇帝稽古定制，亦先分而後合，卒以祖宗竝配，歲惟一舉。至肅皇帝，復定分祭之禮，建大享殿，而特配聖祖，歲凡四舉。其分合繁簡之由，可得聞其槩與？我皇上嗣服之初，肇舉郊祀，輔臣因進《祀禮圖考》，具載祖宗分祭、合祭之規，竝配、特配之制，與諸器數儀文，至詳且悉矣。然謂合祀爲便、竝配爲順、一舉爲宜，俱昉高皇帝定制行之；而於世廟之禮不嫌異同，卽《周禮》〔祠禮〕亦有不必盡泥者，何與？玆俎豆之事也，諸士其折衷以告我，毋諉曰「其義難知」。
translation_en: …—their doctrines are uncanonical and need not be discussed. Yet even when one or two enlightened rulers during those periods admired antiquity and sought to revive it, debates over separate sacrifices versus combined sacrifices, and joint pairing versus sole pairing [of imperial ancestors with Heaven], were tumultuous [? 紛特, likely a misprint for 紛紜], and the institutional regulations were repeatedly changed; which of them was right? When our Exalted Emperor (Gao Huangdi, i.e., the Hongwu Emperor) examined antiquity to establish the regulations, he too first separated and later combined them, ultimately pairing both ancestors (Taizu and Taizong) jointly and performing the sacrifice only once a year. Coming to the莊肅 Reverent Emperor (Su Huangdi, i.e., the Jiajing Emperor), he again established the rite of separate sacrifices, built the Hall of Great Sacrifice (Daxiang dian), and solely paired the Sacred Ancestor (Shengzu), performing the sacrifices four times a year in all. May we hear a general outline of the reasons for their separation or combination, complexity or simplicity? When Our Majesty first succeeded to the throne and inaugurated the suburban sacrifices, the Grand Secretaries thereupon presented the Illustrated Study of Sacrificial Rites (Sili tukao), which fully recorded the ancestral rules for separate and combined sacrifices, the institutions of joint and sole pairing, and all the ritual vessels, numbers, and ceremonies in utmost detail and completeness. Yet it argued that combined sacrifice is more convenient, joint pairing is more harmonious, and performing it once a year is more fitting—all following the established regulations of the Exalted Emperor—while not shying away from diverging from the rites of the Shizong temple (the Jiajing Emperor), and holding that even the Rites of Zhou [? 祠禮, likely a woodblock error for 周禮] need not be adhered to in every detail; why is this? This is a matter of sacrificial vessels and ritual. Gentlemen, weigh the alternatives and inform me; do not excuse yourselves by saying, "Its meaning is difficult to know."

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
問謚法創自周公書法斷自孔子尚矣乃
若所謂大行受大名細行受細名使孝
子慈孫莫能改宜後有榮於華衮貶有嚴
於鈇鉞使亂臣賊子莫不懼其旨可得
繹與且周公謚法與汲冢周書互異孔
子春秋三傳各一其説又安執以爲是
與後之爲謚者十有五家爲書者二十
一史無論仰窺二聖卽不謬於是非大
較得無有足采與夫徵往鑒來此兩端
者萬世不可廢也士宜以爲不急乎頃
朝廷厭請謚之濫亟戒禮官勿輕予
詔復起居注曰
令史官載筆從左右記事記言則謚法書法
之復明茲千載一時也如欲脩周孔之
舊以光賛
聖化士豈無更端可進乎願有聞矣
問自封建既廢語親民者不曰守令哉西
京循良爲盛班孟堅氏別爲傳以紀之
punctuated:
問：謚法創自周公，書法斷自孔子，尚矣。乃若所謂「大行受大名，細行受細名，使孝子慈孫莫能改」；宜後有榮於華衮，貶有嚴於鈇鉞，使亂臣賊子莫不懼，其旨可得繹與？且周公《謚法》與《汲冢周書》互異，孔子《春秋》三傳各一其説，又安執以爲是與？後之爲謚者十有五家，爲書者二十一史，無論仰窺二聖，卽不謬於是非大較，得無有足采與？夫徵往鑒來，此兩端者，萬世不可廢也，士宜以爲不急乎？頃朝廷厭請謚之濫，亟戒禮官勿輕予；詔復《起居注》，曰令史官載筆從左右記事記言，則謚法、書法之復明，茲千載一時也。如欲脩周、孔之舊，以光賛聖化，士豈無更端可進乎？願有聞矣。

問：自封建既廢，語親民者不曰守令哉？西京循良爲盛，班孟堅氏別爲傳以紀之。
translation_en:
Question: The rules for posthumous titles (shifa 謚法) were initiated by the Duke of Zhou (Zhougong 周公), and the principles of historiographical recording (shufa 書法) were determined by Confucius (Kongzi 孔子)—this is of long standing. Yet as for the sayings that "great conduct receives a great name, and petty conduct receives a petty name, so that filial sons and devoted grandsons cannot alter it," and that praise [宜後, for 褒?] is more glorious than ceremonial robes while censure is more severe than the executioner's axe, so that rebellious ministers and villainous sons are all struck with fear—can the purport of these be elucidated? Moreover, the Rules for Posthumous Titles (Shifa 謚法) of the Duke of Zhou and the Book of Zhou from the Ji Tomb (Jizhong Zhoushu 汲冢周書) differ from one another, and for Confucius's Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu 春秋) the Three Commentaries (Sanzhuan 三傳) each hold to their own explanations; which, then, should one hold to as correct? In later times, those who compiled works on posthumous titles numbered fifteen schools, and those who wrote histories produced the Twenty-One Histories (Ershiyi shi 二十一史). Setting aside whether they could look up and fathom the two sages, even in terms of not erring regarding the general outline of right and wrong, might there not be something among them worthy of adoption? Now, verifying the past and providing a mirror for the future—these two matters cannot be dispensed with for ten thousand generations; ought scholars to regard them as unurgent? Recently the Court, weary of the濫 (excessive) requests for posthumous titles, urgently admonished the officials of the Ministry of Rites not to grant them lightly; and it issued an edict restoring the Diaries of Activity and Repose (Qijuzhu 起居注), daily [曰, for 日?] ordering the historiographers (shiguan 史官) to carry their brushes in attendance on the Emperor's left and right to record actions and words. Thus the renewed clarification of the rules for posthumous titles and the principles of historiographical recording makes this an opportunity that comes once in a thousand years. If we wish to restore the old traditions of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius so as to gloriously assist the sacred transformation, how could you scholars have no further points to present? I wish to hear them.

Question: Since the feudal system (fengjian 封建) was abolished, when speaking of those officials who are close to the people, does one not say prefects and magistrates (shouling 守令)? In the Western Capital [Western Han], upright and benevolent officials (xunliang 循良) flourished, and Ban Mengjian [Ban Gu 班固] established a separate collective biography to record them. …

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
夷考其樹功名以自表見多在中州若
守南陽而勸課農桑守潁川而力行教
化尤傑然者乃治平爲天下第一考史
何以失其名而民不敢欺與教吏銛箒
者何乃略弗載與
國初吏稱其職民樂其業二百年來
神聖繼體日以計安元元爲務非有道德溺職
武健愉快之異也而吏治顧日以窳惰
何與異時吏苦屢遷一切爲烜耀目前
===
苟簡歲月之計士議者謂不久任不足
以改絃成理令郡縣之任往往有五六
年不得調者而民生猶未阜教化猶未
宣亦無以大異於舊何與說者謂明賞
罰覈功實申按部破恒格亦有可爲久
任之助者與陸贄氏有言漢武好英風
故其時富瓌偉立名之士漢宣精吏治
故其時萃循良覈實之能豈吏亦在乎
倡之者與頃
punctuated:
夷考其樹功名以自表見，多在中州。若守南陽而勸課農桑，守潁川而力行教化，尤傑然者。乃治平爲天下第一，考史何以失其名？而民不敢欺與教吏銛箒者，何乃略弗載與？
國初吏稱其職，民樂其業。二百年來，神聖繼體，日以計安元元爲務，非有道德溺職、武健愉快之異也，而吏治顧日以窳惰，何與？異時吏苦屢遷，一切爲烜耀目前、苟簡歲月之計。士議者謂不久任不足以改絃成理。令郡縣之任，往往有五六年不得調者，而民生猶未阜，教化猶未宣，亦無以大異於舊，何與？說者謂明賞罰、覈功實、申按部、破恒格，亦有可爲久任之助者與？陸贄氏有言：「漢武好英風，故其時富瓌偉立名之士；漢宣精吏治，故其時萃循良覈實之能。」豈吏亦在乎倡之者與？頃…
translation_en:
…When we examine how they established merit and reputation to distinguish themselves, it was mostly in the Central Plain (Zhongzhou). Those who governed Nanyang and encouraged agriculture and sericulture, or governed Yingchuan and vigorously promoted moral transformation, were especially outstanding. Yet for the one whose peaceful governance was ranked first in the empire, why does the history fail to record his personal name? And as for the one whom the people did not dare to deceive, and the one who taught his sub-officials using sharpened bamboo [as a metaphor for uncovering hidden villains] [? 銛箒], why are they omitted and not included [in that collective biography]?

At the founding of our dynasty, officials matched their duties and the people rejoiced in their livelihoods. For two hundred years, sacred and sage emperors have succeeded to the throne, daily making it their task to devise ways to bring peace to the common people. There has been no divergence like that between officials who neglected their duties out of [misguided] "virtue" and those who delighted in harsh, martial vigor; yet bureaucratic governance has instead grown daily more negligent and sluggish—why is this? In earlier times, officials suffered from frequent transfers, so in all matters they resorted to flashy measures for immediate effect and perfunctory plans simply to pass the months and years. Gentlemen who discussed the matter said that without long tenure in office, it would be impossible to restring the instrument and achieve good order. Now, in commanderies and counties, those holding office often go five or six years without being transferred, yet the people's livelihood is still not abundant, moral transformation is still not diffused, and things are no different from before—why is this? Commentators say that clarifying rewards and punishments, verifying actual achievements, reiterating touring inspections by regional supervisors, and breaking with routine promotion precedents—could these also serve as aids to long tenure? Lu Zhi (陸贄) once said: "Emperor Wu of Han loved heroic spirit, so his era was rich in extraordinary men who established their names; Emperor Xuan of Han was meticulous about bureaucratic governance, so his era gathered upright and capable officials who verified realities." Could it be that the quality of officials also depends upon the one who leads them? Recently, …

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
聖天子舉增秩賜金故事且發
德音襃勵卓越之績視前世璽書不啻重之茲
主德宣民風厚化行俗美日以烝烝是何所施
欲使政平訟理
設與願籌之以爲計吏者助且以覲所
負焉
問士含奥渫而際風雲則辨志不可後矣
儒者論士之品三曰志道德志功名志
富貴然則三者不相爲謀與或謂今之
===
道德卽古之功名今之功名卽古之富
貴信爾安在其爲道德與士以周貴以
秦賤固也漢興若酇侯絳侯輩其人皆
貪冒富貴頑鈍無恥而其功名亦赫然
稱盛何與東京始建則富春𤰈釣太原
辭祿嗣是若入會稽浮遼海耽泉石而
逃軒冕者不可勝數作史者别爲立傳
以紀之其視功名富貴不啻敝屣亦可
謂志道德否與夫道德士所有也至於
punctuated:
聖天子舉增秩賜金故事，且發德音，襃勵卓越之績，視前世璽書不啻重之。茲主德宣，民風厚，化行俗美，日以烝烝，欲使政平訟理，是何所施設與？願籌之，以爲計吏者助，且以覘所負焉。

問：士含奥渫而際風雲，則辨志不可後矣。儒者論士之品三：曰志道德，志功名，志富貴。然則三者不相爲謀與？或謂今之道德卽古之功名，今之功名卽古之富貴。信爾，安在其爲道德與？士以周貴，以秦賤，固也。漢興，若酇侯、絳侯輩，其人皆貪冒富貴，頑鈍無恥，而其功名亦赫然稱盛，何與？東京始建，則富春𤰈釣，太原辭祿。嗣是，若入會稽，浮遼海，耽泉石而逃軒冕者，不可勝數，作史者别爲立傳以紀之。其視功名富貴不啻敝屣，亦可謂志道德否與？夫道德，士所有也；至於
translation_en:
… the Sacred Son of Heaven has revived the precedent of advancing ranks and bestowing gold, and furthermore has issued gracious proclamations praising and encouraging preeminent achievements, attaching far greater weight to them than the imperial letters under the dynastic seal of former ages. Now, the ruler's virtue is proclaimed, the people's customs are generous, moral transformation prevails and mores are refined, advancing day by day; [note: column order in transcription appears transposed here] if we wish to render administration equitable and litigation well-ordered, what measures should be instituted? I wish you to deliberate upon this to assist those who evaluate officials, and also so that we may observe what capabilities you possess.

Question: When a scholar emerges from obscurity and humble circumstances to encounter the winds and clouds of opportunity, discerning his aspirations cannot be put last. Confucian scholars classify scholars into three grades: those who set their minds on the Way and virtue (daode), those who set their minds on merit and fame (gongming), and those who set their minds on wealth and honor (fugui). Does this mean, then, that these three have nothing to do with one another? Some say that the Way and virtue of today are merely the merit and fame of antiquity, and the merit and fame of today are merely the wealth and honor of antiquity. If this is truly so, wherein lies the Way and virtue? That scholars were esteemed under the Zhou and despised under the Qin is certainly true. Yet when the Han arose, men like the Marquis of Zan [Xiao He 蕭何] and the Marquis of Jiang [Zhou Bo 周勃] were all greedy and covetous of wealth and honor, obtuse and shameless [as Jiyi 賈誼 remarked], and yet their merit and fame were illustriously celebrated as flourishing—why was this? When the Eastern Capital [Later Han] was first established, there were those who plowed and fished at Fuchun [Yan Guang 嚴光] and declined emoluments in Taiyuan [Min Gong 閔貢 / Zhou Dang 周黨]. Thereafter, those who entered Kuaiji, floated upon the seas of Liao, or indulged in springs and rocks while fleeing carriages and ceremonial caps [official office] were too numerous to count, so that historians established separate biographical chapters to record them. They regarded merit, fame, wealth, and honor as no more than worn-out sandals—can they also be called men who set their minds on the Way and virtue, or not? Now, the Way and virtue are what a scholar possesses within himself; as for …

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
功名則竹帛於常世之所謂偉男子者
多歸焉而富貴則上之所懸以詔德詔
功者亦可併廢與諸子尚志非始今日
而藉以行志則自今日始也願聞其撰
毋遜毋隱
punctuated: 功名，則竹帛於常，世之所謂偉男子者多歸焉；而富貴則上之所懸以詔德詔功者，亦可併廢與？諸子尚志，非始今日，而藉以行志，則自今日始也。願聞其撰，毋遜毋隱。
translation_en: …achievement and fame, these are inscribed on bamboo and silk and upon the royal banner of merit, and those whom the world calls great men mostly gravitate toward them; and as for wealth and honor, which the ruler holds up to reward virtue and reward merit—can these both be cast aside as well? For you gentlemen, exalting your aspirations did not begin today, yet the opportunity by which you may carry out your aspirations does begin today. I wish to hear what you compose; do not hold back through modesty, and do not conceal your thoughts.

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰我非生而知之者好古敏以求之者
也
曾曰唯
同考試官教諭朱　批〔知由於學夫子豈不自聖之心也作者不寤則誕子獨發揮精切殆好古有得者與〕
同考試官教諭林　批〔得夫子自道意且知好敏子非其遜詞蓋有深識矣取之〕
===
考試官教諭俞　批〔文義渾厚志在復古者〕
考試官教諭孫　批〔見理獨到可式〕
聖人望人以學因表巳之所由知焉夫聖人亦
生知者也猶不敢以自居而謂得之好學焉學
其可以巳乎夫子之意若曰夫人之於道苟不
欲知也然不求其所以知而徒委諸質此知道
之所由鮮乎自我言之天下有生而知之者上
也我非其人也不知而作我無是也然而非生
知也忠信之資與十室同稟焉而擬諸生而神
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

「子曰：『我非生而知之者，好古，敏以求之者也。』」

「曾曰：『唯。』」

同考試官教諭朱批：〔知由於學，夫子豈不自聖之心也？作者不寤則誕，子獨發揮精切，殆好古有得者與！〕
同考試官教諭林批：〔得夫子自道意，且知好敏，子非其遜詞，蓋有深識矣，取之。〕
考試官教諭俞批：〔文義渾厚，志在復古者。〕
考試官教諭孫批：〔見理獨到，可式。〕

聖人望人以學，因表巳之所由知焉。夫聖人亦生知者也，猶不敢以自居，而謂得之好學焉，學其可以巳乎？夫子之意若曰：夫人之於道，苟不欲知也，然不求其所以知，而徒委諸質，此知道之所由鮮乎？自我言之，天下有生而知之者，上也，我非其人也。不知而作，我無是也，然而非生知也。忠信之資，與十室同稟焉，而擬諸生而神
translation_en:
First Session

The Four Books

"The Master said: 'I am not one who was born in possession of knowledge; I am one who is fond of antiquity and earnest in seeking it there.'"

"Zeng [zi] said: 'Yes.'"

Associate Examiner Instructor Zhu comments: [Knowledge comes from learning; how could this merely be the Master's mind of not regarding himself as a sage? Writers who do not grasp this fall into absurdity, yet you alone have elaborated it with precision and incisiveness—surely you are one who is fond of antiquity and has gained something from it!]
Associate Examiner Instructor Lin comments: [He captures the meaning of the Master's own statement, and understands fondness for antiquity and earnestness in seeking—recognizing that the Master's words are not mere expressions of modesty [?]. He indeed possesses deep insight; select this.]
Examiner Instructor Yu comments: [The literary style and meaning are rich and substantial; he is one whose aspiration lies in restoring antiquity.]
Examiner Instructor Sun comments: [His perception of principle is uniquely penetrating; it can serve as a model.]

The sage hopes that people will engage in learning, and therefore sets forth the means by which he himself attained knowledge. Now, the sage was in fact one born with knowledge; yet even he did not dare to claim this for himself, attributing his attainment instead to his fondness for learning—how then could learning ever cease? The Master's meaning is as if to say: In people's relation to the Way, even if it is not that they do not wish to know it [?], yet when they do not seek the means by which to know it and merely leave it to their innate endowment, is this not why those who know the Way are so few? Speaking of myself: in the world there are those who are born with knowledge—they are the highest; I am not such a person. To act or create without knowing—I am free from that; yet I am not one born with knowledge. The natural endowment of loyalty and trustworthiness I share in common with any hamlet of ten households; to compare myself to one born divinely…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
靈則無思無不通也夫何敢以自誣仁聖之理
與羣弟子共明焉而謂之天縱將聖則不慮無
不獲也又安待而自信亦惟以道無古今而覺
有先後前言往行皆可以爲吾博聞多識之地
者也於是心契乎千載之秘即從其心之所嘉
樂者而誦其詩讀其書亹亹乎學之不厭焉夫
固持循而後入未始由天啓也神而明之則吾
豈敢哉志切乎三代之英即從其志之所愛慕
者而學其大學其小孶孶乎求之不已焉夫固
積累而後通未始由性生也默而識之何有於
我哉是蓋好之深則學之自無不至求之敏則
知之自無不眞我之有知知以學而已矣而入
之不學者乃以我爲生知不亦過乎噫此聖學
之所以爲大也聖不自知故其中益虛而學益
不息忘食忘寢非自疲也問禮問官非示遜也
祖述憲章非舊博也而空空如也乃其所以爲
一貫之實際也然則非聖人而不學者其斯道
之棄乎
punctuated: 靈，則無思無不通也，夫何敢以自誣？仁聖之理，與羣弟子共明焉；而謂之天縱將聖，則不慮無不獲也，又安待而自信？亦惟以道無古今，而覺有先後，前言往行，皆可以爲吾博聞多識之地者也。於是心契乎千載之秘，即從其心之所嘉樂者，而誦其詩、讀其書，亹亹乎學之不厭焉。夫固持循而後入，未始由天啓也；神而明之，則吾豈敢哉？志切乎三代之英，即從其志之所愛慕者，而學其大、學其小，孶孶乎求之不已焉。夫固積累而後通，未始由性生也；默而識之，何有於我哉？是蓋好之深則學之自無不至，求之敏則知之自無不眞。我之有知，知以學而已矣！而入之不學者，乃以我爲生知，不亦過乎？噫！此聖學之所以爲大也。聖不自知，故其中益虛而學益不息。忘食忘寢，非自疲也；問禮問官，非示遜也；祖述憲章，非舊博也。而空空如也，乃其所以爲一貫之實際也。然則非聖人而不學者，其斯道之棄乎！
translation_en: …[divinely] intelligent, then without even thinking one comprehends everything—how could I dare to deceive myself with such a claim? I share in illuminating the principles of benevolence and sagehood together with my disciples; if one were to call me a great sage endowed by Heaven, who grasps everything without deliberation, on what basis could I have such confidence in myself? It is simply that the Way knows no past or present, whereas awakening to it comes earlier or later; the words of the ancients and the deeds of the past can all serve as the ground for broadening my learning and expanding my knowledge. Thus, my mind communes with the mysteries of a thousand years, and following what delights my heart, I recite their Odes and read their Documents, tirelessly learning without ever growing weary. Indeed, one enters into it only through steadfast adherence; it never came from Heaven's revelation. As for divinely illuminating it, how would I dare claim that? My aspirations are earnestly set upon the finest minds of the Three Dynasties, and following what my will admires, I study both their great and lesser teachings, diligently seeking without cease. Indeed, one achieves comprehension only through gradual accumulation; it never arose innately from nature. As for silently retaining it in mind, what is that to me? For when one's fondness is deep, one's learning naturally leaves nothing unreached; when one's seeking is earnest, one's knowledge is naturally nothing less than genuine. That I possess knowledge is simply knowledge gained through learning! For people who do not learn [reading 入 as 人?] to regard me as one born with knowledge—is that not an error? Alas! This is why the learning of the sage is so great. Because the sage does not regard himself as born with knowledge, his mind grows ever more receptive and his learning ever more unceasing. Forgetting to eat and forgetting to sleep was not mere self-exhaustion; asking about rites and asking about official titles was not a mere display of humility; transmitting the ancient heritage and modeling upon the regulations of the kings was not a mere show of erudition [? 舊博, likely for 務博 or 誇博]. Rather, approaching it with an utterly empty mind was the true substance of his single thread binding all together. If so, then those who are not sages and yet do not learn—are they not abandoning this Way?

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
君子之道四丘未能一焉所求乎子以事
父未能也所求乎臣以事君未能也所
求乎弟以事兄未能也所求乎朋友先
施之未能也庸德之行庸言之謹有所
不足不敢不勉有餘不敢盡言顧行行
顧言君子胡不慥慥爾
貫待價
同考試官教諭蔣　批〔講自責自脩宛然夫子語〕
氣且不泥陳說尤有卓見宜錄以式
===
考試官教諭俞　批〔格調高古結意更精實〕
考試官教諭孫　批〔渾融峻潔可佳〕
聖人以常道自責而因詳其慎脩之實焉蓋君
子之道常道也責諸己而慎脩之是亦君子而
已矣何以遠人爲哉中庸引言之意如此謂夫
道本不遠於人學貴反求諸己雖聖如孔子亦
有不能外者焉彼其言曰君子依乎中庸者也
而其道則有四丘也願學君子者也而其一尚
未能四者非他也君臣父子兄弟朋友天下之
punctuated:
「君子之道四，丘未能一焉：所求乎子，以事父，未能也；所求乎臣，以事君，未能也；所求乎弟，以事兄，未能也；所求乎朋友，先施之，未能也。庸德之行，庸言之謹，有所不足，不敢不勉，有餘不敢盡。言顧行，行顧言，君子胡不慥慥爾！」
貫待價
同考試官教諭蔣　批：〔講自責自脩，宛然夫子語〕氣，且不泥陳說，尤有卓見，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭俞　批：〔格調高古，結意更精實。〕
考試官教諭孫　批：〔渾融峻潔，可佳。〕
聖人以常道自責，而因詳其慎脩之實焉。蓋君子之道，常道也，責諸己而慎脩之，是亦君子而已矣，何以遠人爲哉？《中庸》引言之意如此。謂夫道本不遠於人，學貴反求諸己，雖聖如孔子，亦有不能外者焉。彼其言曰：君子依乎中庸者也，而其道則有四；丘也願學君子者也，而其一尚未能。四者非他也，君臣、父子、兄弟、朋友，天下之
translation_en:
[Topic from the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong), chapter 13:] "In the Way of the noble man there are four things, none of which I, Qiu, have yet been able to achieve: to serve my father as I would require my son to serve me, I am not yet able; to serve my ruler as I would require my minister to serve me, I am not yet able; to serve my elder brother as I would require my younger brother to serve me, I am not yet able; to be the first to behave toward friends as I would require them to behave toward me, I am not yet able. In the practice of ordinary virtues and the caution of ordinary words, if there is any deficiency, I dare not but exert myself; if there is any excess, I dare not exhaust it. Words correspond to actions, and actions correspond to words—how could the noble man not be earnestly genuine!"

Guan Daijia 貫待價

Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Jiang 蔣 comments: [In explaining self-reproach and self-cultivation, it captures the very tone of the Master's own words]; moreover, it is not bogged down in hackneyed explanations and possesses exceptional insight. It should be selected and recorded as a model.
Examiner, Instructor Yu 俞 comments: [Its style and tone are lofty and antique, and its concluding thought is even more precise and substantial.]
Examiner, Instructor Sun 孫 comments: [Harmoniously integrated and austerely pure; commendable.]

The Sage reproaches himself by the standard of the constant Way, and thereby details the substance of his careful self-cultivation. Indeed, the Way of the noble man is the constant Way. To demand it of oneself and carefully cultivate it is simply to be a noble man oneself—why would one treat the Way as distant from human beings? Such is the meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) in quoting these words.

It means to say that the Way is fundamentally not distant from human beings, and that in learning, what is valued is seeking it within oneself; even a sage like Confucius (Kongzi 孔子) could not depart from this. As his words state: The noble man is one who abides by the Mean and the常 (zhongyong), and his Way has four aspects; I, Qiu, am one who wishes to learn from the noble man, yet I have not been able to achieve even one of them. These four are nothing other than ruler and minister, father and son, elder and younger brother, and friends—the world's…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
大倫也事親事君從兄交友天下之大道也吾
以是而求諸人固欲其兼盡而不遺何其重以
周也及以是而反諸己則歉於躬行之未得又
何其輕以約也然是道也合人己而一之者也
君子能之而我獨不能道豈遠乎哉亦爲之而
已矣故道體諸身庸德也吾行之而尤勉其所
不足道見乎辭庸言也吾謹之而尤約其所有
餘斯則不必遠人以爲言而言皆有物可言亦
可行也不必遠人以爲行而行皆有恒可行亦
===
可言也文之以君子之辭而德足以立其誠實
之以君子之德而文有以足其志豈不慥慥乎
君子哉蓋至是則自脩者爲有成而自責爲不
虛矣在聖人且不敢求諸遠也而況於學者乎
嘗謂無聲無臭性道之極也而其實則庸德庸
言蔽之以爲庸而忽焉故未有能詣其極者觀
堯舜之道盡於孝弟三代之學止於明倫率性
之旨思過半矣孔子方以是爲未逮而脩之彼
棄其庸而高遠其說者皆欲賢於孔子者也尚
punctuated: 大倫也；事親、事君、從兄、交友，天下之大道也。吾以是而求諸人，固欲其兼盡而不遺，何其重以周也！及以是而反諸己，則歉於躬行之未得，又何其輕以約也！然是道也，合人己而一之者也。君子能之，而我獨不能，道豈遠乎哉？亦爲之而已矣。故道體諸身，庸德也，吾行之而尤勉其所不足；道見乎辭，庸言也，吾謹之而尤約其所有餘。斯則不必遠人以爲言，而言皆有物，可言亦可行也；不必遠人以爲行，而行皆有恒，可行亦可言也。文之以君子之辭，而德足以立其誠；實之以君子之德，而文有以足其志，豈不慥慥乎君子哉！蓋至是則自脩者爲有成，而自責爲不虛矣。在聖人且不敢求諸遠也，而況於學者乎？嘗謂無聲無臭，性道之極也，而其實則庸德、庸言蔽之。以爲庸而忽焉，故未有能詣其極者。觀堯、舜之道盡於孝弟，三代之學止於明倫，率性之旨，思過半矣。孔子方以是爲未逮而脩之，彼棄其庸而高遠其說者，皆欲賢於孔子者也，尚
translation_en:
…great cardinal relationships of the world; serving one's parents, serving one's ruler, obeying one's elder brother, and associating with friends are the great universal ways of the world. When I demand these of others, I certainly wish them to fulfill them all without omission—how weighty and comprehensive that is! Yet when I turn and examine myself by these same standards, I feel deficient in not having achieved them in my own personal conduct—how slight and meager that is! Still, this Way is what unites others and the self into one. If the superior man is capable of it and I alone am not, is the Way really far off? It is simply a matter of practicing it.

Therefore, the Way embodied in one's person is ordinary virtue; I practice it and strive especially hard where I fall short. The Way manifested in speech is ordinary words; I am cautious with them and restrain especially what is excessive. Thus one need not distance oneself from humanity in order to speak, for every word has substance, and what can be spoken can also be practiced; one need not distance oneself from humanity in order to act, for every action has constancy, and what can be practiced can also be spoken. Adorning it with the words of a superior man while one's virtue suffices to establish its sincerity, and substantiating it with the virtue of a superior man while one's words suffice to fulfill one's intent—is this not indeed a superior man of earnestness and篤 [genuineness]? For when one reaches this point, self-cultivation achieves completion and self-reproach is not in vain. Even a sage does not dare to seek the Way in what is distant; how much less should learners!

I have held that being "without sound or scent" is the ultimate reach of human nature and the Way, yet in reality it is summed up in ordinary virtues and ordinary words. Because people regard them as ordinary and neglect them, none are able to reach that ultimate height. When we observe that the Way of Yao and Shun was exhausted in filial piety and fraternal respect, and that the learning of the Three Dynasties stopped at clarifying human relationships, we are already more than halfway to grasping the purport of "following one's nature." Confucius himself considered these things something he had not yet attained and cultivated them; those who cast aside what is ordinary and make their doctrines lofty and distant all wish to be worthier than Confucius. How…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
可與入道乎
有布縷之征粟米之征力役之征君子用
其一緩其二
楊鳳
同考試官敎諭張　批〔取民有制先王愛民之實心也子能發之而末復歸重於節儉尤爲有識〕
同考試官學正齊　批〔發揮明悉一結尤見經濟有養之士也錄之〕
考試官敎諭俞　批〔格高詞整〕
考試官敎諭孫　批〔警拔之作〕
===
制天下之賦有三而取之則以時也夫三賦皆
出於民制也而以其時取之庶不病民耳孟氏
之言其有感乎且夫先王之於民也不得已而
制賦尤不得已而用之是故其制之有法而用
之有道焉上焉者計一國之所需而取乎下以
爲經用之常下焉者量一歲之所有以輸乎上
而共惟正之義自任嬪以織而九幣興也於是
布縷有征焉不必織而衣矣自任農以耕而九
punctuated:
可與入道乎？

「有布縷之征，粟米之征，力役之征。君子用其一，緩其二。」
楊鳳
同考試官敎諭張　批〔取民有制，先王愛民之實心也。子能發之，而末復歸重於節儉，尤爲有識。〕
同考試官學正齊　批〔發揮明悉，一結尤見經濟，有養之士也，錄之。〕
考試官敎諭俞　批〔格高詞整。〕
考試官敎諭孫　批〔警拔之作。〕

制天下之賦有三，而取之則以時也。夫三賦皆出於民，制也；而以其時取之，庶不病民耳。孟氏之言，其有感乎！且夫先王之於民也，不得已而制賦，尤不得已而用之。是故其制之有法，而用之有道焉。上焉者，計一國之所需而取乎下，以爲經用之常；下焉者，量一歲之所有以輸乎上，而共惟正之義。自任嬪以織，而九幣興也，於是布縷有征焉，不必織而衣矣；自任農以耕，而九
translation_en:
…can one ever enter into the Way with them?

"There are the levies of cloth and silk thread, the levies of grain and rice, and the levies of corvée labor. A gentleman employs one of them while deferring the other two."
Yang Feng 楊鳳
Associate Examiner, County Instructor Zhang 張, comments: "That taking from the people is governed by regulation reflects the genuine heart of the former kings in loving the people. You have been able to elucidate this, and at the end you further place supreme emphasis on frugality, which shows particular insight."
Associate Examiner, Subprefectural Instructor Qi 齊, comments: "The exposition is clear and thorough, and the conclusion especially reveals statecraft. He is a scholar of cultivation; record it."
Examiner, County Instructor Yu 俞, comments: "Lofty in style and well-ordered in diction."
Examiner, County Instructor Sun 孫, comments: "A striking and outstanding piece."

The exactions instituted for the realm are three, yet they are collected according to the season. Now, that all three exactions come from the people is the established institution; yet collecting them in their proper season ensures that the people are not afflicted. How deeply felt were the words of Mencius! Moreover, in their dealings with the people, the former kings instituted exactions only out of necessity, and employed them with even greater reluctance. Therefore, there was a method in instituting them, and a proper way in employing them. Those above calculated the needs of the entire state and took from those below to serve as the constant provision for regular expenditures; those below measured what they produced in a year to deliver to those above, fulfilling the righteous duty of offering the regular tribute. Once women were charged with weaving and the nine currencies of cloth flourished, there was the levy of cloth and silk thread, so that rulers were clothed without having to weave themselves. Once farmers were charged with plowing and the nine…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
穀生也於是粟米有征焉不必耕而食矣自任
力以夫而九夫有餘力也於是力役有征焉則
又以佚道使之矣夫是三者法也廢一焉不可
也而善用法者君子也兼取焉不可也故夏入
其布縷矣而粟米之賦必俟乎有秋秋斂其粟
米矣而力役之徵必乘乎農隙相天時之消息
以爲後先而用其一者非所以厲民也國計存
焉雖欲不用不可得也而況用之猶有所緩乎
度民力之盈虛以爲伸縮而緩其二者非所以
===
病國也邦本繫焉雖欲不緩不可得也而況緩
之將有所用乎此君子於斂民之中而存愛民
之仁也彼其取民無藝者亦獨何哉抑用一緩
二之道行則盈常在民詘常在國即國用有不
繼柰何曰食之以時用之以禮先王以儉德爲
永圖不繼非所患也故易曰節以制度不傷財
不害民而取民有制惟恭儉之君能之戰國諸
侯以侈相尚其勢不得不橫斂於民卒之民貧
而國益蹙可鑒哉
punctuated: 穀生也，於是粟米有征焉，不必耕而食矣；自任力以夫而九夫有餘力也，於是力役有征焉，則又以佚道使之矣。夫是三者，法也，廢一焉不可也；而善用法者，君子也，兼取焉不可也。故夏入其布縷矣，而粟米之賦必俟乎有秋；秋斂其粟米矣，而力役之徵必乘乎農隙。相天時之消息以爲後先，而用其一者，非所以厲民也，國計存焉，雖欲不用不可得也，而況用之猶有所緩乎？度民力之盈虛以爲伸縮，而緩其二者，非所以病國也，邦本繫焉，雖欲不緩不可得也，而況緩之將有所用乎？此君子於斂民之中而存愛民之仁也，彼其取民無藝者亦獨何哉！抑用一緩二之道行，則盈常在民，詘常在國，即國用有不繼，柰何？曰：食之以時，用之以禮，先王以儉德爲永圖，不繼非所患也。故《易》曰：「節以制度，不傷財，不害民。」而取民有制，惟恭儉之君能之。戰國諸侯以侈相尚，其勢不得不橫斂於民，卒之民貧而國益蹙，可鑒哉！
translation_en: …types of grain grow, and thereupon there is the levy on grain, so one wears food without having to plow; since assigning labor to adult men so that the nine classes of laborers have surplus strength, thereupon there is the levy on corvée labor, and thus again they are employed in a way that gives them ease. Now, these three are the statutory law, and to abolish any one of them is impermissible; yet he who is skilled at applying the law is the noble man, and to exact them simultaneously is impermissible. Therefore, in summer they bring in their cloth and silk thread, while the tax of grain must await the autumn harvest; in autumn they collect their grain, while the requisition of corvée labor must take advantage of the slack season in farming. Observing the waxing and waning of the seasons of Heaven to determine what comes earlier and later, and employing one of them is not meant to oppress the people—the state finances depend on it, so even if one wished not to employ it, that would be impossible; how much more so when in employing it there is still something that is deferred? Measuring the abundance and exhaustion of the people's strength to determine when to expand and contract, and deferring two of them is not meant to harm the state—the foundation of the realm is bound up with it, so even if one wished not to defer them, that would be impossible; how much more so when in deferring them they will eventually be employed? This is how the noble man, in the midst of collecting from the people, preserves the benevolence of loving the people. Why ever is it that those others exact from the people without limit! Yet if the way of employing one and deferring two is practiced, then surplus will always rest with the people and shortfall will always rest with the state; if state expenditures cannot be sustained, what then? One may reply: consume things according to the season and use them according to ritual propriety; the former kings took the virtue of frugality as their lasting plan, so unsustainability was not what they worried about. Therefore the Book of Changes (Yi) says: "Regulating by means of institutional measures, one neither injures wealth nor harms the people." And exacting from the people with moderation is something only a reverent and frugal ruler can achieve. The feudal lords of the Warring States period vied with one another in extravagance; by the force of circumstances they could not avoid levying tyrannical exactions upon the people, and in the end the people were impoverished while their states grew ever more straitened—what a warning this is!

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
易
六三觀我生進退象曰觀我生進退未失
道也六四觀國之光利用賓于王象曰
觀國之光尚賓也九五觀我生君子无
咎象曰觀我生觀民也
曾曰唯
同考試官教諭朱　批〔題意本難隱括作者故易〕
〔支離獨此篇辭旨朗然首尾關鍵得法可佳可佳〕
同考試官教諭林　批〔說君臣爲觀處語意聯絡〕
〔氣象森嚴傑作也錄之〕
===
考試官教諭俞　批〔是易義之精者取之〕
考試官教諭孫　批〔渾融古雅學識俱到〕
二聖歷發觀爻之義而君臣之爲觀備矣夫觀
我觀光臣道也而君之觀民則有大於是者宜
二聖歷發其義與且觀之爲道達乎上下者也
顧爻之所値特位異焉觀亦區以別矣彼六三
六四皆以柔順而位乎九五之下有臣道焉然
三遠而在野觀光猶非其時也故惟觀其所行
punctuated:
《易》
「六三，觀我生，進退。《象》曰：『觀我生進退，未失道也。』六四，觀國之光，利用賓于王。《象》曰：『觀國之光，尚賓也。』九五，觀我生，君子无咎。《象》曰：『觀我生，觀民也。』」
曾曰唯

二聖歷發觀爻之義，而君臣之爲觀備矣。夫觀我、觀光，臣道也；而君之觀民，則有大於是者。宜二聖歷發其義與！且觀之爲道，達乎上下者也。顧爻之所値，特位異焉，觀亦區以別矣。彼六三、六四，皆以柔順而位乎九五之下，有臣道焉。然三遠而在野，觀光猶非其時也，故惟觀其所行…
translation_en:
Classic of Changes (Yijing)

"Six in the third place: Contemplating my own life, to advance or retreat. The Commentary on the Images (Xiang) says: 'Contemplating my own life, to advance or retreat—one has not yet lost the Way.' Six in the fourth place: Contemplating the glory of the state, it is fitting to be a guest of the king. The Commentary on the Images says: 'Contemplating the glory of the state—this esteems being a guest.' Nine in the fifth place: Contemplating my own life, the superior man is without blame. The Commentary on the Images says: 'Contemplating my own life—this means contemplating the people.'"

Zeng Yuewei 曾曰唯

Associate Examiner and Instructor Zhu comments: [The meaning of this topic is inherently difficult to summarize, so writers easily become fragmented. Only in this essay are the diction and purport clear and bright, with the key links from beginning to end well-methodized. Commendable, commendable!]
Associate Examiner and Instructor Lin comments: [Where it discusses ruler and minister engaging in contemplation, the wording and ideas are interconnected and the atmosphere is majestic and solemn. It is a masterpiece; record it.]
Examiner and Instructor Yu comments: [This is a quintessential exposition of the meaning of the Classic of Changes; select it.]
Examiner and Instructor Sun comments: [Harmoniously integrated and classically elegant; both learning and insight have reached the mark.]

The two sages successively set forth the meanings of the lines of the hexagram Contemplation (Guan 觀), and thus the practice of contemplation by ruler and minister is complete. Now, contemplating oneself and contemplating the glory of the state are the way of the minister; whereas the ruler's contemplating the people is something greater than these. How fitting it is that the two sages successively set forth their meanings! Moreover, the way of contemplation extends through both above and below. Yet because the situations encountered by the lines differ specifically in their positions, their contemplation is accordingly differentiated into distinct categories. Both Six in the third place and Six in the fourth place, being yielding and compliant, are positioned below Nine in the fifth place, and thus embody the way of the minister. However, the third line is distant and out in the wilderness, so it is not yet the time for it to contemplate the glory of the state; therefore, it only contemplates its own conduct…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
焉以吾道之通塞爲行藏而始進之正蓋知所
自重矣而象以未失道與之人臣量入之義其
庶乎四近而在國觀民猶非其事也故得觀國
之光焉以吾身之親見爲慶幸而文治之休固
其所樂觀矣而象以尚賓申之人臣遇主之心
其慰乎至若五以剛中居上大下之大觀在焉
爻知天下之不易觀也而以觀我生先之蓋必
天德之無疵而後帝位爲不疚君子其寡過矣
乎象知我生之不易觀也而以觀民先之蓋徵
===
諸民者既詳則本諸身者益信君子其自考矣
乎茲又四之所觀以爲光而三之所恃以稟進
者也要之臣有所觀則道行而君益有所輔君
有所觀則道立而臣益知所尊周孔之繫易也
其爲世道計遠哉雖然君爲觀者也臣觀乎君
者也事君以自顯其六四乎則君以自治其六
三乎故聖人在上近臣式德遠臣希風萬化之
原在上不在下也神道以設教中正以觀天下
則固於君身先圖之易之爲訓昭昭矣
punctuated: 焉。以吾道之通塞爲行藏，而始進之正，蓋知所自重矣；而《象》以「未失道」與之，人臣量入之義，其庶乎！四近而在國，觀民猶非其事也，故得觀國之光焉。以吾身之親見爲慶幸，而文治之休，固其所樂觀矣；而《象》以「尚賓」申之，人臣遇主之心，其慰乎！至若五以剛中居上，大下之大觀在焉。爻知天下之不易觀也，而以「觀我生」先之，蓋必天德之無疵，而後帝位爲不疚，君子其寡過矣乎！《象》知我生之不易觀也，而以「觀民」先之，蓋徵諸民者既詳，則本諸身者益信，君子其自考矣乎！茲又四之所觀以爲光，而三之所恃以稟進者也。要之，臣有所觀則道行，而君益有所輔；君有所觀則道立，而臣益知所尊。周、孔之繫《易》也，其爲世道計遠哉！雖然，君爲觀者也，臣觀乎君者也。事君以自顯，其六四乎！則君以自治，其六三乎！故聖人在上，近臣式德，遠臣希風，萬化之原，在上不在下也。神道以設教，中正以觀天下，則固於君身先圖之，《易》之爲訓昭昭矣。
translation_en: … Putting the success or obstruction of one's own Way as the basis for advancing into office or withdrawing into seclusion, and maintaining rectitude at the outset of one's career—this shows that he knows how to respect himself. And when the Commentary on the Images (Xiang) praises him as "not yet having lost the Way," how close that comes to the principle of a subject measuring his entry into service! The fourth line is close at hand and resides in the state, yet observing the people is still not his affair; therefore, he is able to "observe the splendor of the state." Taking his personal witnessing of it as a matter for celebration, the flourishing of civil governance is indeed what he delights to behold. And when the Commentary on the Images elaborates on this with "honored as a guest," how comforted is the heart of a subject who has met his sovereign! As for the fifth line, occupying the supreme position with firmness and centrality, the great spectacle of all under heaven [transcription reads 大下 for 天下] rests therein. The line text knows that all under heaven cannot be lightly observed, and so puts "observing my own life" first; for only when one's heavenly virtue is without blemish can one occupy the imperial throne without remorse—how few will be the faults of the noble man! The Commentary on the Images knows that one's own life is not easily observed, and so puts "observing the people" first; for when the verification found among the people is already thorough, what is rooted in one's own person is all the more trustworthy—how deeply the noble man examines himself! This, in turn, is what the fourth line observes as splendor, and what the third line relies upon in order to take its cue to advance. In sum, when the subject has something to observe, the Way prevails and the ruler is all the more assisted; when the ruler has something to observe, the Way is established and the subjects all the more know what to revere. When the Duke of Zhou and Confucius appended their words to the Book of Changes (Yi), how far-reaching were their plans for the Way of the world! Even so, the ruler is the one who serves as the spectacle to be observed, while the subjects are those who observe the ruler. Serving the ruler in order to manifest oneself—is that not the Yin-fourth line (liusi)? Modeling oneself on the ruler in order to govern oneself—is that not the Yin-third line (liusan)? Therefore, when a sage is on high, close ministers take his virtue as their model and distant subjects yearn for his moral influence; the source of the myriad transformations lies above, not below. Establishing teachings through the spirit-way and displaying central rectitude before all under heaven—this must certainly be planned first in the ruler's own person. The instruction of the Book of Changes is bright and clear indeed!

text:
日新之謂盛德
史善言
同考試官教諭朱　批〔筆力簡勁體裁森整誦之〕
〔鏗然巾宮商可以言文矣〕

仁顯而不息造化之盛德昭矣盖仁自内顯其
===
機故不息也造化之爲德其盛矣乎大傳以天
地明道若曰道生於陰陽之迭運而神於德業
之互根是故天地之大業固由富有而名矣至
以顯仁爲盛德豈無謂哉使仁藏而未顯德固
無徵也或顯而易窮德猶未盛也惟夫化育流
行兩間之妙用日著機緘呈露天下之美利日
彰統觀之則大生焉廣生焉乾坤不毀而仁之
顯於乾坤者無止息也析觀之則形化焉氣化
焉萬物散殊而仁之顯於萬物者無終窮也日
punctuated:
「日新之謂盛德。」
史善言。

同考試官教諭林批：〔發明日新盛德，意精詞雅，易〕〔義之佳者。〕

仁顯而不息，造化之盛德昭矣。盖仁自内顯，其機故不息也；造化之爲德，其盛矣乎！《大傳》以天地明道，若曰：道生於陰陽之迭運，而神於德業之互根。是故天地之大業，固由富有而名矣；至以顯仁爲盛德，豈無謂哉？使仁藏而未顯，德固無徵也；或顯而易窮，德猶未盛也。惟夫化育流行，兩間之妙用日著；機緘呈露，天下之美利日彰。統觀之，則大生焉、廣生焉，乾坤不毀，而仁之顯於乾坤者無止息也；析觀之，則形化焉、氣化焉，萬物散殊，而仁之顯於萬物者無終窮也。日
translation_en:
"Daily renewal is called flourishing virtue." (Book of Changes, Great Treatise I.5)

By Shi Shanyan 史善言.

Associate Examiner and Instructor Zhu 朱 comments: [The brush-force is concise and vigorous, and the structural form is rigorous and orderly. Reciting it produces a resonant ring that hits [巾, error for 中] the musical notes gong and shang—this can truly be called literature!]
Associate Examiner and Instructor Lin 林 comments: [He elucidates "daily renewal" and "flourishing virtue" with refined thought and elegant diction; a fine piece of exposition on the Book of Changes.]
Examiner and Instructor Yu 俞 comments: [Skillfully brings out the Way of yin and yang.]
Examiner and Instructor Sun 孫 comments: [Precise and exact.]

When benevolence is manifested without cease, the flourishing virtue of creation is made bright. For benevolence manifests itself from within, and therefore its vital mechanism never ceases; how flourishing indeed is the virtue of creation! The Great Treatise (Dazhuan 大傳) illustrates the Way through Heaven and Earth, as if to say: The Way is generated through the alternating movement of yin and yang, and becomes unfathomable through the mutual rooting of virtue and achievement. Therefore, the "great achievement" of Heaven and Earth is indeed named from its "abundant possession"; as for taking the manifestation of benevolence to be "flourishing virtue," how could this be said without reason? Suppose benevolence were stored away and not yet manifested—then virtue would certainly have no verification; or suppose it were manifested yet easily exhausted—then virtue would still not be flourishing. Only when transforming nurture flows forth does the wondrous functioning between Heaven and Earth become daily more evident; only when the vital mechanism reveals itself do the admirable benefits of the world become daily more illustrious. Viewed as a whole, there is great generation and broad generation: Qian 乾 and Kun 坤 are never destroyed, and the benevolence manifested in Qian and Kun never pauses or ceases. Viewed in detail, there is transformation by form and transformation by vital氣 (qi 氣): the myriad things are dispersed in their diversity, and the benevolence manifested in the myriad things never ends or is exhausted. title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
新若此不謂之盛德乎蓋天地之大德不可見
而見於流行者如彼而卒無紀極也則絪緼化
醇之本益以昭大德之敦化本無形而形於呈
露者如斯而卒莫消長也則翕受敷施之原益
以顯有生者必有所以生生者而無聲無臭之
中一元之實理涵焉故仁愈顯而德愈不可窺
也何如其盛也耶有化者必有所以化化者而
惟玄惟默之表一元之真氣宰焉故仁愈新而
德愈不可量也孰能踰其盛耶夫德盛於內而
===
顯者日新陽之根乎陰也仁顯於外而新者日
盛陰之根乎陽也以此觀道不亦彰彰矣乎要
之德業一理顯藏一機故以用為業而曰藏用
莫非仁也以仁為德而曰顯仁莫非用也天地
鼓萬物聖人鼓萬民不同憂而同功者也然則
保大業者莫如盛德昭盛德者莫如日新古有
日新其德者其深於易乎
書
欽哉慎乃有位敬脩其可願
punctuated:
新若此，不謂之盛德乎？蓋天地之大德不可見，而見於流行者如彼，而卒無紀極也，則絪緼化醇之本益以昭；大德之敦化本無形，而形於呈露者如斯，而卒莫消長也，則翕受敷施之原益以顯。有生者，必有所以生生者，而無聲無臭之中，一元之實理涵焉，故仁愈顯而德愈不可窺也，何如其盛也耶！有化者，必有所以化化者，而惟玄惟默之表，一元之真氣宰焉，故仁愈新而德愈不可量也，孰能踰其盛耶！夫德盛於內，而顯者日新，陽之根乎陰也；仁顯於外，而新者日盛，陰之根乎陽也。以此觀道，不亦彰彰矣乎！要之，德業一理，顯藏一機。故以用為業，而曰「藏用」，莫非仁也；以仁為德，而曰「顯仁」，莫非用也。天地鼓萬物，聖人鼓萬民，不同憂而同功者也。然則保大業者莫如盛德，昭盛德者莫如日新。古有「日新其德」者，其深於《易》乎！
《書》
「欽哉！慎乃有位，敬脩其可願。」
translation_en:
…renovation like this, can it not be called "flourishing virtue"? Indeed, the great virtue of Heaven and Earth cannot be seen, yet what is seen in its flowing movement is like that, ultimately without bound or limit; thus the root of its generative fusion and transformative distillation is all the more illuminated. The profound transformation of great virtue originally has no form, yet what takes form in its manifestation is like this, ultimately without waxing or waning; thus the source of its receptive gathering and expansive bestowal is all the more manifested. Where there is generation, there must be that by which generation generates, and amidst that which has neither sound nor scent, the real principle of the unitary origin is contained therein; therefore, the more benevolence is manifested, the more unfathomable virtue becomes—how flourishing it is! Where there is transformation, there must be that by which transformation transforms, and beyond that which is profoundly dark and silent, the true vital energy of the unitary origin governs therein; therefore, the more benevolence is renewed, the more immeasurable virtue becomes—who could surpass its flourishing! Now, virtue flourishes within, while what is manifested is daily renewed: this is yang having its root in yin. Benevolence is manifested without, while what is renewed daily flourishes: this is yin having its root in yang. Viewed in this way, is not the Way brilliantly clear? In sum, virtue and enterprise are a single principle; manifestation and concealment are a single mechanism. Therefore, taking function as the enterprise and speaking of "concealing in the function"—none of this is not benevolence; taking benevolence as virtue and speaking of "manifesting in benevolence"—none of this is not function. Heaven and Earth rouse the myriad things, while the sage rouses the myriad people: they do not share the same anxieties, yet they share the same achievement. This being so, for preserving the great enterprise nothing equals flourishing virtue, and for illuminating flourishing virtue nothing equals daily renovation. In antiquity, he who spoke of "daily renewing his virtue"—how deeply versed he was in the Book of Changes (Yi)!

日二日有萬幾焉而兢業之懷不以可愛而或

Associate Examiner, Instructor Jiang 蔣 comments: In recounting the meaning of the admonition between sovereigns, his discourse on reverence is incisive, refined, and apt, without a single superfluous character or verbose phrase; reading it, one only fears reaching the end.
Examiner, Instructor Yu 俞 comments: He elucidates the reverence of virtue in a manner that is concise, polished, and outstanding.

For a ruler to be cautious in his Heaven-bestowed position lies simply in reverently cultivating his virtue. Great indeed is the necessity of being cautious regarding the Heaven-bestowed position! If one takes the virtue that is desirable and reverently cultivates it, has the way of the ruler not reached its utmost? When Emperor Shun 舜 charged Yu 禹, his meaning was as if to say: Emperors and kings preserve order through centrality, and they harmonize with centrality through reverence. Now that you occupy a position to be cherished and rule over a people to be feared [note: 令 here appears to be a woodblock misprint for 今, "now"], how could you not be reverent? Thus you must reflect on the difficulty of the Heaven-bestowed position: in a single day or two there are ten thousand subtle springs of action, and your feeling of cautious trepidation must never become neglectful because the position is to be cherished. You must reflect on the supreme importance of the foundation of the state: a common man or common woman may seem to prevail over me, and your sense of vigilant wariness must ever endure all the more because they are to be feared. When this mind stands in awe of what is above and below, exercising caution is precisely how one exercises reverence; when one guards the subtle springs between the precarious and the incipient, preserving the state is precisely how one preserves the position. What, then, is the business to be engaged in? It is simply to reverently cultivate what is desirable. For the goodness that is desirable resides in our own mind, and when extended to all under Heaven, it is what is called centrality. To neglect it and fail to cultivate it, or to cultivate it without reverence, is not what is meant by caution. Therefore, in heeding the charge to be cautious of the timely and subtle springs of action, there is no need to yearn for what is distant; the urgent task is solely…

text:
以全吾好德之良懋緝熈之功不必外有求也
而圖之所先惟以復吾同然之理以脩其內則
無敢逸豫也此中之生於心者益以敬而存而
