重周召同心尤非諸經生可及
punctuated:
以全吾好德之良；懋緝熈之功，不必外有求也，而圖之所先，惟以復吾同然之理。以脩其內，則無敢逸豫也，此中之生於心者，益以敬而存，而精一之古，庶幾其不悖乎？以脩其外，則無敢怠荒也，此中之見於事者，益以敬而聚，而聽察之用，庶幾其不淆乎？至是，則主敬之實功旣盡，愼位之大道無遺，君益見其可愛，而民將不復有可畏矣。汝其念之哉！抑禹克勤儉，而又不自滿假，豈復有所不敬，而舜惓惓戒之若是耶？蓋中者，帝王傳心之要，而敬則聖學之所以成始成終者也。他日禹之戒舜，亦曰：「無若丹朱傲。」君臣皆不自聖，而其心常相警也。後有作者，黄虞帝其不可及，信然哉！
曰其稽我古人之德，矧曰其有能稽謀自天。
李文郁
同考試官教諭蔣　批〔形容老成人語語精到，而結〕重周、召同心，尤非諸經生可及。
translation_en:
… lies solely in preserving intact our innate goodness that loves virtue; in exerting oneself in the work of continuous bright diligence, there is no need to seek anything outside, and what one plans first lies solely in restoring the principle shared by all. In cultivating the inner self, one dares not indulge in ease and pleasure; thus this Equilibrium born in the mind is increasingly preserved through reverence, and the ancient teaching [?] of refinement and single-mindedness will perhaps not be violated! In cultivating the outer self, one dares not be lazy or negligent; thus this Equilibrium manifested in affairs is increasingly gathered through reverence, and the function of listening and examining will perhaps not be confused! When this point is reached, the practical effort of holding fast to reverence is exhausted, and nothing of the great Way of being cautious of one's position is left out; the ruler will increasingly be seen as lovable, and the people will no longer be anything to be feared. Be mindful of this! Yet Yu was able to be diligent and frugal, and moreover was not self-satisfied or arrogant—how could there still be anything in which he was not reverent, that Shun should earnestly admonish him like this? For Equilibrium is the essential of the mind-to-mind transmission of emperors and kings, while reverence is that whereby sage learning completes both beginning and end. On another day, when Yu admonished Shun, he likewise said, "Do not be arrogant like Danzhu." Sovereign and minister alike did not regard themselves as sages, and their minds constantly cautioned one another. "Though there be worthy rulers who rise later, the Emperors of the eras of Xuanxuan [?] and Yu cannot be equaled"—truly this is so!

"Look to those who examine the virtue of our ancients; how much more when it is said they are able to examine counsels from Heaven!"
By Li Wenyu 李文郁.
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Jiang comments: 〔Every phrase describing the experienced elders hits the mark with precision, and the conclusion〕 emphasizing the shared mind of the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao is especially beyond the reach of the other examination candidates.

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭俞　批〔識力老成詞華暢竭〕
考試官教諭孫　批〔平正而有鋒芒〕
觀老成之達於事理其不可遺見矣夫事備于
古而理原於天者也老成皆有以稽之有國者
其可遺乎召公致誥成王若曰敬德不可不懋
是治之本也老成不可不任是德之輔也吾欲
王之無遺壽耇者豈無謂哉意曰事之已然者
有古人之德而實今之師也古人往矣而疇其
能稽之惟是壽耇閱歷深而聞見博前言往行
===
則多識焉遺風舊政則多考焉遠稽諸夏而祇
德以開基者可信而述也近稽諸殷而懋德以
永世者可惜而陳也蓋今人與居而實古人與
稽國有壽耇古人之典刑具在矣王欲師古以
建事舍是其奚倚哉矧曰理之自然者有天之
道而實政之憲也天道遠矣而疇其能稽之惟
是壽耇諳練久而計慮精窮神足以繼天志焉
知化足以述天事焉用之開人而成始之謀以
建先天而天弗違也用之立政而成終之謀以
punctuated:
考試官教諭俞　批：〔識力老成，詞華暢竭。〕
考試官教諭孫　批：〔平正而有鋒芒。〕

觀老成之達於事理，其不可遺見矣。夫事備于古，而理原於天者也。老成皆有以稽之，有國者其可遺乎？召公致誥成王若曰：敬德不可不懋，是治之本也；老成不可不任，是德之輔也。吾欲王之無遺壽耇者，豈無謂哉？意曰：事之已然者，有古人之德，而實今之師也。古人往矣，而疇其能稽之？惟是壽耇閱歷深而聞見博，前言往行則多識焉，遺風舊政則多考焉。遠稽諸夏，而祇德以開基者，可信而述也；近稽諸殷，而懋德以永世者，可惜而陳也。蓋今人與居，而實古人與稽。國有壽耇，古人之典刑具在矣。王欲師古以建事，舍是其奚倚哉？矧曰：理之自然者，有天之道，而實政之憲也。天道遠矣，而疇其能稽之？惟是壽耇諳練久而計慮精，窮神足以繼天志焉，知化足以述天事焉。用之開人，而成始之謀以建，先天而天弗違也；用之立政，而成終之謀以
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Yu, comment: [His insight is mature and seasoned, and his literary expression flows to the fullest.]
Examiner and Instructor Sun, comment: [Balanced and upright, yet with a sharp edge.]

Observing how veterans of ripe experience thoroughly comprehend affairs and principles, one can see that they must not be neglected. Now, affairs are fully exemplified in antiquity, and principles have their origin in Heaven. Experienced elders have the means to examine both—how, then, could the ruler of a state neglect them?

When Duke Shao (Shao Gong 召公) delivered his announcement to King Cheng (Cheng Wang 成王), it was as if to say: Reverent virtue cannot fail to be striven after, for it is the root of governance; experienced elders cannot fail to be employed, for they are the coadjutors of virtue. When I wish Your Majesty not to neglect the aged and venerable, how could it be without reason?

They say: Among affairs already past, there is the virtue of the ancients, which truly serves as the teacher of the present. The ancients are gone—who, then, is able to examine their ways? It is only these aged and venerable men, whose experience is deep and whose learning and observation are broad: they remember much of past words and bygone deeds, and they have investigated much of surviving customs and old administrations. Examining back afar to the Xia, how they revered virtue to lay the foundation of the dynasty can be trusted and recounted; examining nearer at hand to the Yin, how they strove in virtue to perpetuate their generations can be drawn upon [?] and set forth. Thus, though one dwells together with men of the present, in reality one is examining things together with the ancients. When the state possesses the aged and venerable, the statutes and models of the ancients are all present therein. If the King wishes to take antiquity as his teacher in establishing enterprises, apart from these men, upon whom could he rely?

How much more so when they say: Among principles that are naturally so, there is the Way of Heaven, which truly serves as the model for administration. The Way of Heaven is distant—who, then, is able to examine its counsels? It is only these aged and venerable men, whose familiarity and practice are long-standing and whose planning and deliberation are refined: their plumbing of the inscrutable is sufficient to carry on the intentions of Heaven, and their understanding of transformation is sufficient to transmit the enterprises of Heaven. Employ them to enlighten men, and counsels for bringing things to their inception are thereby established—preceding Heaven, yet Heaven does not act in opposition to them; employ them to establish governance, and counsels for bringing things to their completion are thereby…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
臧後天而奉天時也蓋人謀爲能而寔天謀爲
能國有壽耇上天之明命如臨矣王欲寔天以
致理舍是其奚從哉夫稽古則敬德爲有徵稽
天則受命爲有本甚矣老成之有益於人國也
嗣王其敬念之哉抑成王以幼冲嗣位師保之
責在周召故召不以跡而嫌於自任周不以親
而嫌於夾輔王雖幼冲卒能用壽耇以祈天永
命而爲守成令主也他日周公之語召公亦曰冀
其以耇造之德延長天命此不惟君臣同心而
六臣又自同心也周業之隆固有自哉
===
詩
有渰萋萋興雨祁祁雨我公田遂及我私
楊鳳
同考試官教諭張　批〔上下一體之意發明親切而語意溫醇是深于詩者〕
同考試官學正齊　批〔盛世太和之景象讀之宛然在目〕
考試官教諭俞　批〔微婉可誦〕
punctuated:
臧，後天而奉天時也。蓋人謀爲能，而寔天謀爲能；國有壽耇，上天之明命如臨矣。王欲寔天以致理，舍是其奚從哉？夫稽古則敬德爲有徵，稽天則受命爲有本，甚矣，老成之有益於人國也，嗣王其敬念之哉！抑成王以幼冲嗣位，師保之責在周、召，故召不以跡而嫌於自任，周不以親而嫌於夾輔；王雖幼冲，卒能用壽耇以祈天永命，而爲守成令主也。他日，周公之語召公，亦曰冀其以耇造之德延長天命。此不惟君臣同心，而六臣又自同心也。周業之隆，固有自哉！

詩
「有渰萋萋，興雨祁祁。雨我公田，遂及我私。」
楊鳳
同考試官教諭張　批〔上下一體之意，發明親切，而語意溫醇，是深于《詩》者。〕
同考試官學正齊　批〔盛世太和之景象，讀之宛然在目。〕
考試官教諭俞　批〔微婉可誦。〕
translation_en:
…is perfected, following Heaven and observing Heaven's seasons. For while they are capable in human counsels, they are in truth capable in Heaven's counsels; when a state possesses aged elders, it is as though the bright mandate of High Heaven were present right before it. If the king wishes to verify [?] Heaven in order to achieve good governance, whom could he follow if he set them aside? By examining antiquity, revering virtue has its verification; by examining Heaven, receiving the Mandate has its root. Great indeed is the benefit of experienced elders to a ruler's state! Let the successor king reverently bear this in mind!

Moreover, King Cheng succeeded to the throne in his tender youth, and the responsibilities of Grand Preceptor and Grand Protector rested with the Dukes of Zhou and Shao. Thus, the Duke of Shao did not shy away from taking the burden upon himself on account of outward appearances, nor did the Duke of Zhou shy away from assisting the king on account of their close kinship. Although the king was young, in the end he was able to employ aged elders to pray to Heaven for an enduring Mandate, becoming an admirable sovereign who preserved the dynastic achievements. On another day, when the Duke of Zhou spoke to the Duke of Shao, he likewise expressed the hope that through the virtue of aged and accomplished elders they might prolong Heaven's Mandate. In this, not only were sovereign and ministers of one mind, but the great [? text has "six", 六 for 大] ministers themselves were also of one mind with one another. The flourishing of the Zhou enterprise truly had its source!

Classic of Poetry (Shijing)
"Thickly gather thedark clouds, / Gently falls the rain. / May it rain first on our public fields, / And then reach our private ones."
Yang Feng 楊鳳
Associate Examiner, Instructor Zhang 張 comments: [The idea of superior and inferior forming a single body is elucidated with intimacy and clarity, while the diction and meaning are gentle and pure; this is someone deeply versed in the Classic of Poetry.]
Associate Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Qi 齊 comments: [Reading this, the scene of supreme harmony in a flourishing age appears vividly before one's eyes.]
Examiner, Instructor Yu 俞 comments: [Subtle, graceful, and worthy of recitation.]

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
農人其將何以為報耶噫此盛世太和之象也
上之言曰食我農人曰穀我士女此其心固無
一日不厚下者而下之懷德而思報則又于公
義焉先之仁施義報豈不藹然上下一體哉此
固三代流風之遠而可以興思於後世者也
聖敬日躋昭假遲遲上帝是祇
安文璧
同考試官教諭張　批〔事天以敬聖學也子能發抒〕
其蘊可以占所養矣
===
曌考試官學正齊　批〔說聖王事天處精切不浮〕
考試官教諭俞　批〔純正充融〕
考試官教諭孫　批〔得頌聖之體〕
商人頌聖祖敬德之至見受命之有自也夫敬
而久於格天敬之至也帝命之受豈偶然哉商
人祫祭之詩若曰帝王之興皆受命於天也然
天之所命在德而德之所聚在敬我湯既應時
而生矣而其事天之敬寧有所不至乎是故兢
業以自持不以帝命不違為可恃也而所以顧
punctuated:
農人其將何以為報耶？噫！此盛世太和之象也。上之言曰：「食我農人」，曰：「穀我士女」，此其心固無一日不厚下者；而下之懷德而思報，則又于公義焉先之。仁施義報，豈不藹然上下一體哉！此固三代流風之遠，而可以興思於後世者也。

「聖敬日躋，昭假遲遲，上帝是祇。」
安文璧
同考試官教諭張　批〔事天以敬，聖學也。子能發抒〕其蘊，可以占所養矣。
曌考試官學正齊　批〔說聖王事天處，精切不浮。〕
考試官教諭俞　批〔純正充融。〕
考試官教諭孫　批〔得頌聖之體。〕

商人頌聖祖敬德之至，見受命之有自也。夫敬而久於格天，敬之至也，帝命之受，豈偶然哉？商人祫祭之詩，若曰：帝王之興，皆受命於天也。然天之所命在德，而德之所聚在敬。我湯既應時而生矣，而其事天之敬，寧有所不至乎？是故兢業以自持，不以帝命不違為可恃也，而所以顧
translation_en:
…how then shall we farmers repay him? Ah! This is the very image of the supreme harmony of a flourishing age. The ruler speaks of "feeding our farmers" and "nourishing our young men and women"—his heart indeed never goes a single day without being generous to those below. And when those below cherish his virtue and think of repaying him, they in turn put public duty first. Benevolence is bestowed and righteousness returned in repayment—how harmoniously are ruler and subjects united as one body! Truly, this reflects the far-reaching influence of the customs of the Three Dynasties, which may well inspire reflection in later ages.

"His sagely reverence daily ascended; his bright influence reached far and long; the Lord on High he revered."
An Wenbi 安文璧
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔Serving Heaven with reverence is the learning of the sages. That you are able to unfold〕 its deeper meaning allows one to gauge what you have cultivated.
Associate [?] Examiner Qi, Subprefectural Instructor, comments: 〔The discussion of how the sage king serves Heaven is precise, incisive, and free of superficiality.〕
Examiner Yu, Instructor, comments: 〔Pure, upright, full, and harmonious.〕
Examiner Sun, Instructor, comments: 〔Captures the proper form for praising a sage.〕

The people of Shang praised the utmost reverent virtue of their sagely ancestor, thereby showing the source from which he received the Mandate. Now, to be reverent and enduring in reaching Heaven is the ultimate degree of reverence; how could the reception of the Lord's Mandate be accidental? In the ode for the collective ancestral sacrifice of the Shang people, it is as if to say: The rise of sovereigns and kings always comes from receiving the Mandate from Heaven. Yet what Heaven mandates rests upon virtue, and that wherein virtue gathers rests upon reverence. Since our Tang 湯 was born in response to the times, how could the reverence with which he served Heaven fail to reach the utmost in any respect? Therefore, he maintained himself with cautious diligence, not presuming that the unfailing favor of the Lord's Mandate could be relied upon; and the way in which he kept in view…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭孫　批〔雅暢〕
詩人望天澤而明於公私之義焉夫天普物而
無心者也詩人望雨而義先乎公其殆有以感
之乎大田之雅農夫所以荅君也意謂農人之
易其田也能盡其力而不能必其成成之者天
也而得天者其吾君乎今也苗盛而害除正百
穀仰膏之時而三農卒歲之望甚殷也安得渰
然作雲而氣之絪緼于山川者蓁蓁乎其上浮
沛然下雨而澤之霑被于田野者祁祁乎其有
===
漸夫雲雨興於天而其盛其徐皆上帝之賜也
感通田於人而雲行雨施皆君德之徵也顧我
農夫豈敢貪天功而忘帝力哉吾願神明之貺
先足於公卿之大田而後同井八家均得以沾
夫普徧之澤冲漠之施先既於曾孫之多稼而
後一夫百畝均得以沐夫優渥之恩蓋天以君
之故而降雨其眷顧乎君者亦因以敷錫于民
也民以君之故而遂私其徼福于天者實所以
受賜于君也君之格天有素而天之惠我無窮
punctuated:
考試官教諭孫　批〔雅暢〕

詩人望天澤而明於公私之義焉。夫天普物而無心者也，詩人望雨而義先乎公，其殆有以感之乎？《大田》之雅，農夫所以荅君也。意謂農人之易其田也，能盡其力而不能必其成，成之者天也，而得天者其吾君乎！今也苗盛而害除，正百穀仰膏之時，而三農卒歲之望甚殷也。安得渰然作雲，而氣之絪緼于山川者蓁蓁乎其上浮；沛然下雨，而澤之霑被于田野者祁祁乎其有漸。夫雲雨興於天，而其盛其徐皆上帝之賜也；感通田於人，而雲行雨施皆君德之徵也。顧我農夫，豈敢貪天功而忘帝力哉！吾願神明之貺，先足於公卿之大田，而後同井八家均得以沾夫普徧之澤；冲漠之施，先既於曾孫之多稼，而後一夫百畝均得以沐夫優渥之恩。蓋天以君之故而降雨，其眷顧乎君者，亦因以敷錫于民也；民以君之故而遂私，其徼福于天者，實所以受賜于君也。君之格天有素，而天之惠我無窮，
translation_en:
Examiner and County Director of Studies Sun comments: 〔Refined and fluent〕

The poet hopes for Heaven's moisture and is clear about the right principle of public versus private. Now, Heaven extends universally to all things without partial intent; when the poet hopes for rain and puts the public interest first in righteousness, is it not perhaps because something has moved him to do so? The Minor Ode "Great Fields" (Datian) is that whereby the farmers respond to their ruler. Its meaning is that when farmers cultivate their fields, they can exhaust their strength, yet they cannot guarantee the harvest; what brings it to completion is Heaven, and the one who wins Heaven's favor—is it not our ruler? Now the sprouts are flourishing and the pests are removed; it is just the time when the hundred grains look up for fertilizing rain, and the three classes of farmers have most ardent hopes of completing the year. How might we obtain clouds gathering densely, their vital vapor coalescing over mountains and streams, rising luxuriantly upward; and rain falling in abundance, its moisture soaking the fields and wilds, coming gently and gradually! Now, clouds and rain arise in Heaven, and both their fullness and their gentle pace are gifts of the Lord on High; sympathetic resonance originates [?] in man, and the movement of clouds and bestowal of rain are both tokens of the ruler's virtue. Yet as for us farmers, how would we dare to covet Heaven's achievement as our own or forget the sovereign's effort! We wish that the bounty of the spirits may first suffice for the great fields of the lords and ministers, and only afterward may the eight families of the same well-field all alike be moistened by that universal grace; that the bestowal from the vast unseen may first be consummated among the manifold crops of the "distant descendant" [the ruler], and only afterward may each husbandman's hundred mu all alike be bathed in that generous favor. For Heaven sends down rain for the ruler's sake, and its loving regard for the ruler is thereby also spread and bestowed upon the people; the people fulfill their private needs for the ruler's sake, and the blessings they seek from Heaven are in reality received as gifts from the ruler. The ruler's reaching of Heaven has been long established, and Heaven's kindness to us is inexhaustible…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
諟乎明命者日勵夫嚴翼之誠時幾以自勑不
以天錫勇知爲足多也而所以緝熙乎敬德者
允底於高明之極制事制心聖域雖優入矣而
內外交脩之功尤有遲遲乎日新而月盛者蓋
天之命不已而湯之心乎敬亦不已也不邇不
殖大德雖懋昭矣而始終惟愼之心尤有遲遲
乎日就而月將者蓋天之命不息而湯之格乎
天亦不息也克敬惟親天何心也湯卽以此心
明事之簡在方殷而欽崇之益至靜與俱動與
===
游上帝其陟降矣奚俟於明禋之薦而後格耶
惟德是輔天何心也湯卽以此心祇若之眷顧
方切而對越之益恭繼其志述其事神明其合
德矣奚俟於黍稷之馨而後享耶至是則濬哲
之德以全而長發之祥自應其受命而式九圍
也宜哉抑斯敬也精一之心法也湯固得統于
三聖而弼贊之功尹居多焉觀其言曰以祇承
上帝神祇罔不祇肅可知已然則敬固受命之
本而佐命保邦所頼於一德之臣者豈其微哉
punctuated: 諟乎明命者，日勵夫嚴翼之誠；時幾以自勑，不以天錫勇知爲足多也，而所以緝熙乎敬德者，允底於高明之極。制事制心，聖域雖優入矣，而內外交脩之功，尤有遲遲乎日新而月盛者，蓋天之命不已，而湯之心乎敬亦不已也。不邇不殖，大德雖懋昭矣，而始終惟愼之心，尤有遲遲乎日就而月將者，蓋天之命不息，而湯之格乎天亦不息也。克敬惟親，天何心也？湯卽以此心明事之，簡在方殷，而欽崇之益至，靜與俱，動與游，上帝其陟降矣，奚俟於明禋之薦而後格耶？惟德是輔，天何心也？湯卽以此心祇若之，眷顧方切，而對越之益恭，繼其志，述其事，神明其合德矣，奚俟於黍稷之馨而後享耶？至是，則濬哲之德以全，而長發之祥自應，其受命而式九圍也宜哉！抑斯敬也，精一之心法也。湯固得統于三聖，而弼贊之功，尹居多焉。觀其言曰「以祇承上帝，神祇罔不祇肅」，可知已。然則敬固受命之本，而佐命保邦，所頼於一德之臣者，豈其微哉！
translation_en: … contemplating the bright mandate of Heaven, daily spurred on his stern and reverent sincerity. Ever watchful of the subtle springs of action to admonish himself, he did not regard the valor and wisdom bestowed by Heaven as sufficient cause for complacency; and thus that whereby he continuously brightened his reverent virtue truly reached the utmost height and brilliance. In regulating affairs and regulating his mind, although he had already entered effortlessly into the realm of sagehood, his effort at cultivating both the internal and the external still advanced unhurriedly, renewing itself day by day and flourishing month by month—for the mandate of Heaven is unceasing, and Tang's mindfulness of reverence was likewise unceasing. Neither approaching sensual pleasures nor hoarding wealth, although his great virtue shone forth brightly, his mind of constant caution from beginning to end still advanced unhurriedly, making daily progress and monthly attainment—for the mandate of Heaven never rests, and Tang's reaching to Heaven likewise never rested. "Having affection only for those who are capable of reverence"—what mind does Heaven have in this? Tang simply served Heaven enlightenedly with this very mind. Even when Heaven's selection of him was at its height, his reverence and veneration grew all the more extreme. Accompanying Him in stillness and roaming with Him in movement, the Lord on High ascended and descended with him! Why wait for the offering of pure sacrifices before reaching Him? "Assisting only virtue"—what mind does Heaven have in this? Tang simply complied with Heaven reverently with this very mind. Even when Heaven's affectionate regard was most earnest, his standing in response before It grew all the more respectful. Continuing Its will and carrying forward Its undertakings, he united his virtue with the spirits and gods! Why wait for the fragrant aroma of millet offerings before they would accept? When it came to this, his profound and wise virtue was complete, and the auspicious omen of long-lasting prosperity naturally responded. That he received the Mandate and became the model for the nine regions—how fitting indeed! Yet this reverence is none other than the mental discipline of refinement and single-mindedness. To be sure, Tang inherited the line of transmission from the Three Sages, yet in the merit of assisting and supporting him, Yi Yin held the greater part. Looking at his words, "Thereby reverently receiving the Lord on High, so that among the spirits of Heaven and Earth there were none that did not reverently stand in awe," one may know this well enough. Since this is so, while reverence is assuredly the root of receiving the Mandate, in assisting the Mandate and preserving the state, is that which depends upon a minister of pure and single virtue anything slight?

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄

春秋
晉侯伐秦〔文公四年〕
韓果

春秋善强國之改過故不責霸兵以致意焉夫
改過不吝王者事也觀秦穆之受晉兵其賢足
===
稱矣春秋不貶晉以深善之固宜且晉曷伐秦
報王官之役也而秦師不出自是二國之兵爭
絕焉然則不報者秦也必報者晉也春秋宜罪
襄矣而爵之何君子曰襄何足責哉穆之賢因
以著矣蓋立於無過惟聖者能之過而能改亦
君子之所難也穆公初敗於殽悔過自誓亦知
所自新矣使在今日晉曰伐秦亦曰戰穆何以
賢於襄乎乃能審致師之由而深悔其前事之
失堅自誓之義而不敢爲怙終之非邧邑之圍
punctuated:
《春秋》
晉侯伐秦〔文公四年〕
韓果
同考試官教諭余　批〔《書》錄《秦誓》，取穆公善補過也。子於《春秋》不責晉兵處互發之，而辭復高古嚴正，當是異才。〕
考試官教諭俞　批〔題難，而作更古雅。〕
考試官教諭孫　批〔高簡磊落，可愛。〕
《春秋》善强國之改過，故不責霸兵以致意焉。夫改過不吝，王者事也。觀秦穆之受晉兵，其賢足稱矣，《春秋》不貶晉以深善之，固宜。且晉曷伐秦？報王官之役也。而秦師不出，自是二國之兵爭絕焉。然則不報者，秦也；必報者，晉也。《春秋》宜罪襄矣，而爵之，何？君子曰：襄何足責哉！穆之賢因以著矣。蓋立於無過，惟聖者能之；過而能改，亦君子之所難也。穆公初敗於殽，悔過自誓，亦知所自新矣。使在今日，晉曰伐，秦亦曰戰，穆何以賢於襄乎？乃能審致師之由，而深悔其前事之失；堅自誓之義，而不敢爲怙終之非。邧邑之圍，
translation_en:
Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
"The Marquis of Jin attacked Qin" [Fourth year of Duke Wen]
Han Guo 韓果
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Yu: [The Book of Documents (Shu) records the "Oath of Qin" ("Qin shi"), approving of Duke Mu's ability to make amends for his faults. You cross-illuminate this at the point where the Spring and Autumn Annals does not censure Jin's military action, and your diction is moreover lofty, ancient, stern, and upright—truly an extraordinary talent.]
Comment by Examiner Instructor Yu: [The topic is difficult, yet the composition is all the more ancient and elegant.]
Comment by Examiner Instructor Sun: [Lofty, concise, open, and forthright—delightful.]
The Spring and Autumn Annals commends a powerful state for reforming its faults, and therefore does not censure the hegemon's military action, so as to convey this meaning. Now, not being stingy in reforming one's faults is the business of a true king. Observing how Duke Mu of Qin accepted Jin's military attack, his worthiness is well worth praising; that the Spring and Autumn Annals does not demean Jin in order to deeply commend him is certainly fitting. Moreover, why did Jin attack Qin? To retaliate for the campaign of Wangguan. Yet the Qin army did not come out, and from this point the military strife between the two states ceased. This being so, the one that did not retaliate was Qin, and the one determined to retaliate was Jin. The Spring and Autumn Annals ought to have condemned Duke Xiang of Jin, yet it refers to him by his noble rank—why? The gentleman says: How is Xiang worth censuring! The worthiness of Mu was thereby made manifest. Indeed, to stand completely free of fault is something only a sage can do; to have faults and be able to reform them is also what a gentleman finds difficult. When Duke Mu was first defeated at Yao, he repented of his faults and made a solemn oath to himself, thus knowing how to renew himself. Supposing that on this day, when Jin said "attack," Qin had also said "fight," how would Mu have been any worthier than Xiang? Instead, he was able to examine the reason that had drawn the enemy army, and deeply repent the errors of his past actions; he held fast to the righteousness of his self-oath, and did not dare commit the wrong of persisting in error to the end. title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
晉之脩怨深矣而惟堅壁以自全非百二之險
不足憑也念責人之不如自責而所謂詢黃髮
以罔愆者其克踐乎新城之取秦之受侮亟矣
而惟囷囷以退避非三帥之力不足恃也悟勇
夫之不如良士而所謂思秉聖以職利者其兌
蹈乎噫昔日之貳過一秦也今日之改過又一
秦也穆也賢乎哉春秋大改過嘉釋怨故晉以
爵稱非貸晉也以常情待襄而以王事賢穆也
君子謂不譏晉爲予秦蓋得聖人錄秦誓之意
===
與且穆何以能賢哉蓋思蹇叔用孟明而子桑
百里彬彬在位視先軫諸臣過之是故襄之不
穆以佐之者非也雖然穆亦未爲得焉濟河之
忿已逞而新城之師不出其悔過也誠耶僞耶
即霸非君子所談而況不終爲盟主耶
楚屈完來盟于師盟于召陵〔僖公四年夏〕
四月己巳晉侯齊師宋師秦師及楚人
戰于城濮楚師敗績〔僖公二十有八年〕
晉欒書帥師救鄭〔成公六年夏五月甲〕
punctuated:
晉之脩怨深矣，而惟堅壁以自全，非百二之險不足憑也，念責人之不如自責，而所謂「詢黃髮以罔愆」者，其克踐乎？新城之取，秦之受侮亟矣，而惟囷囷以退避，非三帥之力不足恃也，悟勇夫之不如良士，而所謂「思秉聖以職利」者，其兌蹈乎？噫！昔日之貳過，一秦也；今日之改過，又一秦也。穆也賢乎哉！《春秋》大改過，嘉釋怨，故晉以爵稱，非貸晉也，以常情待襄，而以王事賢穆也。君子謂不譏晉爲予秦，蓋得聖人錄《秦誓》之意與！且穆何以能賢哉？蓋思蹇叔，用孟明，而子桑、百里彬彬在位，視先軫諸臣過之。是故襄之不穆，以佐之者非也。雖然，穆亦未爲得焉。濟河之忿已逞，而新城之師不出，其悔過也，誠耶？僞耶？即霸非君子所談，而況不終爲盟主耶？

楚屈完來盟于師，盟于召陵。〔僖公四年〕夏四月己巳，晉侯、齊師、宋師、秦師及楚人戰于城濮，楚師敗績。〔僖公二十有八年〕晉欒書帥師救鄭。〔成公六年〕夏五月甲…
translation_en:
…Jin’s pursuit of its grievance went deep indeed, yet Qin merely fortified its ramparts to preserve itself. This was not because its strategic passes—where two men could hold off a hundred—were insufficient to rely upon; rather, Duke Mu reflected that blaming others was not as good as blaming oneself, and thus was he not able to fulfill his own words about "consulting the yellow-haired elders so as to be free from error"? In the capture of Xincheng, the humiliation suffered by Qin was acute indeed, yet it merely withdrew and stayed coiled in defense [? 囷囷]. This was not because the strength of its three commanders was insufficient to depend upon; rather, he realized that brave warriors were not as good as virtuous officers, and thus was he not able to truly tread the path of what he called "hoping for one who holds fast to sageliness in order to secure benefit for our descendants" [? 思秉聖以職利者其兌蹈乎]?

Alas! The Qin that repeated its transgression in the past was one Qin; the Qin that reformed its transgression today is another Qin. How worthy was Duke Mu! The Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) attaches great importance to reforming transgressions and commends letting go of resentment. Therefore, the ruler of Jin is referred to by his noble title—not out of leniency toward Jin, but because the text treats Duke Xiang according to ordinary human passions while honoring Duke Mu according to the affairs of a true king. When the gentleman says that refraining from criticizing Jin is a way of praising Qin, has he not grasped the Sage’s intention in recording the "Oath of Qin" (Qin shi) in the Book of Documents?

Moreover, how was Duke Mu able to attain such worthiness? It was because he remembered Jian Shu, employed Mengming, and had Zisang and Baili Xi flourishing in office—ministers who surpassed Xian Zhen and the other officials of Jin. Therefore, that Duke Xiang failed to match Duke Mu was because those who assisted him were not the right men. Even so, Duke Mu cannot be considered to have fully attained the right way either. Once his anger had already been vented by crossing the Yellow River, he then declined to send out troops at Xincheng—was his repentance of his faults sincere, or was it feigned? Even hegemony is not something a gentleman speaks of, how much less one who did not even end up as lord of the covenant!

Qu Wan of Chu came to make a covenant with the allied army, and made a covenant at Shaoling. [Fourth year of Duke Xi.] In summer, in the fourth month, on the jisi day, the Marquis of Jin, the army of Qi, the army of Song, and the army of Qin fought with the men of Chu at Chengpu; the army of Chu was utterly defeated. [Twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi.] Luan Shu of Jin led an army to relieve Zheng. [Sixth year of Duke Cheng.] In summer, in the fifth month, on the jia…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
午遂滅偪陽〔襄公十年〕
馬循龍
同考試官教諭余　批〔敍桓文善兵書法善將詞〕
簡而意盡可佳可佳
考試官教諭俞　批〔暢達之文結意正大〕
考試官教諭孫　批〔詞格嚴正得春秋體〕
春秋之所均予有用兵得其道者有主將得其
道者此見桓文之善用兵而書甇之善主將也
春秋均予之而失道者可以愧矣自易有師貞
===
之訓則知惟謀乃臧者用兵之善經也吾於桓
文得之方楚之始而伐鄭繼而圍宋也敵勢亦
孔張矣使無謀者處之其何以制勝乎乃桓也
結江黃爲犄角而義聲赫奕於陘亭文也攜曹
衞之黨援而兵威振疊於四國其猷壯其慮周
誠有凜乎其不可犯者楚人安所用其強乎卒
之屈完納款子玉喪氣而鄭宋之不俘於江南
者桓文力也偉哉二霸之績乎彼救江之處父
失之固宜其無功也已自易有長子之命則知
punctuated:
午，遂滅偪陽。〔襄公十年〕
馬循龍
同考試官教諭余　批：〔敍桓、文善兵，書、甇善將，詞〕簡而意盡，可佳，可佳。
考試官教諭俞　批：〔暢達之文，結意正大。〕
考試官教諭孫　批：〔詞格嚴正，得《春秋》體。〕
《春秋》之所均予，有用兵得其道者，有主將得其道者，此見桓、文之善用兵，而書、甇之善主將也。《春秋》均予之，而失道者可以愧矣。自《易》有師貞之訓，則知惟謀乃臧者，用兵之善經也，吾於桓、文得之。方楚之始而伐鄭，繼而圍宋也，敵勢亦孔張矣。使無謀者處之，其何以制勝乎？乃桓也，結江、黃爲犄角，而義聲赫奕於陘亭；文也，攜曹、衞之黨援，而兵威振疊於四國。其猷壯，其慮周，誠有凜乎其不可犯者，楚人安所用其強乎？卒之屈完納款，子玉喪氣，而鄭、宋之不俘於江南者，桓、文力也。偉哉，二霸之績乎！彼救江之處父失之，固宜其無功也已。自《易》有長子之命，則知
translation_en:

Ma Xunlong

Associate Examiner and Instructor Yu comments: [In narrating how Dukes Huan and Wen excelled at deploying troops and how Luan Shu and Zhi Ying (written 書法/書甇 in the transcription) excelled as commanding generals, the wording] is concise while the meaning is fully expressed. Praiseworthy, praiseworthy!
Examiner and Instructor Yu comments: [A fluent and clear essay, with an upright and grand concluding thought.]
Examiner and Instructor Sun comments: [The diction and style are strict and proper, capturing the manner of the Spring and Autumn Annals.]

What the Spring and Autumn Annals equally commends includes those who grasped the proper way of employing troops and those who grasped the proper way of acting as a commanding general. From this we see how Dukes Huan and Wen excelled at employing troops, and how Luan Shu and Zhi Ying excelled as commanding generals. The Spring and Autumn Annals equally commends them, so that those who lost the proper way may feel ashamed.

Since the Book of Changes contains the precept of "correctness in the army" (shi zhen), we know that "only through planning is there success" is the sound norm for employing troops; I find this exemplified in Dukes Huan and Wen. Just when Chu first attacked Zheng and subsequently besieged Song, the enemy's momentum was rampant indeed. Had someone without strategic planning dealt with it, how could he have secured victory? Yet Duke Huan allied with Jiang and Huang as mutual supports, and his reputation for righteousness shone brightly at Xingting; Duke Wen broke up the partisan aid of Cao and Wei, and his military might struck awe and terror across the four states. Their plans were bold and their foresight comprehensive; truly there was about them an awe-inspiring quality that could not be violated—how then could the men of Chu make use of their strength? In the end, Qu Wan offered submission, Ziyu lost heart, and that Zheng and Song were not taken captive south of the Yangtze was through the effort of Dukes Huan and Wen. Magnificent indeed were the achievements of the two霸 (hegemons)! That Yang Chufu, in going to rescue Jiang, lost this way—surely it was fitting that he achieved nothing.

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
惟斷乃成者主將之微權也吾於書罃得之當
書之救鄭罃之滅偪陽也謀夫亦孔多矣使無
斷者處之其何以底績乎乃書則遷戮是戒而
不徇夫八人之請罃則必克是令而不奪於二
卿之疑其命專其權一誠有屹乎其不可動者
三軍敢不用其命乎卒之桑隧全師武宮獻捷
而進退之不辱乎君命者書罃能也美哉二子
之功乎彼于邲之林父失之固宜其不免也已
吁此義行而後之將將兵者其知所法乎雖
然召陵美矣知非王命何城濮克矣知用詭道
何欒書完師而親匠氏之惡知罃取勝而蹈通
吳之踈故曰桓文之節制不足以敵湯武之仁
義而書罃之權詐豈文武吉甫其匹乎君子於
是取節焉可也
禮記
動則左史書之言則右史書之
馬鍾粹
同考試官教諭王　批〔此題全重天子　自防之禮而〕
punctuated:
惟斷乃成者，主將之微權也，吾於書、罃得之。當書之救鄭、罃之滅偪陽也，謀夫亦孔多矣。使無斷者處之，其何以底績乎？乃書則遷戮是戒，而不徇夫八人之請；罃則必克是令，而不奪於二卿之疑。其命專，其權一，誠有屹乎其不可動者，三軍敢不用其命乎？卒之桑隧全師，武宮獻捷，而進退之不辱乎君命者，書、罃能也。美哉二子之功乎！彼于邲之林父失之，固宜其不免也已。吁！此義行，而後之將將兵者，其知所法乎？雖然，召陵美矣，知非王命何？城濮克矣，知用詭道何？欒書完師，而親匠氏之惡；知罃取勝，而蹈通吳之踈。故曰：「桓、文之節制，不足以敵湯、武之仁義。」而書、罃之權詐，豈文武吉甫其匹乎？君子於是取節焉可也。

禮記
動則左史書之，言則右史書之。
馬鍾粹
同考試官教諭王　批〔此題全重天子　自防之禮，而〕
translation_en:
…that only through decisiveness is success achieved is the subtle authority of the commander-in-chief; I find this realized in Luan Shu 欒書 and Zhi Ying 知罃. When Shu went to rescue Zheng and Ying went to extinguish Biyang, the counselors were indeed numerous! Had someone lacking decisiveness been in their place, how could they have brought about results? Yet Shu warned of banishment and execution, refusing to yield to the requests of the eight sub-commanders; Ying issued an order that they must conquer, refusing to be swayed by the doubts of the two ministers. Their command was undivided and their authority unified; truly they stood firm like mountains that could not be moved—how would the Three Armies dare not obey their orders? In the end, at Sangsui the army was preserved intact, and at the Temple of Wu the victory was presented; that in advancing and retreating they did not disgrace their lord's commission was due to the ability of Shu and Ying. Admirable indeed were the achievements of these two masters! As for Xun Linfu 荀林父 at Bi, he failed in this, so it was only fitting that he could not escape defeat. Alas! When this principle is put into practice, will those in later times who command generals and lead troops not know what to take as their model? Even so, the campaign at Shaoling was admirable, yet what of the fact that it was not by the King's command? The battle at Chengpu was a victory, yet what of its use of deceptive ways? Luan Shu kept his army intact, yet personally committed the crime at the artisan Li's residence; Zhi Ying won victory, yet fell into the carelessness of opening relations with Wu. Therefore it is said: "The disciplined control of Huan and Wen is no match for the benevolence and righteousness of Tang and Wu." And how could the expedient artifice of Shu and Ying make them peers of Yin Jifu 尹吉甫, who was both civil and martial? For the gentleman to approve of their merits in particular instances is sufficient.

Record of Rites (Liji)
"When he acts, the Left Scribe records it; when he speaks, the Right Scribe records it."
By Ma Zhongcui 馬鍾粹

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
作者類多忽此獨子體認眞切指詞簡古可以式矣
考試官教諭俞　批　爾雅之作
考試官教諭孫　批　理明詞典
備史職以紀言動天子之自防亦周矣蓋君身
貴立於無過也一言動而史得書之自防之禮
其嚴乎玉藻記此蓋曰君身敬肆之間天下治
忽之幾也使夾輔之無其人鮮有不疚者矣於
是有自防之禮焉彼天子將納民于軌物不動
而敬其道也使防之少懈能必其無過動乎故
===
惟無動而動則左史書之蓋左史以記事爲職
動有臧否彼皆得直其文以爲王詔曾不敢以
近臣之故而周其私無虛美焉無隱惡焉是措
諸躬行者將布之史冊也君雖欲忽於動而有
史在左寧不惕然其有警乎天子將樹民之風
聲不言而信其道也使防之少踈能必其無過
言乎故惟無言而言則右史書之蓋右史以記
言爲職言有善否彼皆得正其詞以爲王箴亦
不敢以近臣之故而易其法觀省備焉鑒戒昭
punctuated:
作者類多忽此。獨子體認眞切，指詞簡古，可以式矣。
考試官教諭俞批：爾雅之作。
考試官教諭孫批：理明詞典。
備史職以紀言動，天子之自防亦周矣。蓋君身貴立於無過也，一言動而史得書之，自防之禮，其嚴乎！《玉藻》記此，蓋曰：君身敬肆之間，天下治忽之幾也。使夾輔之無其人，鮮有不疚者矣，於是有自防之禮焉。彼天子將納民于軌物，不動而敬，其道也。使防之少懈，能必其無過動乎？故惟無動，而動則左史書之。蓋左史以記事爲職，動有臧否，彼皆得直其文以爲王詔，曾不敢以近臣之故而周其私。無虛美焉，無隱惡焉，是措諸躬行者，將布之史冊也。君雖欲忽於動，而有史在左，寧不惕然其有警乎！天子將樹民之風聲，不言而信，其道也。使防之少踈，能必其無過言乎？故惟無言，而言則右史書之。蓋右史以記言爲職，言有善否，彼皆得正其詞以爲王箴，亦不敢以近臣之故而易其法。觀省備焉，鑒戒昭
translation_en:
…writers generally tend to overlook this. You alone have grasped it with genuine insight; your exposition and diction are concise and antique, worthy to serve as a model.
Examiner and Instructor Yu's comment: A work of classical elegance.
Examiner and Instructor Sun's comment: The reasoning is clear and the diction is canonical.
By establishing the offices of the Scribes to record words and actions, the Son of Heaven's self-restraint was indeed comprehensive! For it is vital that the sovereign's person stand free of transgression; when every single word or action may be written down by the Scribes, how strict is the ritual of self-restraint! In recording this, the "Jade-Bead Pendants" (Yuzao) chapter of the Record of Rites is saying: Between reverence and laxity in the sovereign's person lies the pivotal juncture of order and neglect for all under Heaven. Were there no men at his side to assist him, rarely would he be free from fault; therefore, there exists the ritual of self-restraint. Now, the Son of Heaven seeks to guide the people into regular norms and standards; to command reverence without acting is his Way. Yet if his guard is relaxed even slightly, can one be certain that he will have no errant actions? Therefore, unless he does not act at all, whenever he acts, the Scribe of the Left records it. For the Scribe of the Left has the recording of affairs as his duty. Whether an action is good or bad, he is able to write down the account straightforwardly to serve as instruction for the king, never daring on account of being an intimate minister to cover up for his personal partialities. With no empty praise and no concealed wrongdoing, what is put into personal practice will be spread across the pages of history. Even if the ruler wished to be careless in his actions, with the Scribe at his left, how could he not befilled with vigilance and alarm! The Son of Heaven seeks to establish moral influence and reputation among the people; to inspire trust without speaking is his Way. Yet if his guard is negligent even slightly, can one be certain that he will have no errant words? Therefore, unless he does not speak at all, whenever he speaks, the Scribe of the Right records it. For the Scribe of the Right has the recording of words as his duty. Whether a word is admirable or not, he is able to set forth the phrasing uprightly to serve as admonition for the king, likewise never daring on account of being an intimate minister to alter his standards. With observation and reflection thus made complete, and the mirror of warning made bright…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
馬是著之話言者將垂之載籍也君雖欲忽於
言而有史在右寧不懍然其有畏乎如是則左
右交儆無一人非師資也言動交脩無一念非
敬德也此天子之所以動不過則言不過辭得
之豫養者深也自防之禮可少乎哉大抵人情
喜逸豫而不樂拘檢而況地有可肆欲爲易攻
古之帝王知其然故以禮自防禁於未發而交
儆之助則又隨寓而存如工誦御規士傳民語
之類皆是不特左右史而已今其禮具載周典
===
舉而行之存乎其人
致樂以治心則易直子諒之心油然生矣
易直子諒之心生則樂樂則安安則久
人則天天則神天則不言而信神則不
怒而威致樂以治心者也
高第
同考試官教諭王　批　題長而氣脉聯絡作者爲難
此篇詞意清新而主張布置出於常格殆深於樂者
考試官教諭俞　批　詞理通暢
punctuated:
馬。是著之話言者，將垂之載籍也。君雖欲忽於言，而有史在右，寧不懍然其有畏乎？如是，則左右交儆，無一人非師資也；言動交脩，無一念非敬德也。此天子之所以動不過則、言不過辭，得之豫養者深也，自防之禮可少乎哉？大抵人情喜逸豫而不樂拘檢，而況地有可肆，欲爲易攻。古之帝王知其然，故以禮自防，禁於未發，而交儆之助，則又隨寓而存，如工誦、御規、士傳、民語之類皆是，不特左右史而已。今其禮具載《周典》，舉而行之，存乎其人。

致樂以治心，則易直子諒之心油然生矣。易直子諒之心生則樂，樂則安，安則久，人則天，天則神。天則不言而信，神則不怒而威，致樂以治心者也。
高第
同考試官教諭王　批：題長而氣脉聯絡，作者爲難。此篇詞意清新，而主張布置出於常格，殆深於樂者。
考試官教諭俞　批：詞理通暢。
translation_en:
… there [reading 馬 as 焉]. Thus, what is set forth in his spoken words will be handed down in the written records. Even if the ruler wished to be careless in his speech, with the Scribe at his right, how could he not be filled with awe and dread? When it is like this, those on his left and right admonish him in turn, so there is not a single person who is not a teacher and resource; his words and actions are cultivated together, so there is not a single thought that is not reverent virtue. This is why the Son of Heaven acts without transgressing the rules and speaks without exceeding proper expression, having gained deeply from prior cultivation. How could the rites of self-restraint be dispensed with? In general, human nature delights in ease and comfort and dislikes restraint and scrutiny—all the more so when one's position allows for indulgence and desires easily assail one. The emperors and kings of antiquity knew this was so; therefore, they restrained themselves with rites, checking impulses before they arose, while the aid of mutual admonition was present wherever they turned—such as blind musicians reciting verses, attendants offering remonstrances, officers transmitting messages, and commoners conversing—not merely the Scribes of the Left and Right alone. Today, these rites are fully recorded in the Canons of Zhou (Zhoudian); taking them up and putting them into practice depends upon the person.

"When one masters music to regulate the mind, then an easy, honest, loving, and sincere heart effortlessly arises. When an easy, honest, loving, and sincere heart arises, there is joy; with joy comes peace; with peace comes long duration; with long duration [reading 人 as 久] comes heavenliness; with heavenliness comes spirituality. Like Heaven, to be trusted without speaking; like a spirit, to be awe-inspiring without anger—this comes from mastering music to regulate the mind."

Gao Di 高第
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Wang comments: The topic is long, making it difficult for the writer to keep the vital thread connected. This essay is fresh in its wording and thought, and its thesis and structure rise above the ordinary mold; he is surely one who has a deep understanding of music.
Examiner and County Director of Studies Yu comments: The expression and reasoning are fluent and clear.

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭孫　批〔是知樂之情者錄之〕
觀致樂養心之妙而樂之切于人益明矣蓋樂
由心生者也致此以治心而自得之妙豈容已
乎樂記之言曰樂也者非他也人心之和也先
王本人心之和以作樂即亦由太和之理以養
心是故其爲教至切也君子欲治其心其必由
樂乎誠能窮性術之變以爲脩內之資察聲氣
之元以致養心之實則吾心之眞機一觸而吾
心之眞樂自融由是和順於道德而衆善萃焉
===
爲易爲直爲慈爲良機之有感而遂通者莫不
油然生矣生則惡可已乎由是交暢於性情而
衆妙臻焉以安以久以天以神理之相生而無
窮者皆將渾然化矣化則惡可測乎惟天則至
誠妙於不息天下之大信也不必假言而後彰
焉惟神則篤恭妙於不顯天下之德威也不必
假怒而後震焉夫治心之妙一至於此非致樂
其能然哉蓋樂由中出而衆善之自生固樂之
所以導其和也心與樂孚而衆妙之自致固心
punctuated:
考試官教諭孫批：〔是知樂之情者，錄之。〕

觀致樂養心之妙，而樂之切于人益明矣。蓋樂由心生者也，致此以治心，而自得之妙，豈容已乎？《樂記》之言曰：樂也者，非他也，人心之和也。先王本人心之和以作樂，即亦由太和之理以養心，是故其爲教至切也。君子欲治其心，其必由樂乎！誠能窮性術之變，以爲脩內之資；察聲氣之元，以致養心之實。則吾心之眞機一觸，而吾心之眞樂自融。由是和順於道德而衆善萃焉，爲易、爲直、爲慈、爲良，機之有感而遂通者，莫不油然生矣。生則惡可已乎？由是交暢於性情而衆妙臻焉，以安、以久、以天、以神，理之相生而無窮者，皆將渾然化矣。化則惡可測乎？惟天則至誠妙於不息，天下之大信也，不必假言而後彰焉；惟神則篤恭妙於不顯，天下之德威也，不必假怒而後震焉。夫治心之妙一至於此，非致樂其能然哉？蓋樂由中出，而衆善之自生，固樂之所以導其和也；心與樂孚，而衆妙之自致，固心…
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Sun 孫 comments: [This is one who understands the true nature of music; record it for publication.]

Observing the subtle wonder of delving deeply into music to nourish the mind, it becomes all the clearer how vital music is to human beings. For music is born from the mind; when one delves deeply into it to regulate the mind, how could the subtle wonder of self-realization ever cease? As the Record of Music (Yueji 樂記) states: what is called music is nothing other than the harmony of the human mind. The former kings based their creation of music on the harmony of the human mind, and likewise drew upon the principle of Supreme Harmony to nourish the mind; therefore, its teaching is most vital. If the gentleman wishes to regulate his mind, must it not be through music! If he can truly fathom the transformations of human nature and its ways as a resource for cultivating the inner self, and examine the primal origins of sound and vital breath to achieve the reality of nourishing the mind, then once the true spring of our mind is touched, the true joy of our mind naturally blends in harmony. From this, one becomes harmonious and compliant with the Way and its Virtue, and all goodness gathers therein: becoming easy, forthright, compassionate, and benign—those springs that are stirred and immediately penetrate all sprout forth abundantly. Once sprouted, how can they be stopped? From this, they flow freely through one's nature and emotions, and all subtle wonders are attained: becoming tranquil, enduring, heaven-like, and spirit-like—the principles that generate one another endlessly will all be indistinguishably transformed. Once transformed, how can they be fathomed? Only through being heaven-like is utmost sincerity wondrous in its ceaselessness; this is the great trustworthiness of the world, which has no need to rely on words to become manifest. Only through being spirit-like is steadfast reverence wondrous in its imperceptibility; this is the virtuous awe of the world, which has no need to rely on anger to shake all things. That the subtle wonder of regulating the mind reaches such a height—could it be so without delving deeply into music? For music issues from within, and the spontaneous birth of all goodness is indeed how music guides its harmony; the mind and music are in mutual accord, and the spontaneous attainment of all subtle wonders is indeed how the mind…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
之所以通其極也故曰致樂以治心觀此則知
樂之不可斯須去矣抑心與樂非有二也而治
心者亦非取諸樂以助之也蓋太和流行於宇
宙具之人則爲心宣之聲容則爲樂故樂之感
人也微而君子樂得其道蓋至於天且神焉而
心體未甞益也大哉樂乎昔舜命胄教而以典
樂盡之要其歸於和神人治心之道備矣
第貳場
論
===
孟軻述唐虞三代之德
曾曰唯
同考試官教諭朱　批〔得孟子重自任意議論層出〕
〔中多感慨非博雅不能也錄之可以服多士矣〕
同考試官教諭林　批〔體裁高古色象渾涵蓋自命〕
〔意處超然有精詣豈獨工於文哉吾爲子斂衽矣〕
考試官教諭俞　批〔意高語新敬服敬服〕
考試官教諭孫　批〔辯博渾成是一手筆〕
聖賢思以道易天下故不敢以天下易其道何
punctuated:
之所以通其極也。故曰：「致樂以治心。」觀此，則知樂之不可斯須去矣。抑心與樂非有二也，而治心者亦非取諸樂以助之也。蓋太和流行於宇宙，具之人則爲心，宣之聲容則爲樂。故樂之感人也微，而君子樂得其道，蓋至於天且神焉，而心體未甞益也。大哉樂乎！昔舜命胄教，而以典樂盡之，要其歸於和神人，治心之道備矣。

第貳場
論
孟軻述唐虞三代之德
曾曰唯
同考試官教諭朱　批〔得孟子重自任意，議論層出，中多感慨，非博雅不能也。錄之可以服多士矣。〕
同考試官教諭林　批〔體裁高古，色象渾涵，蓋自命意處超然有精詣，豈獨工於文哉！吾爲子斂衽矣。〕
考試官教諭俞　批〔意高語新，敬服敬服。〕
考試官教諭孫　批〔辯博渾成，是一手筆。〕

聖賢思以道易天下，故不敢以天下易其道。何
translation_en:
…by which it penetrates to the ultimate. Therefore it is said: "Master music in order to govern the mind." Observing this, one knows that music cannot be set aside even for a moment. Yet the mind and music are not two separate things, nor does one who governs the mind merely draw upon music as an external aid. Rather, Supreme Harmony flows throughout the universe: endowed in human beings, it is the mind; expressed in sound and movement, it is music. Thus the way music moves people is subtle, and when the gentleman rejoices in attaining its Way, even when he reaches the level of the heavenly and the numinous, the substance of his mind has had nothing added to it. Great indeed is music! In antiquity, when Shun commanded the education of the noble youth, he encompassed it entirely within the charge of directing music, summing up its ultimate aim as harmonizing spirits and human beings—thus the Way of governing the mind was made complete.

Second Session
Discourse
"Meng Ke recounted the virtue of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties"
Zeng Yuewei
Associate Examiner Instructor Zhu comments: [He captures Mencius's intent in taking this heavy responsibility upon himself. Arguments emerge layer upon layer, filled with deep emotion inside; none but a scholar of broad learning and refinement could achieve this. Printing it will win the admiration of the multitude of scholars.]
Associate Examiner Instructor Lin comments: [The style is lofty and antique, its tone and imagery渾涵 (all-encompassing and profound). From the very conception of its ideas, it transcends the ordinary and reaches subtle perfection—how could this merely be skill in writing! I adjust my robes in respect for you.]
Examiner Instructor Yu comments: [Lofty in conception and fresh in phrasing—deeply admirable, deeply admirable.]
Examiner Instructor Sun comments: [Eloquent, broad, and seamlessly integrated—truly the work of a master hand.]

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
也道不可易也道不可易而後可與易天下也
蓋道原於天而備於人天下之人與聖賢同今
之人與古之人同焉者也夫是以不可易也乃
人之不聖賢也今之不古也則非有道者莫與
易之使欲易其道以徇天下而求易是以今治
今以衆人傳衆人猶之投膏止燎揚湯止沸也
無益明矣卒之天下不可易而道已先爲天下
裂豈蓋天下之過與故聖賢無一日不欲用其
道於天下而天下之用與否不可必吾道在焉
===
不與世爲汙隆不因人爲枉直非過自高也重
道所以重天下也然則孟軻氏身處戰國而述
唐虞三代之德豈無意乎詩云天生烝民有物
有則民之秉彝好是懿德是德之在人天畀之
也天畀之則恒性惟均非有餘於聖賢而不足
於衆庶者也非仁義於唐虞三代而功利於春
秋戰國者也顧豈有時而可易乎乃風會下趨
人心不古知德者鮮悖德者多而聖賢者則固
守唐虞三代之德而有易天下之具焉其具在
punctuated: 也？道不可易也，道不可易而後可與易天下也。蓋道原於天而備於人，天下之人與聖賢同，今之人與古之人同焉者也，夫是以不可易也。乃人之不聖賢也，今之不古也，則非有道者莫與易之。使欲易其道以徇天下而求易，是以今治今、以衆人傳衆人，猶之投膏止燎、揚湯止沸也，無益明矣！卒之天下不可易，而道已先爲天下裂，豈蓋天下之過與？故聖賢無一日不欲用其道於天下，而天下之用與否不可必。吾道在焉，不與世爲汙隆，不因人爲枉直，非過自高也，重道所以重天下也。然則孟軻氏身處戰國而述唐虞三代之德，豈無意乎？《詩》云：「天生烝民，有物有則。民之秉彝，好是懿德。」是德之在人，天畀之也。天畀之，則恒性惟均，非有餘於聖賢而不足於衆庶者也，非仁義於唐虞三代而功利於春秋戰國者也，顧豈有時而可易乎？乃風會下趨，人心不古，知德者鮮，悖德者多，而聖賢者則固守唐虞三代之德，而有易天下之具焉。其具在
translation_en: … is that? It is because the Way cannot be altered; only when the Way cannot be altered can one thereby transform the world. For the Way originates in Heaven and is complete in man; the people of the world are the same as the sages and worthies, and the people of today are the same as the people of antiquity—that is why it cannot be altered. Yet when people fail to be sages and worthies, and the present fails to be like antiquity, then none without the Way can transform them. Suppose one wished to alter one's Way to accommodate the world and thereby seek to transform it: this would be governing the present with the present, and instructing the multitude by means of the multitude—like pouring grease to extinguish a fire or scooping up boiling water to stop it from boiling. That it is useless is obvious! In the end, the world cannot be transformed, while the Way has already first been torn apart by the world. Could this be entirely [?] the fault of the world? Therefore, there is not a single day when sages and worthies do not wish to put their Way to use in the world, yet whether the world uses it or not cannot be guaranteed. As long as our Way is present, it does not sink or rise with the age, nor does it bend or straighten on account of others. This is not holding oneself excessively high; prizing the Way is the means by which to prize the world. This being so, when Meng Ke 孟軻 [Mencius] lived in the Warring States period and yet recounted the virtue of Tang 唐 [Yao 堯], Yu 虞 [Shun 舜], and the Three Dynasties, could it have been without purpose? The Book of Odes (Shi 詩) says: "Heaven gave birth to the multitude of people; where there is a thing, there is a norm. In the constant nature that the people hold fast, they love this admirable virtue." This means that the presence of virtue in man is bestowed by Heaven. Since Heaven bestows it, this constant nature is uniform in all: it is not abundant in sages and worthies while deficient in the common multitude, nor was it benevolence and righteousness in the eras of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties while being utility and profit in the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods. How, then, could there ever be a time when it might be altered? Yet as the customs and ethos of the age declined and human minds were no longer like those of antiquity, few understood virtue and many violated it; the sages and worthies, however, held fast to the virtue of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, and possessed the wherewithal to transform the world. Since that wherewithal resides in …

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
我而世不唐虞三代則其心曾未能以一日安
是故孔子不能不春秋也而轍環列國思以唐
虞三代之德易之耳孟子顚學孔子亦不能不
戰國也而傳食諸侯思以唐虞三代之德易之
耳是孟子之心孔子之心也孔子之心唐虞三
代之心也夫唐虞三代何心也曰民饑我饑之
也民寒我寒之也民溺我溺之也民罪我陷之
也匹夫不獲予辜也一人衡行予恥也數聖人
之視天下無一非我則其自視無一非天下所
===
以爲悅安强教者無不至焉故其時卒無饑寒
無陷溺無不獲無衡行者以有是心而位又足
以行其德也孟氏明數聖人之德於戰國而無
其位其視饑寒於攻伐者甚矣而不能爲之衣
食陷溺於水火者甚矣而不能爲之極援衡行
於天下不獲於溝中者滔滔是矣而不能爲之
廓清保息勢旣有所不能致而其心又不敢以
自已其言曰天欲平治天下當今之世舍我其
誰誠知其道在我責固不容辭也嗟乎孟氏之
punctuated: 我，而世不唐、虞、三代，則其心曾未能以一日安。是故孔子不能不春秋也，而轍環列國，思以唐、虞、三代之德易之耳；孟子顚學孔子，亦不能不戰國也，而傳食諸侯，思以唐、虞、三代之德易之耳。是孟子之心，孔子之心也；孔子之心，唐、虞、三代之心也。夫唐、虞、三代何心也？曰：「民饑，我饑之也；民寒，我寒之也；民溺，我溺之也；民罪，我陷之也。匹夫不獲，予辜也；一人衡行，予恥也。」數聖人之視天下，無一非我；則其自視，無一非天下。所以爲悅安强教者，無不至焉。故其時卒無饑寒、無陷溺、無不獲、無衡行者，以有是心，而位又足以行其德也。孟氏明數聖人之德於戰國，而無其位。其視饑寒於攻伐者甚矣，而不能爲之衣食；陷溺於水火者甚矣，而不能爲之極援；衡行於天下、不獲於溝中者滔滔是矣，而不能爲之廓清保息。勢旣有所不能致，而其心又不敢以自已。其言曰：「天欲平治天下，當今之世，舍我其誰？」誠知其道在我，責固不容辭也。嗟乎！孟氏之
translation_en: … in oneself, yet if the world is not like that of Tang [Yao], Yu [Shun], and the Three Dynasties, then their minds could never rest at ease for a single day. For this reason, Confucius could not avoid living in the Spring and Autumn period, yet his carriage tracks circled the various states, wishing only to transform them with the virtue of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties. Mencius, whose wish [reading 願 for 顚?] was to learn from Confucius, likewise could not avoid living in the Warring States period, yet he traveled from one feudal lord to another receiving their support, wishing only to transform them with the virtue of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties. Thus the mind of Mencius was the mind of Confucius, and the mind of Confucius was the mind of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties. And what was the mind of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties? They said: "If the people are hungry, it is I who have starved them; if the people are cold, it is I who have left them cold; if the people are drowning, it is I who have drowned them; if the people fall into crime, it is I who have entrapped them. If a single common man fails to find his place, it is my guilt; if a single person runs rampant across the land, it is my shame." When those several sages looked upon the world, there was nothing in it that they did not regard as part of themselves; and when they looked upon themselves, there was nothing in them that did not belong to the world. Thus, in bringing pleasure, security, and vigorous instruction to the people, there was nothing they did not carry to the utmost. Therefore, in their times there were ultimately none who suffered hunger or cold, none who were entrapped or drowned, none who failed to find their place, and none who ran rampant—because they possessed this mind, and their stations were moreover sufficient to put their virtue into practice. Mencius elucidated the virtue of those several sages during the Warring States period, yet he lacked their station. He saw all too clearly those who suffered hunger and cold amid military campaigns and attacks, yet he could not clothe and feed them; he saw all too clearly those who were entrapped and drowning in flood and fire, yet he could not rescue them [reading 拯 for 極?]; those running rampant across the world and those failing to find their place and perishing in ditches were everywhere like a rushing flood, yet he could not sweep the realm clean and nurture them back to rest. Since his circumstances did not allow him to bring this about, and yet his mind dared not cease on its own, he said: "If Heaven wishes to bring peace and order to the world, in the present age, who is there besides me?" Truly, he knew that since the Way was in him, the responsibility was one he could not decline. Alas! Was not Mencius's …

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
心不可識乎是故不忍捄其道以自賢亦不能
貶其道以自售齊梁滕魯不必皆賢也執起儀
衍之徒不必皆豪傑也富國强兵弗敢荅也合
從連衡弗敢聞也知有唐虞三代之德而已矣
是德也幼而學之壯而欲行之行之不得以自
致則惓惓焉述之以告人庶幾有聞而行之者
功利不足以勝仁義而戰國猶可挽而爲三代
進而爲唐虞也孔子奚取於桓文以其猶有尊
周之名也仁義充塞之時得仁義之似者而可
===
也安知戰國無桓文乎又安知其止於似而已
乎茲其望天下甚仁而自任甚重是故舉天下
之少者而庠序之舉天下之壯者而孝弟忠信
之舉天下之老者而肉帛之舉天下之望雲霓
者而時雨之舉天下之疾首蹙額者而歡樂之
則天下定於一而周益尊蓋孟氏之心也非用
唐虞三代之德不可也乃地醜德齊者狃於富
强則見以爲迂緩而不急放恣橫議者馳於從
衡則見以爲闊略而無當茲所謂急小喜而忘
punctuated: 心，不可識乎？是故不忍捄其道以自賢，亦不能貶其道以自售。齊、梁、滕、魯，不必皆賢也；執、起、儀、衍之徒，不必皆豪傑也。富國强兵，弗敢荅也；合從連衡，弗敢聞也；知有唐、虞、三代之德而已矣。是德也，幼而學之，壯而欲行之。行之不得以自致，則惓惓焉述之以告人，庶幾有聞而行之者。功利不足以勝仁義，而戰國猶可挽而爲三代，進而爲唐、虞也。孔子奚取於桓、文？以其猶有尊周之名也。仁義充塞之時，得仁義之似者而可也。安知戰國無桓、文乎？又安知其止於似而已乎？茲其望天下甚仁，而自任甚重。是故舉天下之少者而庠序之，舉天下之壯者而孝弟忠信之，舉天下之老者而肉帛之，舉天下之望雲霓者而時雨之，舉天下之疾首蹙額者而歡樂之，則天下定於一而周益尊，蓋孟氏之心也，非用唐、虞、三代之德不可也。乃地醜德齊者狃於富强，則見以爲迂緩而不急；放恣橫議者馳於從衡，則見以爲闊略而無當。茲所謂急小喜而忘
translation_en: …heart—can it not be understood? For this reason, he could neither bear to withhold [?] his Way in order to consider himself superior, nor could he debase his Way in order to peddle himself. The rulers of Qi, Liang, Teng, and Lu were not necessarily all worthy; men of the ilk of Shen Buhai [?] (Zhi [?]), Wu Qi, Zhang Yi, and Zou Yan were not necessarily all heroes. Of enriching the state and strengthening the army, he dared not speak in reply; of vertical and horizontal alliances, he dared not hear; he knew only the virtue of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties. This virtue is what one studies in youth and desires to practice in maturity. When in trying to practice it he could not bring it about himself, he earnestly expounded it to inform others, hoping that there might be someone who would hear it and put it into practice—so that utilitarian gain would not suffice to overcome benevolence and righteousness, and the Warring States might still be drawn back to become the Three Dynasties, and advance to become Tang and Yu. What did Confucius find to approve in Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin? It was because they still upheld the nominal cause of honoring the Zhou. In an age when benevolence and righteousness are blocked up, even finding what merely resembles benevolence and righteousness is acceptable. How could one know that there would be no Duke Huan or Duke Wen in the Warring States? And how could one know that they would stop merely at resemblance? Thus his hope for the world was most benevolent, and the burden he took upon himself was most heavy. Therefore, to take all the young of the world and educate them in schools; to take all the able-bodied of the world and instruct them in filial piety, brotherly respect, loyalty, and trustworthiness; to take all the aged of the world and provide them with meat and silk; to take all in the world who long for clouds and rainbows and give them timely rain; to take all in the world who have aching heads and knitted brows and bring them joy—so that the world would be settled in unity and the Zhou would be ever more honored: this was indeed the heart of Mencius, and it could not be done without employing the virtue of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties. Yet rulers of equal territory and matching virtue were habituated to wealth and power, and so regarded his Way as迂回 (indirect), slow, and not urgent; unbridled and perverse disputants raced after vertical and horizontal alliances, and so regarded it as broad, sketchy, and impractical. This is what is meant by being eager for petty pleasures while forgetting…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
大憂餌近功而貽遠患適足以塗炭其民而肘
足人國也豈知孟氏所述爲萬世不易之道乎
夫大匠不以拙工廢繩墨羿不以拙射變彀率
是不易於所不能也師曠不以晉平好新聲而
棄其五音之節王子期不以趙襄好易馬而改
其六御之法是不易於所不尚也戰國之人所
尚在彼所不能在此而孟氏終不能舍所學以
從之而猶日述其所不欲聞而止其所必不可
已豈爲是不近人情哉誠冀夫太陽之明無爝
===
火洪鐘之響無擊缶道其常耳而合不合則人
也遇不遇則天也寧枘鑿不相入而唐虞三代
之德不可使少貶焉如以爲合之難而委曲以
幸一遇而結果其說以就之則出乎仁義功利
之而已矣功利而可爲也鞅起儀衍之徒不少
矣安在孟氏以戰國而易戰國哉又何以異於
勸燕伐燕助粤攻粤哉故進而不遇於七國仁
義暫蝕於一時退而作孟子七篇仁義大明於
萬世使萬世之下較然别邪正之塗晰王霸之
punctuated: 大憂，餌近功而貽遠患，適足以塗炭其民而肘足人國也，豈知孟氏所述爲萬世不易之道乎？夫大匠不以拙工廢繩墨，羿不以拙射變彀率，是不易於所不能也；師曠不以晉平好新聲而棄其五音之節，王子期不以趙襄好易馬而改其六御之法，是不易於所不尚也。戰國之人，所尚在彼，所不能在此，而孟氏終不能舍所學以從之，而猶日述其所不欲聞，而止其所必不可已，豈爲是不近人情哉？誠冀夫太陽之明無爝火，洪鐘之響無擊缶，道其常耳。而合不合則人也，遇不遇則天也。寧枘鑿不相入，而唐虞三代之德不可使少貶焉。如以爲合之難，而委曲以幸一遇，而結果其說以就之，則出乎仁義，功利之而已矣。功利而可爲也，鞅、起、儀、衍之徒不少矣，安在孟氏以戰國而易戰國哉？又何以異於勸燕伐燕、助粤攻粤哉？故進而不遇於七國，仁義暫蝕於一時；退而作《孟子》七篇，仁義大明於萬世。使萬世之下，較然别邪正之塗，晰王霸之
translation_en: …great anxieties, taking the bait of immediate success while leaving behind distant calamities—which only sufficed to plunge their people into mire and ashes and bind the elbows and feet of their states! How could they know that what Mencius recounted was the unchanging Way for ten thousand generations? Now, a master carpenter does not discard his ink-line on account of clumsy workmen, nor did Yi alter his standard for drawing the bow on account of clumsy archers; this is not changing because of what others are unable to do. Music Master Kuang did not abandon the rhythms of his five tones because Duke Ping of Jinwas fond of new music, nor did Wang Ziqi alter his six methods of charioteering because Viscount Xiang of Zhao was fond of exchanging horses; this is not changing because of what others do not esteem. What the men of the Warring States esteemed lay there, and what they were unable to do lay here; yet Mencius to the end could not abandon what he had learned in order to follow them, and instead daily recounted what they did not wish to hear and sought to halt what they felt they could by no means stop doing. Why did he act in a way so contrary to ordinary human sentiment? Truly he hoped that beneath the brightness of the great sun there would be no torch-fires, and amid the resonance of a great bell there would be no beating of earthen jars—he was simply stating the constant norm. Whether one's counsel is accepted or not depends on men; whether one meets with a worthy ruler or not depends on Heaven. Better that tenon and mortise fail to fit together than that the virtue of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties be allowed to suffer the slightest diminution. If, considering agreement difficult to achieve, he had bent himself to hope for a chance encounter and tailored [?] his doctrines to accommodate them, then in departing from benevolence and righteousness he would merely have pursued utilitarian profit. And if utilitarian profit were something to be practiced, there were already plenty of men of the ilk of Shang Yang, Wu Qi, Zhang Yi, and公孫衍 (Gongsun Yan)—where would be the sense in Mencius using the ways of the Warring States to transform the Warring States? And how would that have differed from urging Yan to attack Yan, or helping Yue to attack Yue? Therefore, when he advanced and failed to meet with acceptance among the Seven States, benevolence and righteousness were temporarily eclipsed for a single era; when he withdrew and composed the seven books of the Mencius, benevolence and righteousness were made brilliantly clear for ten thousand generations. That for ten thousand generations thereafter men have been able clearly to distinguish the paths of the crooked and the upright, to discern the…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
辨黜功利正人心而知尊君親上之大道者孟
氏之訓在也唐虞三代之遺也史遷敘而傳之
其知孟氏哉雖然似矣三騶同傳而以淳于荀
卿之間遇之淺之乎知孟氏哉
表
擬宋幸國子監令博士李覺講周易泰卦
賜緑段謝表〔端拱元年〕
楊鳳
同考試官教諭張　批〔對揚之辭類多靡靡兹作就〕
===

同考試官學正齊　批〔作表欲句切事要語關君身而〕
〔又應手中倫誦之若出金石如此篇者蓋難矣取之取之〕

端拱元年八月二十六日國子監博士臣
李覺恭遇
車駕幸學命臣進講周易泰卦伏蒙
恩賜緑段者伏以三陽啓泰
punctuated:
辨，黜功利，正人心，而知尊君親上之大道者，孟氏之訓在也，唐虞三代之遺也。史遷敘而傳之，其知孟氏哉？雖然，似矣。三騶同傳，而以淳于、荀卿之間遇之，淺之乎知孟氏哉！

表

擬宋幸國子監，令博士李覺講《周易》泰卦，賜緑段謝表〔端拱元年〕
楊鳳
同考試官教諭張　批〔對揚之辭類多靡靡，兹作就題命意，陳古諷今，是博學而抱忠愛者，高薦之。〕

端拱元年八月二十六日，國子監博士臣李覺，恭遇車駕幸學，命臣進講《周易》泰卦，伏蒙恩賜緑段者。伏以三陽啓泰，
translation_en:
…distinction, reject utilitarianism and profit, rectify the human heart, and understand the great Way of honoring the ruler and loving one's superiors—this is because the teachings of Mencius remain, the legacy of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties. When the Grand Scribe Sima Qian (史遷) narrated and wrote his biography, did he truly know Mencius? Even so, he came close; yet by placing him in the same biography as the three Zous (三騶) and treating him among Chunyu Kun (淳于) and Xun Qing (荀卿), how shallowly did he know Mencius!

Memorial (表)

Imitation of a Memorial of Thanks from the Song Dynasty, on the Occasion of an Imperial Visit to the Directorate of Education (國子監), Ordering Erudite (博士) Li Jue (李覺) to Lecture on the Tai Hexagram of the Book of Changes (Zhouyi 周易), and Bestowing Green Satin upon Him [first year of the Duangong 端拱 era (988)]
By Yang Feng (楊鳳)

He is one of broad learning who cherishes loyalty and affection for his sovereign; I highly recommend it.]
Comment by Associate Examiner and Subdirector of Studies (學正) Qi: [In composing a memorial, one desires phrases that hit the essentials of the matter and words that concern the person of the ruler, while also answering the hand in accord with principle and sounding like bronze and stone when recited. title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
聖人作而文運昌五服有章
天命昭而德施普幸覯
臨雍之典俄分在笥之珍輝映六符懽騰八
裔〔臣〕覺誠惶誠恐稽首頓首上言粤自虞
廷命胄司存四德之和周室尊師禮重三
雍之對緊明倫爲立敎之本而太學延賢
上所關天王問道於澤宮樂正升歌於壁
水樞衣鼓篋萃東西南北之英敬業樂羣
備春夏秋冬之訓譽髦育德思服流聲惟
===
兹懿軌既湮遂爾麻風罕繼詩書閒事虛
敦闕里牲牢更𢀖徒尊祇飾橋門觀聽况
入易稱五經之祖而聖人脩十翼之辭象
爻組織於玄黃奇耦樞機乎造化圖讖古
壁幸秦燼之未殘業侈顓門慨漢箋之互
異丘賀膏肓於讖緯殊忝褒書京房墨守
其家林無裨哀職豈陰陽之未泰致上下
之不交雖勤卜蔡之思竟負拔茅之志事
誠有待文不在兹兹蓋伏遇
punctuated: 聖人作而文運昌；五服有章，天命昭而德施普。幸覯臨雍之典，俄分在笥之珍，輝映六符，懽騰八裔。〔臣〕覺誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首上言：粤自虞廷命胄，司存四德之和；周室尊師，禮重三雍之對。緊明倫爲立敎之本，而太學延賢上所關。天王問道於澤宮，樂正升歌於壁水。樞衣鼓篋，萃東西南北之英；敬業樂羣，備春夏秋冬之訓。譽髦育德，思服流聲。惟兹懿軌既湮，遂爾麻風罕繼。詩書閒事，虛敦闕里牲牢；更𢀖徒尊，祇飾橋門觀聽。况入《易》稱五經之祖，而聖人脩十翼之辭。象爻組織於玄黃，奇耦樞機乎造化。圖讖古壁，幸秦燼之未殘；業侈顓門，慨漢箋之互異。丘、賀膏肓於讖緯，殊忝褒書；京房墨守其家林，無裨哀職。豈陰陽之未泰，致上下之不交？雖勤卜蔡之思，竟負拔茅之志。事誠有待，文不在兹？兹蓋伏遇
translation_en:
… a sage arises and literary fortune flourishes; the five vestments display their emblems, Heaven’s Mandate shines forth and virtuous largesse extends universally. Having the good fortune to witness the ceremony of the imperial visit to the Hall of Harmony, I suddenly received a share of the treasures kept in the royal hampers; their radiance illuminates the six stars of the Grand Staircase, and joy surges across the eight borderlands.

Your servant [Li] Jue, in utmost fear and trepidation, bows his head to the ground and submits these words: Ever since the court of Yu charged the Director of Music with educating the noble heirs, that office preserved the harmony of the four virtues; and when the House of Zhou honored its teachers, its ritual gave weight to responses in the three ceremonial halls. Truly, clarifying human relationships is the foundation of establishing education, and the National University [?] is what connects worthy men with the sovereign above. The Heavenly King inquired after the Way in the Marsh Palace, and the Director of Music ascended to sing by the Biyong moat. Lifting their robes and tapping their book-boxes, the finest talents from east, west, south, and north gathered together; revering their studies and delighting in fellowship, they completed the teachings of spring, summer, autumn, and winter. Celebrated talents nurtured their virtue, and admiring submission spread their renown.

Yet once these admirable tracks were obliterated, that glorious wind [?] was rarely continued. The Odes and Documents became an idle affair, even as sacrificial beasts were emptily lavished at Queli; the ritual of the Thrice Venerable and Five Elders was honored in vain, merely adorning the spectacle for observers at the bridged gates of the academy. How much more so given that the Great [?] Changes (Yi) is acclaimed as the ancestor of the Five Classics, and the Sage composed the words of the Ten Wings! Its images and lines weave together the dark of Heaven and the yellow of Earth; its odd and even numbers form the pivot of creation’s transformations. With diagrams hidden [?] in ancient walls, it fortunately survived the ashes of Qin intact; yet as scholarship boasted of specialized lineages, one laments the mutual discrepancies of the Han commentaries. [Meng] Xi [?] and [Jing] He were incurably obsessed with prognostic apocrypha, deeply shaming the edicts of praise; Jing Fang rigidly guarded his family’s Forest of Changes (Jialin), bringing no benefit to the imperial duties [?]. Was it that yin and yang had not yet reached a state of Peace (Tai), causing above and below to fail to commune? Though men were diligent in thoughts of divining with tortoise shells, in the end they betrayed the aspiration of pulling up the cogon grass by its roots. Truly the matter awaited its time—does not culture reside right here? This is because I humbly encounter…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
聖學日新
文明天啓
性耽圖籍開卷忘勞
躬履儉純澣衣求舊
崇聖賢之封襲功德邁於表章
念機杼之艱勞仁愛溢於綸綍
分陰希禹雖退食而靡遑
中昃師文眞望道而未見爰
===
諮舊典夙
駕乘輿遵槐市以
鳴鑾望杏壇而
駐蹕儒臣委佩爭依
弁冕之光相辟垂紳凜列簪纓之序
釋奠之儀甫畢談經之
命斯申謂說天莫辨乎易書而保治尤資於泰
卦考成均之鼓
召及庸流展帝乙之編陳斯奧義上行下濟
punctuated: 聖學日新，文明天啓。性耽圖籍，開卷忘勞；躬履儉純，澣衣求舊。崇聖賢之封襲，功德邁於表章；念機杼之艱勞，仁愛溢於綸綍。分陰希禹，雖退食而靡遑；中昃師文，眞望道而未見。爰諮舊典，夙駕乘輿；遵槐市以鳴鑾，望杏壇而駐蹕。儒臣委佩，爭依弁冕之光；相辟垂紳，凜列簪纓之序。釋奠之儀甫畢，談經之命斯申。謂說天莫辨乎《易》書，而保治尤資於《泰》卦。考成均之鼓，召及庸流；展帝乙之編，陳斯奧義。上行下濟，
translation_en:
… [Your Majesty], whose sagely learning is daily renewed and whose cultural splendor is heaven-inspired. By nature fond of charts and books, You forget fatigue upon unrolling a scroll; personally practicing frugality and purity, You wear washed robes and seek out veterans of old. You exalt the enfeoffments and hereditary successions of sages and worthies, Your merit and virtue surpassing past commemorations; You bear in mind the hardship and toil of the loom, Your benevolence and love overflowing in Your silken edicts. Cherishing every fraction of time in emulation of Yu, even when retiring for meals You take no leisure; working from midday till sunset with King Wen as Your teacher, You truly gaze toward the Way as though having not yet seen it.

Thereupon You consulted the old canons and early in the morning yoked the imperial carriage; following the Locust-Tree Market of the academy, You sounded the carriage bells, and gazing toward the Apricot Altar, You halted the imperial cortege. Confucian officials, their girdle pendants trailing, vied to bask in the radiance of the imperial cap and crown; assisting lords and princes, their sashes hanging down, stood in awe-inspiring array in the ranks of hairpins and cap-strings. No sooner had the ceremony of the libation sacrifice to Confucius concluded than the command to discourse upon the Classics was issued. Declaring that in explaining Heaven nothing is more discerning than the Book of Changes (Yi), and that for preserving good governance one relies especially upon the hexagram Peace (Tai), You struck the drums of the Imperial Academy (Chengjun) and extended Your summons even to a mediocre scholar like myself; unfolding the chapters speaking of Emperor Yi, I set forth its profound meaning. As the above goes forth and the below responds with aid, …

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
神明之德用彰小往大來消長之機具見
俯攄臆說仰瀆
宸聰道尚中行冀沃心之有補占孚元吉感
虛受之不遺前席增輝下堂思懼何意綺紋
之
貺特加韋布之微彩挹鳳苞奚俟霞生九色
織同蟬翼居然星繞七襄匪朱紱之爲華
惟玄纁其比重
尚方傳錫
===
恩踰漢祖之解衣東序欽承榮並唐皇之賜錦
且累絲尚難㦯匠而敝袴宜待有功曾無
尺寸之勞忝藉冠裳之會
寵靈優渥愧汗繽紛伏念臣覺一介孤寒九
流佔俾起家將作旋膺墨綬之榮進秩膠
庠竊效青衿之詠纖線之長雖竭無益經
綸箕裘之業未荒僅資縫掖
六龍在御喜
堯雲舜日之共膽一象粗諫慚孔思周情之尚
punctuated: 神明之德用彰；小往大來，消長之機具見。俯攄臆說，仰瀆宸聰。道尚中行，冀沃心之有補；占孚元吉，感虛受之不遺。前席增輝，下堂思懼。何意綺紋之貺，特加韋布之微！彩挹鳳苞，奚俟霞生九色；織同蟬翼，居然星繞七襄。匪朱紱之爲華，惟玄纁其比重。尚方傳錫，恩踰漢祖之解衣；東序欽承，榮並唐皇之賜錦。且累絲尚難㦯匠，而敝袴宜待有功；曾無尺寸之勞，忝藉冠裳之會。寵靈優渥，愧汗繽紛。伏念臣覺一介孤寒，九流佔俾。起家將作，旋膺墨綬之榮；進秩膠庠，竊效青衿之詠。纖線之長雖竭，無益經綸；箕裘之業未荒，僅資縫掖。六龍在御，喜堯雲舜日之共膽；一象粗諫，慚孔思周情之尚
translation_en: … thereby the virtue of spiritual intelligence is made manifest; as the small departs and the great approaches, the mechanisms of waning and waxing are fully revealed. Humbly pouring forth my personal conjectures, I have presumptuously importuned the imperial hearing. The Way prizes the course of the mean, and I hoped to offer some aid in enriching Your Majesty's mind; the divination accords with supreme auspiciousness, and I am moved that Your receptive humility overlooked nothing. Having my mat moved forward added to my glory; descending from the hall, I reflected in trepidation. How could I have expected that a bestowal of patterned damask would be specially conferred upon one as lowly as a wearer of leather and homespun! Its colors draw from the phoenix's plumage—what need to wait for the clouds to bring forth nine hues? Its weave is like a cicada's wing, naturally as though the stars had circled through the seven shifts of the sky. It is not the vermilion knee-covers that constitute splendor; only the dark and crimson silks can compare in weight of honor. Transmitted and bestowed from the Directorate for Imperial Manufactories, this grace surpasses the Han Founder's unfastening of his own robe; reverently received in the Eastern Collège, this glory equals the Tang Emperor's gift of brocade. Moreover, accumulating single threads still challenges a skillful artisan [?], and even worn-out trousers ought to be reserved for those of merit; yet without an inch or a foot of achievement, I have unworthily shared in this gathering of caps and robes. Your favored grace is so abundant and generous that my sweat of shame flows profusely. Humbly I reflect that I, Jue, am a solitary man of humble origins, merely droning over texts among the Nine Schools. Starting my official career in the Directorate for Palace Buildings, I soon received the honor of the black ribbon; promoted in rank to the Imperial Academy, I privately emulated the song of the "Blue Collar." Though I exhaust my slender thread-like talent, it is of no avail to the grand ordering of statecraft; though the inherited craft of my ancestors has not been neglected, it suffices only to clothe me in the wide-sleeved robe of a scholar. Now that the Six Dragons are driven by Your Majesty, I rejoice that all behold the clouds of Yao and the sun of Shun; yet having roughly expounded [?] a single hexagram-image, I am ashamed that the thoughts of Confucius and the sentiments of the Duke of Zhou remain so…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
遠受服循虞其三褫白公無斁於五紀蓋
聖人之心下交故君子之道日長被茲輕煖慶
乃遭逢臣敢不仰止宮牆遡眞精于秘畫
希聲竹帛期黼黻乎
皇猷伏願
德合坤乾
文成經緯
垂旒塞纊勿自用其聰明
負扆臨軒期廣延乎俊傑
政擬結繩而治
===
道不下帶而存
極則成輔相之能奠生靈於衽席
謹往復平陂之戒繫
國祚於苞桑天地交而萬物通永保
垂裳之化
明良會而庶事舉於昭廣被之麻臣覺無任瞻
天仰
聖激切感戴之至謹奏
punctuated: 遠。受服循虞其三褫，白公無斁於五紀。蓋聖人之心下交，故君子之道日長。被茲輕煖，慶乃遭逢。臣敢不仰止宮牆，遡眞精于秘畫；希聲竹帛，期黼黻乎皇猷。伏願德合坤乾，文成經緯。垂旒塞纊，勿自用其聰明；負扆臨軒，期廣延乎俊傑。政擬結繩而治，道不下帶而存。極則成輔相之能，奠生靈於衽席；謹往復平陂之戒，繫國祚於苞桑。天地交而萬物通，永保垂裳之化；明良會而庶事舉，於昭廣被之麻。臣覺無任瞻天仰聖，激切感戴之至，謹奏
translation_en:
…far off. Upon receiving my robes, I still fear having them stripped away thrice [hexagram Song 訟, 6 in the top place]; yet in service to the state I shall be untiring in the five threads of silk [Odes, "Gao Yang" 羔羊]. For because the Sage's heart communicates downward with his subjects, the Way of the gentleman grows daily [hexagram Tai 泰].Clothed in this light and warm garment, I rejoice in such an encounter with Your Majesty's grace. How could your servant dare not look up to the Master's precinct wall, tracing the true essence in the mysterious trigrams, and aspire to leave a reputation on bamboo and silk, hoping to embroider the August Plan?

Humbly I pray that Your Majesty's virtue may match Earth and Heaven, and Your cultural pattern form warp and woof; that hanging down the jade pendants of Your crown and stopping Your ears with floss, You do not rely solely on Your own acuteness of sight and hearing; and that with Your back to the painted screen as You approach the front gallery, You seek to extend a wide welcome to men of outstanding talent. May Your governance rival the Era of Knotted Cords in its order, and the Way abide closer than below the sash. May You bring to perfection the capacity of assisting and complementing Heaven and Earth [hexagram Tai, Grand Image], settling the living people upon secure mats; and heed the warning that level ground becomes a slope and going is followed by return [hexagram Tai, 9 in the third place], binding the dynastic fortune to clustering mulberry roots [hexagram Pi 否, 9 in the fifth place]. When Heaven and Earth are in communion, the myriad things flourish, forever preserving the transformative rule of the Sovereigns who governed simply by letting their robes hang down; when an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers meet, all affairs prosper, gloriously manifesting widely diffused blessings! Your servant Jue is overcome with the utmost emotion and gratitude in looking up to Heaven and beholding the Sage, and respectfully presents…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
表稱
謝以
聞
第參場
策〔五道〕
第一問
劉不溢
同考試官教諭木　批　我
皇上敬德性生
書法亦自天授此作揄揚得體末復歸重謹微美不忘規忠矣録之可不謂
===
得士乎
同考試官教諭林　批　前代帝王垂教萬世暨我
祖宗並美十六初旨以持敬爲聖功非獨其言善也今
皇上以英年默契危爲最難子能悉舉而闡揚之爛然有第可取可取
考試官教諭俞　批　闡揚
聖敬爲持盈守成之本最是文更博雅當是鴻儒
考試官教諭孫　批　四代之典謨
本朝之敬戒十五陛也吾子能博綜而約說之可録哉
punctuated:
表稱謝以聞。

第參場
策〔五道〕

第一問
劉不溢
同考試官教諭木　批：我皇上敬德性生，書法亦自天授。此作揄揚得體，末復歸重謹微，美不忘規，忠矣。録之，可不謂得士乎？
同考試官教諭林　批：前代帝王垂教萬世，暨我祖宗並美十六初旨，以持敬爲聖功，非獨其言善也。今皇上以英年默契，危爲最難。子能悉舉而闡揚之，爛然有第，可取，可取。
考試官教諭俞　批：闡揚聖敬，爲持盈守成之本，最是。文更博雅，當是鴻儒。
考試官教諭孫　批：四代之典謨，本朝之敬戒，十五陛也。吾子能博綜而約說之，可録哉！
translation_en:
… a memorial expressing gratitude, for Your Majesty's information.

Third Session
Policy Essays [Five Questions]

First Question
Liu Buyi 劉不溢
Associate Examiner and Instructor Mu 木 comments: Our August Emperor's reverent virtue is innate, and his calligraphy is likewise heaven-bestowed. This composition praises him appropriately, and at the end returns its emphasis to exercising caution in small matters; in praising beauty it does not forget admonition—truly loyal! In recording it for selection, can we not say that we have obtained a true scholar?
Associate Examiner and Instructor Lin 林 comments: The emperors and kings of former dynasties handed down teachings for ten thousand generations, and together with our Imperial Ancestors they match in excellence the original sixteen-character precept [of the Book of Documents], taking the maintenance of reverence as the achievement of sagehood—it is not merely that their words are good. Now our August Emperor in his youthful prime silently accords with this, recognizing that being mindful of peril is most difficult. You have been able to cite all of this and expound upon it in brilliant order. Worthy of selection, worthy of selection!
Examiner and Instructor Yu 俞 comments: Expounding upon sagely reverence as the foundation for preserving fullness and maintaining existing achievements is most fitting. The writing is moreover erudite and refined; he must be a great Confucian scholar.
Examiner and Instructor Sun 孫 comments: The canons and counsels of the Four Dynasties and the reverent admonitions of Our Dynasty are like ascending fifteen steps [?]. You have been able to synthesize them broadly and explain them concisely; worthy of recording indeed!

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
聖人之心至敬也是故躬天下之至德而
不有覆天下之至尊而不居德爲聖人何
不有也進德之功無已不敢以自盈也尊
爲天子何不居也保尊之道惟艱不敢以
自暇也有厥善者喪厥善危其心者安其
身幾固爾也聖人知幾於豫而防慾於微
故春冰之履常若陷而九軌之所以平也
朽索之馭常若驚而六馬之所以調也是
不有其德不居其尊者莫如聖人而常有
===
其德常居其尊者亦莫如聖人彼昫昫惟
桎梏其說者豈足與論聖人之心哉今夫
聖人所恃以宰制天下者心也而所資以
訓命天下者言也脩省惕於中儆戒設於
外防逸慾節性情以帝以王用是道也匪
是則晝脂鏤冰而黼藻其盤盂辭雖工壯
夫不爲也而況聖人乎楊子之言曰虞夏
之書渾渾爾商書灝灝爾謂忠質之化未
漓而其辭淳也周書噩噩爾謂禮樂之文
punctuated:
聖人之心，至敬也。是故躬天下之至德而不有，覆天下之至尊而不居。德爲聖人，何不有也？進德之功無已，不敢以自盈也；尊爲天子，何不居也？保尊之道惟艱，不敢以自暇也。有厥善者喪厥善，危其心者安其身，幾固爾也。聖人知幾於豫而防慾於微，故春冰之履常若陷，而九軌之所以平也；朽索之馭常若驚，而六馬之所以調也。是不有其德、不居其尊者，莫如聖人；而常有其德、常居其尊者，亦莫如聖人。彼昫昫惟桎梏其說者，豈足與論聖人之心哉！
今夫聖人所恃以宰制天下者，心也；而所資以訓命天下者，言也。脩省惕於中，儆戒設於外，防逸慾、節性情，以帝以王，用是道也。匪是，則晝脂鏤冰而黼藻其盤盂，辭雖工，壯夫不爲也，而況聖人乎！楊子之言曰：「虞夏之書渾渾爾，商書灝灝爾。」謂忠質之化未漓，而其辭淳也。「周書噩噩爾。」謂禮樂之文
translation_en:
The mind of the sage is one of utmost reverence. Therefore, he embodies the supreme virtue under heaven without claiming possession of it, and occupies the supreme honor under heaven without resting comfortably in it. When his virtue is that of a sage, why does he not claim possession of it? Because the effort of advancing in virtue is endless, and he dares not be self-satisfied. When his honor is that of the Son of Heaven, why does he not rest comfortably in it? Because the way of preserving such honor is arduous, and he dares not allow himself ease. He who claims possession of his goodness loses his goodness; he who keeps his mind alert to danger secures his person—such is inherently the subtle mechanism of things. The sage perceives these subtle beginnings beforehand and guards against desires in their minutest states. Thus, treading as if on spring ice, constantly fearful of falling through, is precisely how the nine-track highway is kept level; driving as if with rotten reins, constantly fearful of bolting, is precisely how the six horses are kept in harmony. Therefore, none is more reluctant to claim his virtue or rest in his honor than the sage, and yet none more constantly possesses his virtue and retains his honor than the sage. How could those petty pedants who merely shackle themselves to rigid doctrines be worthy of discussing the mind of the sage!

Now then, what the sage relies upon to govern and regulate the world is his mind, and what he draws upon to instruct and command the world are his words. Cultivating self-examination and vigilance within, setting up admonitions and warnings without, guarding against indulgent desires and regulating the dispositions and emotions—whether ruling as an emperor or as a王 (king), it is by this Way. Without this, it would be like painting on grease or carving on ice just to adorn washbasins and bowls with flowery patterns; though the words might be skillful, a grown man would not do it, much less a sage! Master Yang (Yang Xiong 楊雄) said: "The Documents of Yu and Xia are profound and vast; the Documents of Shang are grand and boundless"—meaning that the transformative influence of loyalty and substance had not yet thinned out, and so their words were pure. "The Documents of Zhou are solemn and rigorous"—meaning that the refinement of rites and music…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
日開而其辭察也蓋擬其氣象若此至要
之兢兢業業則商不能改乎虞夏周不能
改乎商相授一道相守一心其帝王之德
業所由弘而訓命所由著乎嘗觀作總章
以奉政者舜也其辭曰畏天而愛民恤遠
而親近好問而好察隱惡而揚善至於惟
危惟微之命尤凜凜焉銘筍簴以聽治者
禹也其辭曰教以道者擊鼓諭以義者擊
鐘告以事者振鐸語以憂者擊磬有訟獄
者撻鞀至於禽荒色荒之戒尤諄諄焉此
===
虞夏之文文其心之敬而已也湯作諸器
用之銘書不盡載其銘盤以自儆則曰苟
日新日日新又日新旁求俊彥啓迪後人
其爲官刑警于有位則曰惟兹三風十愆
卿士邦君不可有一于身武王聞丹書之
言惕若恐懼退而銘其席之前左端曰安
樂必敬右端曰毋行可悔後左端曰一反
一側亦不可以忘右端曰所監不遠視爾
punctuated: 日開，而其辭察也。蓋擬其氣象若此。至要之兢兢業業，則商不能改乎虞、夏，周不能改乎商，相授一道，相守一心，其帝王之德業所由弘，而訓命所由著乎？嘗觀作總章以奉政者，舜也，其辭曰：「畏天而愛民，恤遠而親近，好問而好察，隱惡而揚善。」至於「惟危惟微」之命，尤凜凜焉。銘筍簴以聽治者，禹也，其辭曰：「教以道者擊鼓，諭以義者擊鐘，告以事者振鐸，語以憂者擊磬，有訟獄者撻鞀。」至於「禽荒色荒」之戒，尤諄諄焉。此虞、夏之文，文其心之敬而已也。湯作諸器用之銘，《書》不盡載。其銘盤以自儆，則曰：「苟日新，日日新，又日新。」旁求俊彥，啓迪後人，其爲《官刑》警于有位，則曰：「惟兹三風十愆，卿士、邦君不可有一于身。」武王聞《丹書》之言，惕若恐懼，退而銘其席之前左端曰：「安樂必敬。」右端曰：「毋行可悔。」後左端曰：「一反一側，亦不可以忘。」右端曰：「所監不遠，視爾
translation_en:
… unfolded day by day, and its words are discerning. Thus did he characterize their overarching spirit. Yet when it comes to the essential point of being cautious and conscientious, the Shang could not alter that of Yu and Xia, nor could the Zhou alter that of the Shang. Passing down the single Way and upholding the single mind—is this not whereby the virtuous achievements of emperors and kings were broadened, and whereby their instructions and commands were made manifest?

Consider how Shun constructed the Grand Hall (Zongzhang) to administer governance; his words read: "Revere Heaven and love the people; show compassion to the distant and hold close the near; delight in questioning and delight in examining; conceal evil and promote goodness." And when it came to the charge regarding "how precarious, how subtle," he was especially awe-struck. He who inscribed the bell-and-chime frames to hear governance was Yu; his words read: "He who would instruct me in the Way, strike the drum; he who would advise me in righteousness, strike the bell; he who would report on affairs, shake the clapper-bell; he who would speak of anxieties, strike the stone chime; he who has a lawsuit, beat the hand-drum." And when it came to the warnings against "addiction to hunting and addiction to sensual pleasure," he was especially earnest. Thus the literary expressions of Yu and Xia were nothing more than giving outward form to the reverence of their minds.

Tang composed inscriptions for various vessels and implements, which the Book of Documents does not record in full. In inscribing his washbasin to admonish himself, he said: "If you can renovate yourself one day, do so from day to day; let there be daily renovation." Seeking out men ofoutstanding talent on all sides and enlightening his successors, he composed the Punishments for Officials (Guanxing) to warn those in office, saying: "As for these three decadent customs and ten faults, neither ministers and officers nor rulers of states may harbor a single one in their persons."

When King Wu heard the words of the Cinnabar Book (Danshu), he was seized with reverent fear; withdrawing, he inscribed the front left corner of his mat: "In peace and pleasure, you must be reverent"; the right corner: "Do not do what you may regret"; the rear left corner: "Even in tossing and turning, you must not forget"; and the right corner: "What you should take as a mirror is not far off: look to what you…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
所代銘於鑑曰見爾前慮爾後銘於盤
曰與其溺於人也寧溺於淵銘於楹曰毋
曰胡害其禍將大毋曰胡傷其禍將長銘
於杖曰烏乎危於忿疐失道於嗜慾相忘
於富貴銘於席曰愼戒必恭恭則壽銘於
劒曰帶之以為服動必行德銘於矛曰造
矛造矛少間弗忍終身之羞予一人所聞
以戒後世子孫是商周之文亦文其心之
敬而已也而所謂渾渾灝灝噩噩者其天
===
下之至文乎故丹青於一時而龜鑑於萬
世舜禹巍巍乎湯武身之也四代之所以
隆也豈惟四代前乎此而帝堯有之矣立
木而使天下得盡其言建旌而使天下得
盡其才置鼓而使天下得攻其過是何心
耶前乎堯而黃帝又有之矣作輿几之箴
以警宴安作金几之銘以戒逸欲不自高
其道不自聖其躬是何心耶由古以來聖
人享國長久令名無窮者固未始不自其
punctuated: 所代。」銘於鑑曰：「見爾前，慮爾後。」銘於盤曰：「與其溺於人也，寧溺於淵。」銘於楹曰：「毋曰胡害，其禍將大；毋曰胡傷，其禍將長。」銘於杖曰：「烏乎危於忿疐，失道於嗜慾，相忘於富貴。」銘於席曰：「愼戒必恭，恭則壽。」銘於劒曰：「帶之以為服，動必行德。」銘於矛曰：「造矛造矛，少間弗忍，終身之羞。予一人所聞，以戒後世子孫。」是商周之文，亦文其心之敬而已也。而所謂渾渾、灝灝、噩噩者，其天下之至文乎！故丹青於一時，而龜鑑於萬世。舜、禹巍巍乎，湯、武身之也，四代之所以隆也。豈惟四代，前乎此而帝堯有之矣。立木而使天下得盡其言，建旌而使天下得盡其才，置鼓而使天下得攻其過，是何心耶？前乎堯而黃帝又有之矣。作《輿几之箴》以警宴安，作《金几之銘》以戒逸欲，不自高其道，不自聖其躬，是何心耶？由古以來，聖人享國長久、令名無窮者，固未始不自其
