title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
之以德意而遠近之吏莫不竦心滌慮以
承休德者此則上之所使也漢宣帝曰庶
民安其田里而無歎息愁恨之聲者政平
訟理也與我共此者其惟良二千石乎斯
言也可不謂深達治本者哉是故裂百十
里而爲縣縣有令環數縣而爲郡郡有守
朝有便焉下之民夕達之矣夕有便焉下
之民朝達之矣其視四封之內皆其家也
其家人子弟之衆與其器用財賄可以耳
目習而頤指使之也故其膏澤易及而敎
===
化易行也而其本則在於上焉司馬遷有
言法令者治之具而非制治淸濁之源也
尚寬和則道德齊禮之俗成崇法罔則武
健嚴酷之士進循斯以談豈惟士之自靡
哉亦其勢使之然也以漢事論之漢初天
子加惠元元思與休息尤重守令之選數
召見二千石問治效下璽書褒美增秩賜
金公卿缺則選諸所表用之故三代下漢
punctuated: 之以德意，而遠近之吏莫不竦心滌慮以承休德者，此則上之所使也。漢宣帝曰：「庶民安其田里，而無歎息愁恨之聲者，政平訟理也。與我共此者，其惟良二千石乎！」斯言也，可不謂深達治本者哉？是故裂百十里而爲縣，縣有令；環數縣而爲郡，郡有守。朝有便焉，下之民夕達之矣；夕有便焉，下之民朝達之矣。其視四封之內，皆其家也；其家人子弟之衆，與其器用財賄，可以耳目習而頤指使之也。故其膏澤易及，而敎化易行也。而其本則在於上焉。司馬遷有言：「法令者，治之具，而非制治淸濁之源也。」尚寬和，則道德齊禮之俗成；崇法罔，則武健嚴酷之士進。循斯以談，豈惟士之自靡哉？亦其勢使之然也。以漢事論之：漢初天子加惠元元，思與休息，尤重守令之選。數召見二千石，問治效，下璽書褒美，增秩賜金；公卿缺，則選諸所表用之。故三代下，漢…
translation_en: …extending it with benevolent intent, so that officials near and far without exception rouse their hearts and cleanse their thoughts to uphold the sovereign's fine virtue—this is brought about by the ruler above. Emperor Xuan of the Han (Han Xuandi 漢宣帝) said: "That the common people are secure in their fields and villages, with no sounds of sighing, sorrow, or resentment, is because governance is fair and litigation is well-ordered. Are not those who share this task with me the worthy two-thousand-bushel officials (prefects and commandery governors)?" Can these words not be called deeply penetrating to the root of governance? Therefore, territory of a hundred or tens of li is carved out to form a district, and each district has a magistrate; several districts are encircled to form a commandery, and each commandery has a governor. If there is a measure beneficial in the morning, the people below feel its reach by evening; if there is a measure beneficial in the evening, the people below feel its reach by the next morning. They regard everything within their four borders as their own household; the multitude of their household members and younger kinsmen, along with their implements and wealth, can all be familiar to their ears and eyes and directed with a nod of the chin. Thus, their nurturing grace easily reaches the people, and their moral transformation is easily carried out. Yet the root of this lies above. Sima Qian 司馬遷 had a saying: "Laws and ordinances are the instruments of governance, not the source that determines whether governance is pure or turbid." When leniency and harmony are prized, customs guided by virtue and regulated by ritual are formed; when the net of the law is exalted, fierce, vigorous, stern, and harsh men advance in office. Speaking along these lines, how could it merely be that scholars allow themselves to be swept along? It is also the force of circumstances that makes it so. To discuss this in terms of Han affairs: in the early Han, the Son of Heaven bestowed kindness upon the common folk and sought to give them rest and recuperation, placing particular weight on the selection of commandery governors and district magistrates. Emperors frequently summoned two-thousand-bushel officials for audiences to inquire into the effectiveness of their governance, sent down imperial letters under seal to praise and commend them, raised their official ranks, and bestowed gold upon them; when posts among the Three Dukes and Nine卿 (Grand Counselors and Ministers) fell vacant, candidates were selected and appointed from among those who had been singled out for distinction. Therefore, after the Three Dynasties, Han…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
治號爲近古夷考其時若河內守吳公治
平爲天下第一而史失其名彼蓋循循悶
悶不以名自見也嗣是而京兆渤海表表
一時若循吏傳所紀者未易悉數其在中
州則黃次公守潁川而力行敎化召信臣
守南陽而勸課農桑究其所務心不出乎
雞豚米鹽之細而身不越乎阡陌泉渠之
間蓋庶乎家視郡邑而子視烝黎矣當時
神爵之集召父之稱豈虛也哉若治鄴投
===
巫民不敢欺智足稱也而近於譎矣敎吏
鉅箭破散豪傑能足稱也而近於儌矣史
氏之不傳於循吏者不爲過也嗟夫民之
望治於守令也甚矣其親之以父母而尊
之以師帥寒欲其衣饑欲其食勞苦疾困
欲其噢咻噢然一有不得則以爲父母
者之棄已況望其殘肌膚以自逞哉倫理
欲其敎爭奪欲其治姦宄矯虔欲其鋤剪
睊睊然一有不遂則以爲師帥者之遺已
punctuated: 治號爲近古。夷考其時，若河內守吳公，治平爲天下第一，而史失其名，彼蓋循循悶悶，不以名自見也。嗣是而京兆、渤海，表表一時，若《循吏傳》所紀者，未易悉數。其在中州，則黃次公守潁川而力行敎化，召信臣守南陽而勸課農桑。究其所務，心不出乎雞豚米鹽之細，而身不越乎阡陌泉渠之間，蓋庶乎家視郡邑，而子視烝黎矣。當時神爵之集、「召父」之稱，豈虛也哉！若治鄴投巫，民不敢欺，智足稱也，而近於譎矣；敎吏鉅箭，破散豪傑，能足稱也，而近於儌矣。史氏之不傳於循吏者，不爲過也。嗟夫！民之望治於守令也甚矣！其親之以父母，而尊之以師帥。寒欲其衣，饑欲其食，勞苦疾困欲其噢咻，噢然一有不得，則以爲父母者之棄已，況望其殘肌膚以自逞哉！倫理欲其敎，爭奪欲其治，姦宄矯虔欲其鋤剪，睊睊然一有不遂，則以爲師帥者之遺已，
translation_en:
…governance was renowned as approaching that of antiquity. If we examine that era objectively, someone like Duke Wu (Wu gong 吳公), Governor of Henei, ranked first in the empire for peaceful governance, yet the histories lost his personal name—for he was doubtless methodical and unostentatious, not seeking to distinguish himself through fame. Thereafter, governors in Jingzhao and Bohai stood out prominently in their times, and those recorded in the "Biographies of Upright Officials" (Xunli zhuan) are too numerous to count in full. Here in the Central Plain (Henan), Huang Cigong (Huang Ba 黃霸) served as Governor of Yingchuan and vigorously promoted moral transformation through education, while Shao Xinchen (召信臣) served as Governor of Nanyang and encouraged and supervised agriculture and sericulture. If we examine what they devoted themselves to, their minds did not stray beyond the small particulars of chickens, pigs, rice, and salt, and their persons did not go beyond the footpaths between fields and the springs and irrigation channels. Indeed, they came close to regarding the commanderies and counties as their own households, and the common multitude as their own children! At that time, how could the gathering of auspicious phoenixes (shenjue) or the appellation "Father Shao" have been empty praise? As for governing Ye by casting the shamans into the river so that the people dared not deceive—the wisdom is worthy of praise, yet it bordered on craftiness; or instructing clerks with hooked bamboo tubes (jujian 距筩 [? 鉅箭]) to break up and scatter powerful local bullies—the capability is worthy of praise, yet it bordered onopportunistic scheming (jiao 儌). That the historians did not include them among the Upright Officials is not unreasonable.

Alas! How intensely the people long for good governance from their Governors and Magistrates! They feel affection for them as father and mother, and revere them as teachers and leaders. When cold, they wish for them to clothe them; when hungry, they wish for them to feed them; when exhausted, suffering, sick, or distressed, they wish for them to soothe and comfort them. Moaning in pain [? 噢然], if there is a single thing they fail to obtain, they feel that those who are their father and mother have abandoned them—how much less would they expect them to mutilate their flesh and skin to gratify their own ambitions! In human moral relations, they wish for them to instruct them; in disputes and seizures, they wish for them to adjudicate; toward traitors, villains, and violent extortionists, they wish for them to weed and prune them out. Looking on anxiously, if there is a single thing left unfulfilled, they feel that those who are their teachers and leaders have forsaken them—…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
況望其剝膏髓以自封哉而世之君子顧
有慮不動於閭閻情不切於痌瘝顧擊搏
於鷹鸇而立威名於督伯者朝廷亦何取
於斯人而用之也
明興
高皇帝生長民間習知民隱尤精察吏治郡縣
之吏不十餘年不遷其廉能最著卓有成
効者召對稱
旨輒超拜卿貳無問資格尤重贓墨之懲不少
===
寬假以故吏稱其職民樂其業二百年餘
道洽方外化被羣生致治之盛有由然也
後以士樂速遷銓敘立法調停二千石令
長往往三歲一代於是吏多爲烜赫目前
苟簡歲月之計溫仁多恕蒲鞭示辱固亦
有焉而張急揚沸以爲能者未始無也下
車問俗敬老恤孤固亦有焉而察淵竭澤
以爲智者未始無也柱後之意勝則甘棠
之德衰乳虎之習多則騶虞之化遠其下
punctuated:
況望其剝膏髓以自封哉！而世之君子，顧有慮不動於閭閻，情不切於痌瘝，顧擊搏於鷹鸇，而立威名於督伯者，朝廷亦何取於斯人而用之也？
明興，高皇帝生長民間，習知民隱，尤精察吏治。郡縣之吏，不十餘年不遷；其廉能最著、卓有成効者，召對稱旨，輒超拜卿貳，無問資格。尤重贓墨之懲，不少寬假。以故吏稱其職，民樂其業。二百年餘，道洽方外，化被羣生，致治之盛，有由然也。後以士樂速遷，銓敘立法調停，二千石、令長往往三歲一代。於是吏多爲烜赫目前、苟簡歲月之計。溫仁多恕、蒲鞭示辱，固亦有焉，而張急揚沸以爲能者，未始無也；下車問俗、敬老恤孤，固亦有焉，而察淵竭澤以爲智者，未始無也。柱後之意勝，則甘棠之德衰；乳虎之習多，則騶虞之化遠。其下
translation_en:
…how much less would they expect them to strip away their fat and marrow to enrich themselves! Yet among the gentlemen of the world, there are nonetheless those whose thoughts are not moved by the common folk in their villages, and whose feelings are not touched by the people's distress and sickness, who instead strike and seize like hawks and falcons and establish a fearsome reputation through severe punishment [?]. What then does the court find desirable in such men that it employs them?

When the Ming arose, the Exalted Emperor (Gao Huangdi) grew up among the common people; he was intimately familiar with the hidden sufferings of the populace and was especially discerning in examining the governance of officials. Officials of commanderies and counties were not transferred until more than ten years had passed. Those whose integrity and capability were most prominent and who had achieved outstanding results were summoned for an audience, and if they pleased the Imperial Will, they were immediately promoted out of turn to be Chief Ministers or Vice Ministers, without regard to seniority or qualifications. He placed particular emphasis on punishing corruption and venality, showing not the slightest leniency. For this reason, officials fulfilled their duties and the people rejoiced in their livelihoods. For more than two hundred years, the Way has permeated the realm and moral transformation has covered all living beings; there is truly a reason for this flourishing achievement of good governance.

Later, because scholars delighted in rapid promotion, the personnel selection system established laws to accommodate them, and two-thousand-bushel officials [prefects] and county magistrates were often replaced every three years. Thereupon, officials mostly made plans for dazzling immediate displays and perfunctory, makeshift measures to pass the months and years. Those who are gentle, benevolent, and forgiving, using whips of rushes merely to show shame, certainly do exist, yet it is not that there are none who regard stringing the bow taut and stirring up boiling water as capability; those who inquire into local customs upon alighting from their carriages, respecting the aged and showing compassion for orphans, certainly do exist, yet it is not that there are none who regard peering into the deep abyss and draining the marshes as wisdom. When the spirit of the iron-crowned judicial cap prevails, the virtue of the sweet-pear tree declines; when the habits of nursing tigers multiply, the moral transformation of the righteous zouyu beast grows distant. Those below them…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
者逼怵無聊剝民爲利而已夫士君子欲
以興利除害化民成俗固非數歲所能也
而三載之內業不能待其成不有希奇曷
所自見薦剡名譽逼於後而優秩尊遇誘
於前自非學道愛人寵辱不驚之君子亦
安能廿心積薪忘情枳棘鬱龐眉之都尉
而挫猿臂之將軍哉則所以驅天下而啟
惰者亦非獨吏之過也近者
廟堂之上燭見弊源力破舊習疏行久任郡縣
===
長吏有五六年不得調者於是士無苟簡
之心民有寧一之望矣而民生猶未阜教
化猶未宣者何也議者曰是在明賞罰覈
功實由按部破恒格斯固一道也亦有不
可盡恃者夫功高蒙厚賞故烈士爭趨罪
著有顯戮故貪夫改行此賞罰之所宜明
者也而巧於掩覆者能保無漏網耶其廉
吏以某事知廉故廉非矯飾某能吏以某
事知能故能非誣善此功實之所宜覈者
punctuated: 者，逼怵無聊，剝民爲利而已。夫士君子欲以興利除害、化民成俗，固非數歲所能也。而三載之內，業不能待其成，不有希奇，曷所自見？薦剡名譽逼於後，而優秩尊遇誘於前，自非學道愛人、寵辱不驚之君子，亦安能廿心積薪，忘情枳棘，鬱龐眉之都尉，而挫猿臂之將軍哉？則所以驅天下而啟惰者，亦非獨吏之過也。近者廟堂之上，燭見弊源，力破舊習，疏行久任，郡縣長吏有五六年不得調者。於是士無苟簡之心，民有寧一之望矣。而民生猶未阜，教化猶未宣者，何也？議者曰：是在明賞罰、覈功實、由按部、破恒格。斯固一道也，亦有不可盡恃者。夫功高蒙厚賞，故烈士爭趨；罪著有顯戮，故貪夫改行，此賞罰之所宜明者也。而巧於掩覆者，能保無漏網耶？其廉吏以某事知廉，故廉非矯飾；某能吏以某事知能，故能非誣善，此功實之所宜覈者…
translation_en:
…those of the lowest sort, pressed by anxiety and at their wits' end, merely fleece the common people for their own profit. Now, when a scholar-gentleman wishes to promote what is beneficial and eliminate what is harmful, to transform the people and perfect their customs, this is certainly not something that can be accomplished in just a few years. Yet within a three-year term, one already cannot wait for the work to reach completion; without striving for novelty and spectacle, how can one distinguish oneself? When recommendations and reputation press from behind, while superior ranks and honored treatment entice from ahead, unless one is a gentleman who has studied the Way and loves the people, unmoved by favor or disgrace, how could one be content [廿心, read 甘心] to be passed over like firewood piled beneath new logs, remain indifferent to a lowly perch among thorns and brambles, leave the bushy-browed Commandant (Yan駟) languishing in obscurity, or frustrate the ape-armed General (Li Guang)? Thus, that which drives the empire and encourages negligence is not solely the fault of the officials themselves.

Recently, those in the imperial court have clearly perceived the source of these abuses, vigorously broken with old habits, and memorialized to implement long-term tenure, so that some chief officials of prefectures and counties go five or six years without being transferred. As a result, scholar-officials no longer harbor intentions of perfunctory makeshift governance, and the people have hope for peace and stability. Yet why is it that the people's livelihood is still not abundant, and moral transformation is still not widespread? Those who deliberate on policy say: "This lies in clarifying rewards and punishments, verifying actual achievements, relying on the touring regional inspectors, and breaking with routine precedents." This is certainly one approach, yet there are aspects of it that cannot be wholly relied upon.

When high merit receives generous reward, ardent men vie to step forward; when manifest crime meets with public punishment, greedy men reform their conduct—this is why rewards and punishments ought to be made clear. Yet can we guarantee that those skillful at covering up their tracks will not slip through the net? When a certain incorrupt official is known to be incorrupt through a specific deed, his incorruptibility is not pretentious affectation; when a certain capable official is known to be capable through a specific deed, his capability is not falsely attributed virtue—this is why actual achievements ought to be verified…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
也而工於枼著者能保無匿情耶多指亂
視多聽亂聰是故舉劾貴專也而諸道直
指理不得不重之事權當事者業已難之
矣又試以責其成厚報以勵其志是故恒
格宜破也而欲以新進之人加之老成之
上人情且有所不堪矣大抵法可以防奸
而不可以盡奸激勸行於君子而刑威不
能化乎小人況上用目則下飾形上用耳
則下飾聲隱微之地能一一而察之哉陸
贄氏有言漢武好英風故其時富瓌偉立
名之士漢宣精吏治故其時萃循良覈實
之能夫吏亦在乎倡之而已
===
聖天子舉增秩賜金故事且發
德音褒勵卓越之績視前世璽書不啻重之一
時大小臣工莫不改觀易聽惟
上所令冀以宣
主德而厚民生蓋凜凜如也執事者猶欲議吏
於儒生顧儒生豈有知乎抑有說焉龔遂
punctuated: 也，而工於枼著者，能保無匿情耶？多指亂視，多聽亂聰，是故舉劾貴專也，而諸道直指理不得不重之事權，當事者業已難之矣。又試以責其成，厚報以勵其志，是故恒格宜破也，而欲以新進之人加之老成之上，人情且有所不堪矣。大抵法可以防奸，而不可以盡奸；激勸行於君子，而刑威不能化乎小人。況上用目則下飾形，上用耳則下飾聲，隱微之地，能一一而察之哉？陸贄氏有言：「漢武好英風，故其時富瓌偉立名之士；漢宣精吏治，故其時萃循良覈實之能。」夫吏亦在乎倡之而已。聖天子舉增秩賜金故事，且發德音，褒勵卓越之績，視前世璽書不啻重之。一時大小臣工，莫不改觀易聽，惟上所令，冀以宣主德而厚民生，蓋凜凜如也。執事者猶欲議吏於儒生，顧儒生豈有知乎？抑有說焉。龔遂
translation_en:
…. Yet for those skilled at making an outward display [?], how can one guarantee there is no concealed truth? Too many pointing fingers confuse the sight, and too many voices confuse the hearing; therefore, in recommending and impeaching officials, it is vital that authority be concentrated. Yet as for the Regional Inspectors of the various circuits, who in principle must be entrusted with heavy authority in these matters, those currently in charge already find this difficult to manage. Furthermore, testing officials over time to hold them responsible for results and rewarding them generously to encourage their ambitions—for these reasons, routine promotion rules ought to be broken. Yet if one wishes to place newly advanced men above seasoned veterans, human sentiment will find it unbearable.

On the whole, laws can guard against malfeasance, but they cannot eliminate it completely; incentives and encouragement work upon gentlemen, yet penal severity cannot transform petty men. Moreover, when superiors rely on their eyes, subordinates dress up appearances; when superiors rely on their ears, subordinates dress up their reputation. In hidden and subtle matters, how could one possibly inspect every single detail? Lu Zhi 陸贄 once said: "Emperor Wu of Han 漢武 loved heroic spirit, and so his era was rich in extraordinary men who established their names; Emperor Xuan of Han 漢宣 focused on administrative governance, and so his era gathered upright and capable officials who verified realities." Indeed, the quality of officials simply depends on how they are led from above.

His Sacred Majesty the Son of Heaven has revived the precedent of advancing ranks and bestowing gold, and has furthermore issued gracious decrees praising and encouraging outstanding achievements—attaching far greater weight to them than the imperial letters of former ages. At present, officials great and small have all changed their outlook and sharpened their attention, obeying only His Majesty's commands in the hope of spreading the Sovereign's virtue and enriching the people's livelihood, filled with reverent awe. Yet you, the examiners, still wish to discuss official administration with a Confucian student. How could a mere scholar know anything of value? Even so, there is something that might be said. When Gong Sui 龔遂…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
拜渤海召見請毋拘文法故得以盡生渤
海之民近世如張益州亦得便宜從事而
方面之續稱最今銅章墨綬之長衆庶所
俯伏而敬畏者也而顛息以上不能自主
即欲問疾苦教樹畜而簿書期會有餘功
乎欲行阡陌巡郊野而約束要結敢擅越
乎況敢置數十萬反側不問也謂宜稍寛
其文法使得於筐篋之外有所樹立庶豪
傑不困於掣肘而異績可施也士固有輕
千乘薄萬鍾而蘄於史冊之名者兩漢傳
循吏至今猶豔慕焉
===
國朝名臣如楊廉彭惠安所撰述郡守自況
蘇州外亦寂寂爾矣謂宜令翰苑儒臣采
外郡遺思最著者略倣循吏傳編爲成書
播之中外庶循良之績益彰而思齊者爭
力也漢文帝諭季布曰河東吾股肱郡故
特召君耳光武褒崇卓傳且詔厲郡國後
世觀其君臣相得欣然願生其時人主一
punctuated: 拜渤海，召見，請毋拘文法，故得以盡生渤海之民。近世如張益州，亦得便宜從事，而方面之續稱最。今銅章墨綬之長，衆庶所俯伏而敬畏者也，而顛息以上不能自主。即欲問疾苦、教樹畜，而簿書期會有餘功乎？欲行阡陌、巡郊野，而約束要結敢擅越乎？況敢置數十萬反側不問也？謂宜稍寛其文法，使得於筐篋之外有所樹立，庶豪傑不困於掣肘，而異績可施也。士固有輕千乘、薄萬鍾，而蘄於史冊之名者，兩漢傳循吏，至今猶豔慕焉。國朝名臣如楊廉、彭惠安所撰述，郡守自況蘇州外，亦寂寂爾矣。謂宜令翰苑儒臣，采外郡遺思最著者，略倣《循吏傳》編爲成書，播之中外，庶循良之績益彰，而思齊者爭力也。漢文帝諭季布曰：「河東吾股肱郡，故特召君耳。」光武褒崇卓傳，且詔厲郡國。後世觀其君臣相得，欣然願生其時，人主一
translation_en:
…was appointed to Bohai, upon being summoned for an audience he requested not to be bound by legalistic regulations, and thus he was able to restore the livelihoods of all the people of Bohai. In more recent times, men such as Zhang of Yizhou (Zhang Yong 張詠) were also permitted to act at their own discretion as circumstances required, and their achievements as regional commanders were praised as the finest. Today, the chiefs who wear bronze seals and black ribbons [i.e., county magistrates] are those before whom the common multitude prostrate themselves in reverent awe, yet from the slightest breath upward [?] they cannot act on their own initiative. Even if they wish to inquire into the people's sufferings and teach them arboriculture and animal husbandry, do they have any spare energy left over from account books and scheduled deadlines? If they wish to walk the field paths and tour the rural outskirts, do they dare to overstep the restrictions and binding agreements without authorization? How much less would they dare to leave hundreds of thousands of rebellious and unsettled people unquestioned! I would say that the legalistic regulations upon them should be slightly relaxed, allowing them to establish achievements beyond their document boxes, so that men of outstanding talent will not be hampered by having their elbows restrained, and extraordinary accomplishments may be carried out.

There are indeed scholars who think lightly of a thousand chariots and disdain ten thousand Zhong of grain, seeking instead a name in the pages of history. The biographies of Upright Officials (Xunli 循吏) from the two Han dynasties are still admired and envied to this day. In the accounts compiled by renowned ministers of our own dynasty, such as Yang Lian 楊廉 and Peng of Hui'an (Peng Shao 彭韶, posthumously titled Hui'an 惠安), among prefectural governors, apart from Kuang of Suzhou (Kuang Zhong 況鍾), the record is altogether quiet and sparse. I would say that Confucian officials of the Hanlin Academy should be ordered to gather accounts of those in the outer prefectures who are most famously remembered with fond longing, and compile them into a complete book roughly modeled on the Biographies of Upright Officials (Xunli zhuan 循吏傳), circulating it throughout the court and the provinces, so that the achievements of upright and good officials will become ever more manifest and those who wish to emulate them will strive with all their might.

Emperor Wen of Han instructed Ji Bu 季布, saying: "Hedong is my vital prefecture, and therefore I have specially summoned you." Emperor Guangwu praised and exalted Zhuo [Mao 卓茂] and Fu [Jun 傅俊?], and moreover issued edicts to encourage the commanderies and kingdoms. When later generations observe the mutual understanding between ruler and minister, they gladly wish they had been born in those times. A single [word] from the sovereign…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
言圉榮於華衮也請於
萬幾之暇
上時宣召三輔牧吏問所疾苦而諸長吏考績
入
覲見者時
賜咨詢凡以考其材能庶銜恩知報而感遇
益奮也聞之故老宣弘間風淳俗厚禁防
踈闊吏亦廉潔重自愛後稍陵夷矣今
主上勵精圖治日考百官圖以計安元元爲務
而公卿大臣同心協德明學術正風俗以
佐之羔羊素絲之風可復而唐虞三代之
治不難見矣
===
第五問
馬鍾粹
同考試官教諭王　批〔道德功名富貴三者本相爲用　如子所論不激不隨聖賢求志達道之學不過如此〕
考試官教諭俞　批〔議論偲偲尚志有素者〕
考試官教諭孫　批〔識趣端正所養〕
punctuated:
言，圉榮於華衮也。請於萬幾之暇，上時宣召三輔牧吏，問所疾苦；而諸長吏考績入覲見者，時賜咨詢，凡以考其材能，庶銜恩知報，而感遇益奮也。聞之故老，宣、弘間風淳俗厚，禁防踈闊，吏亦廉潔重自愛，後稍陵夷矣。今主上勵精圖治，日考百官圖，以計安元元爲務，而公卿大臣同心協德，明學術、正風俗以佐之，羔羊素絲之風可復，而唐虞三代之治不難見矣。

第五問
馬鍾粹
同考試官教諭王批〔道德、功名、富貴三者本相爲用。如子所論，不激不隨，聖賢求志達道之學，不過如此。〕
考試官教諭俞批〔議論偲偲，尚志有素者。〕
考試官教諭孫批〔識趣端正，所養〕
translation_en:
… word is more glorious than ceremonial robes [?]. I beg that in His leisure from the myriad affairs of state, His Majesty from time to time summon the prefects and magistrates of the capital region to ask about the hardships of the people, and that when senior territorial administrators enter for an audience upon the evaluation of their merits, He occasionally grant them inquiries—all in order to examine their talents and abilities, so that they may cherish His grace, know to repay it, and be all the more roused with gratitude for the favor they have met. I have heard from the elders that during the Xuande (1426–1435) and Hongzhi (1488–1505) eras, customs and morals were pure and generous, prohibitions and safeguards were broad and unrestrictive, and officials were also incorruptible and set great store by self-respect; later this gradually declined. Now His Majesty devotes His energies to good governance and daily examines the roster of all officials, taking calculations for bringing peace to the common people as His priority, while the dukes, ministers, and great officials unite in heart and virtue to clarify learning and rectify customs so as to assist Him. Thus the ethos of the Ode of the Lambskin and White Silk may be restored, and the governance of Yao, Shun, and the Three Dynasties will not be difficult to behold.

Fifth Question
Ma Zhongcui 馬鍾粹
Associate Examiner, Instructor Wang 王 comments: 〔Morality, meritorious achievement, and wealth and honor originally serve one another in application. As you have argued, neither extreme nor compliant, the learning of the sages and worthies in pursuing their aspirations and bringing the Way to prevail is nothing more than this.〕
Examiner, Instructor Yu 俞 comments: 〔His discourse is earnest and perceptive; he is one who has long cultivated lofty aspirations.〕
Examiner, Instructor Sun 孫 comments: 〔His judgment and inclinations are upright; what he has cultivated …〕

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
許昌靳裁之氏論士而其言曰士之品有
三志於道德者功名不足以累其心志於
功名者富貴不足以累其心有味乎其言
之也然猶有未盡焉夫士脩之於奧㵲而
養之於衡茅非以自爲也所以爲天下也
道德所自有也秉而立之功斯立矣載而
行之名由彰焉雖欲不富貴已胡可得也
是三者非二物也譬之於水流爲川止爲
澤通氣爲雲非二物也而論士者岐之爲
===
三且以是定士品則亦士有以取之也語
曰志燕而燕志越而越士固有志可不早
辨哉是故周之士也貴上貴之也秦之士
也賤上賤之也因上以爲貴賤是功名富
貴士也非所與議於道德者也先王之於
士也於四民之中而特寵異之爲其有是
道德也道成德尊而功立焉王功曰勳國
功曰功民功曰庸事功曰勞治功曰力戰
功曰多銘之太常書之竹帛天下後世曾
punctuated: 許昌靳裁之氏論士，而其言曰：「士之品有三：志於道德者，功名不足以累其心；志於功名者，富貴不足以累其心。」有味乎其言之也，然猶有未盡焉。夫士脩之於奧㵲，而養之於衡茅，非以自爲也，所以爲天下也。道德，所自有也；秉而立之，功斯立矣；載而行之，名由彰焉。雖欲不富貴，已胡可得也？是三者，非二物也。譬之於水：流爲川，止爲澤，通氣爲雲，非二物也。而論士者岐之爲三，且以是定士品，則亦士有以取之也。語曰：「志燕而燕，志越而越。」士固有志，可不早辨哉？是故周之士也貴，上貴之也；秦之士也賤，上賤之也。因上以爲貴賤，是功名富貴士也，非所與議於道德者也。先王之於士也，於四民之中而特寵異之，爲其有是道德也。道成德尊而功立焉：王功曰勳，國功曰功，民功曰庸，事功曰勞，治功曰力，戰功曰多。銘之太常，書之竹帛，天下後世曾
translation_en: Master Jin Caizhi 靳裁之 of Xuchang 許昌 discussed scholars, and his words were: "There are three grades of scholars: for those whose aspirations lie in the Way and its Virtue, achievement and fame are not enough to encumber their minds; for those whose aspirations lie in achievement and fame, wealth and rank are not enough to encumber their minds." How meaningful are his words! Yet there is still something he left unexhausted. Now, a scholar cultivates himself in the inner chambers and nurtures himself beneath a humble thatched roof—not for his own sake, but for the sake of all under Heaven. The Way and its Virtue are what he possesses within himself; when he holds fast to them and establishes them, achievement is thereby established; when he embodies them and puts them into practice, his fame thereby becomes manifest. Even if he wished to avoid wealth and rank, how could he possibly do so? These three are not separate things. Compare them to water: flowing, it becomes a river; still, it becomes a marsh; sending up vapor, it becomes clouds—they are not separate things. That those who discuss scholars split them into three, and moreover use this to determine the grades of scholars, is also something that scholars have brought upon themselves. The proverb says: "Set your mind on Yan 燕 and you reach Yan; set your mind on Yue 越 and you reach Yue." Scholars certainly have their aspirations—how can they not distinguish them early on? Therefore, the scholars of Zhou 周 were noble because their superiors honored them; the scholars of Qin 秦 were base because their superiors despised them. Those who depend on superiors for their nobility or baseness are scholars of achievement, fame, wealth, and rank; they are not the ones with whom to discuss the Way and its Virtue. In the former kings' treatment of scholars, they specially favored and distinguished them among the four classes of people because they possessed this Way and Virtue. When the Way is perfected and Virtue is revered, achievement is established therein: achievement for the king is called royal merit (xun 勳); achievement for the state is called state merit (gong 功); achievement for the people is called civil merit (yong 庸); achievement in affairs is called service merit (lao 勞); achievement in governance is called administrative merit (li 力); achievement in battle is called military merit (duo 多). Engraved upon the Grand Standard (Taichang 太常) and recorded upon bamboo and silk, in all under Heaven and in later generations…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
不得攀躋而望焉名赫然顯矣是功名者
世以此視士士固不知有功名也而況於
富貴乎彼知有功名富貴者皆不升其堂
不嘗其胾者也世士德衰徒見阿衡起畎
畝而升阿尚父出磻谿而爲帝者師以爲
乘時遘會得之而不深求其本於是好名
喜功之徒爭致力焉其下焉者不過誇駟
馬之榮侈名位之寵都厚貲據崇秩以自
豐苟富貴而已矣由是觀之始亦未嘗不
===
相須以致用而其後遂判然離也士亦與
有責焉耳矣漢興酇侯絳侯依日月之末
光何謹守關中轉餉以成帝業赫然佐命
元勳天下既平絳侯誅諸呂匡復社稷卽
袁盎亦不得訾其功是二子者於漢家勳
周召而下孰能遠過然治未央王諸呂稱
制大率皆阿諛順旨而械繫下獄且靦然
不媿其去患得患失無幾耳殆功名富貴
之間乎東京始建則富春畊釣萬乘不能
punctuated: 不得攀躋而望焉，名赫然顯矣。是功名者，世以此視士，士固不知有功名也，而況於富貴乎？彼知有功名富貴者，皆不升其堂、不嘗其胾者也。世士德衰，徒見阿衡起畎畝而升阿，尚父出磻谿而爲帝者師，以爲乘時遘會得之，而不深求其本，於是好名喜功之徒爭致力焉。其下焉者，不過誇駟馬之榮，侈名位之寵，都厚貲，據崇秩，以自豐，苟富貴而已矣。由是觀之，始亦未嘗不相須以致用，而其後遂判然離也，士亦與有責焉耳矣。漢興，酇侯、絳侯依日月之末光。何謹守關中，轉餉以成帝業，赫然佐命元勳；天下既平，絳侯誅諸呂，匡復社稷，卽袁盎亦不得訾其功。是二子者，於漢家勳，周、召而下，孰能遠過？然治未央、王諸呂稱制，大率皆阿諛順旨，而械繫下獄，且靦然不媿，其去患得患失無幾耳，殆功名富貴之間乎！東京始建，則富春畊釣，萬乘不能
translation_en:
… could not even climb up to gaze upon them, and their renown shone forth brilliantly. Thus, as for achievement and fame, the world looks upon scholars in these terms, yet the scholar himself truly has no thought for achievement and fame—how much less for wealth and rank! Those who think only of achievement, fame, wealth, and rank are all people who have never ascended the hall of the Way and Virtue or tasted a slice of their meat. As the virtue of scholars in the world declined, they merely saw how Aheng [Yi Yin 伊尹] rose from the furrowed fields to ascend to the 阿 [court/chief ministership], and how Father Shang [Lü Shang 呂尚] emerged from the Pan Stream (Panxi 磻谿) to become preceptor to an emperor. They supposed that these men attained such positions simply by seizing the moment and meeting with opportunity, without inquiring deeply into their fundamental root; thereupon, those fond of fame and eager for achievement vied to exert themselves toward such ends. Those lower still did no more than boast of the glory of a four-horse carriage and flaunt the favor of fame and position, amassing generous fortunes and occupying lofty ranks to enrich themselves, caring haphazardly for wealth and rank and nothing more. Viewed in this light, in the beginning these qualities did not fail to depend on one another to be put to practical use, yet afterward they diverged sharply from one another; for this, scholars too must share the blame!

When the Han arose, the Marquis of Zan [Xiao He 蕭何] and the Marquis of Jiang [Zhou Bo 周勃] relied upon the trailing radiance of the sun and moon. Xiao He carefully guarded Guanzhong and transported provisions to bring the imperial enterprise to completion, standing out brilliantly as the foremost meritoriouschen of the founding mandate. Once the realm was pacified, the Marquis of Jiang executed the Lü 呂 clan and restored the altars of soil and grain; even Yuan Ang 袁盎 could not disparage his achievement. As for the merit of these two men toward the House of Han, from the Dukes of Zhou 周公 and Shao 召公 downward, who could far surpass them? Yet in the construction of the Weiyang Palace and the enfeoffment of the Lüs as kings under the Empress's regency, for the most part they flattered and complied with imperial wishes; and when put in fetters and cast into prison, they moreover felt no shame on their faces. They were not far removed from those who worry about gaining office and worry about losing it—were they not hovering between achievement and fame on the one hand, and wealth and rank on the other?

When the Eastern Capital was first established, there was the one who plowed and fished at Fuchun [Yan Guang 嚴光], whom the lord of ten thousand chariots could not…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
加是所謂泥塗軒冕昭揭日月者太原周
黨辭祿食貧亦各行其志也梁鴻傭會稽
而義行於妻子冀缺恭敬昭德何以尚焉
管寧度遼入海潔身去亂曹氏不能汙斯
亦高士之大槩已諸若申屠接傳於河華
德公肥遯於鹿門韓伯休逃名於藥肆徐
孺子高蹈於南州彬彬未易悉數是豈不
謂亭亭物表皎皎塵外度白雪而干青雲
者哉雖然謂之能遺功名富貴則可謂之
===
道德則不可夫所不有於功名者謂其隨
世以就也使建立必本於道德則功名何
可後即匪功名道德奚自見也所不有於
富貴者謂其貪位以苟也使名寵恒稱其
事業則富貴何可輕即匪富貴功名奚自
顯也而兩漢之士方且甘於其所慕而仇
於其所棄其下焉者既以為重器大寶而
其高焉者且以為腐鼠土苴斯二者皆過
也巢許洗耳而論士於唐虞者不以箕潁
punctuated: 加，是所謂泥塗軒冕、昭揭日月者。太原周黨辭祿食貧，亦各行其志也。梁鴻傭會稽而義行於妻子，冀缺恭敬昭德，何以尚焉？管寧度遼入海，潔身去亂，曹氏不能汙，斯亦高士之大槩已。諸若申屠接傳於河華，德公肥遯於鹿門，韓伯休逃名於藥肆，徐孺子高蹈於南州，彬彬未易悉數。是豈不謂亭亭物表、皎皎塵外，度白雪而干青雲者哉？雖然，謂之能遺功名富貴則可，謂之道德則不可。夫所不有於功名者，謂其隨世以就也；使建立必本於道德，則功名何可後？即匪功名，道德奚自見也？所不有於富貴者，謂其貪位以苟也；使名寵恒稱其事業，則富貴何可輕？即匪富貴，功名奚自顯也？而兩漢之士，方且甘於其所慕，而仇於其所棄。其下焉者，既以為重器大寶；而其高焉者，且以為腐鼠土苴。斯二者皆過也。巢、許洗耳，而論士於唐、虞者，不以箕、潁
translation_en: … impose upon him; this is what is meant by treating high carriages and official caps as mud and holding one's integrity as bright as the sun and moon. Zhou Dang 周黨 of Taiyuan declined office to live in poverty; each simply carried out his own resolution. Liang Hong 梁鴻 hired himself out as a laborer in Kuaiji, yet righteous conduct was practiced between husband and wife; even Ji Que 冀缺, whose reverence and respect made bright his virtue—how could he surpass this? Guan Ning 管寧 crossed the Liao River and took to the sea, keeping himself pure and leaving disorder behind so that the Cao 曹 clan could not sully him; such was also the general manner of a lofty gentleman. As for others—like Shentu蟠 [Shentu Pan] taking transient lodging between the Yellow River and Mount Hua, Pang Degong 龐德公 retiring contentedly to Lumen Mountain, Han Boxiu 韓伯休 [Han Kang 韓康] fleeing fame in a medicine shop, and Xu Ruzi 徐孺子 [Xu Zhi 徐穉] treading loftily in Nanzhou—they were so numerous in their refinement that they cannot easily be counted in full. Could these not be called men who stood towering above the material world and gleamingly pure beyond the dusty realm, surpassing the white snow and reaching into the blue clouds? Even so, to say that they were able to cast aside merit, fame, wealth, and rank is permissible, but to call this the Way and its Virtue is not. Now, what is unworthy in merit and fame is that one merely conforms to the age to achieve them; if one's achievements are necesariamente rooted in the Way and its Virtue, then how can merit and fame be put last? Indeed, without merit and fame, how can the Way and its Virtue manifest themselves? What is unworthy in wealth and rank is that one covets position to get by ignobly; if renown and favor always match one's accomplishments, then how can wealth and rank be slighted? Indeed, without wealth and rank, how can merit and fame become illustrious? Yet the scholars of the Two Han dynasties were just theneither indulging gladly in what they yearned for or treating as an enemy what they spurned. Those of the lower sort regarded them as precious vessels and great treasures, while those of the loftier sort regarded them as rotten rats and dirt or dregs. Both of these are excesses. Chao Fu 巢父 and Xu You 許由 washed their ears, yet those who judge worthies in the eras of Tang and Yu do not, on account of the loftiness of Mount Ji and the Ying River…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
之高而薄臯夔稷契伯夷叔齊恥周粟而
餓首陽而論士於周者不以畢畢散周召
何至甘華麗之悅心望非常之絕世希蹤
竹帛而馳情大蒸者哉亦何至慷慨絕俗
瀟灑外方厭煩情於飄聲而恥受汗於名
姓者哉蓋嘗論之有功名之功名有道德
之功名有富貴之富貴有道德之富貴用
之而道德則功名富貴亦道德也用之而
功名則道德亦功名也用之而富貴則功
===
名亦富貴也後車數十乘從者數百人在
孟氏則爲食功在儀秦則爲妾婦千乘之
國六七十里之邦在孔門則爲行義在漢
儒則爲宦達亦顧其所志何如耳是故存
乎始辨焉不爲威怵不爲利回所以貞介
也寧爲蠖屈不爲尋直所以明守也其文
易詩書禮樂春秋其倫君臣父子夫婦昆
弟朋友其德仁義禮智所以盡性也十年
離經辨志又十年知類通達又十年強立
punctuated: 之高而薄臯、夔、稷、契；伯夷、叔齊恥周粟而餓首陽，而論士於周者，不以畢、畢、散、周、召。何至甘華麗之悅心，望非常之絕世，希蹤竹帛，而馳情大蒸者哉？亦何至慷慨絕俗，瀟灑外方，厭煩情於飄聲，而恥受汗於名姓者哉？蓋嘗論之：有功名之功名，有道德之功名；有富貴之富貴，有道德之富貴。用之而道德，則功名、富貴亦道德也；用之而功名，則道德亦功名也；用之而富貴，則功名亦富貴也。後車數十乘，從者數百人，在孟氏則爲食功，在儀、秦則爲妾婦；千乘之國，六七十里之邦，在孔門則爲行義，在漢儒則爲宦達，亦顧其所志何如耳。是故存乎始辨焉。不爲威怵，不爲利回，所以貞介也；寧爲蠖屈，不爲尋直，所以明守也。其文《易》、《詩》、《書》、《禮》、《樂》、《春秋》，其倫君臣、父子、夫婦、昆弟、朋友，其德仁、義、禮、智，所以盡性也；十年離經辨志，又十年知類通達，又十年強立
translation_en:
… the loftiness of [Mount Ji and the Ying River] to disparage Gao Yao, Kui, Hou Ji, and Xie. Bo Yi and Shu Qi were ashamed to eat the grain of Zhou and starved on Mount Shouyang, yet those who evaluate scholars in the Zhou era do not thereby [belittle ?] Bi [Gong], San [Yisheng], the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao. Why should one go so far as to indulge in splendors that please the heart, hope for extraordinary feats that surpass the age, aspire to leave one's trace on bamboo and silk, and let one's passions race after the grandwinter sacrifice [in the ancestral temple]? And why should one go so far as to indignantly cut oneself off from the world, remain aloof beyond the realm, loathe the annoyance of the sound of a hanging gourd, and feel ashamed to have one's name sullied?

Indeed, if we discuss it: there is the merit and fame of mere merit and fame, and there is the merit and fame of morality and virtue; there is the wealth and rank of mere wealth and rank, and there is the wealth and rank of morality and virtue. If one employs them through morality and virtue, then merit, fame, wealth, and rank are also morality and virtue; if one employs them for merit and fame, then morality and virtue are also mere merit and fame; if one employs them for wealth and rank, then merit and fame are also mere wealth and rank. To have several dozen carriages following behind and several hundred attendants—for Mencius, this was being supported in accordance with one's merit, whereas for Zhang Yi and Su Qin, it was the way of concubines and wives. To govern a state of a thousand chariots or a territory of sixty or seventy li—for the disciples of Confucius, this was practicing righteousness, whereas for the scholars of the Han, it was merely achieving official advancement. It simply depends on what one's aspiration is.

Therefore, everything lies in making the distinction at the very beginning. Not being intimidated by awe and not being deflected by profit is the means to keep one's integrity firm; preferring to curl up like an inchworm rather than bend a principle to gain eight feet is the means to make clear one's moral steadfastness. Having for one's cultural texts the Book of Changes (Yi), the Book of Odes (Shi), the Book of Documents (Shu), the Record of Rites (Li), the Book of Music (Yue), and the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu); having for one's human relationships those between ruler and minister, father and son, husband and wife, elder and younger brother, and friend and friend; and having for one's virtues benevolence, righteousness, propriety, and wisdom—this is the means to fully realize one's nature. Taking ten years to punctuate the texts and discern one's aspirations, another ten years to understand categories and achieve thorough comprehension, and another ten years to stand firm…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
不反所以厚養也不特此耳飽仁義以爲
膏粱而蒿目怵中常有當世之憂令聞廣
譽以爲文繡而側身常若不及師友義皇
蜉蝣宇宙一琴一瑟足以自樂而必於轍
環天下席不暇煖巖居川觀侶烟霞而友
泉石足以自適而必於胝無胈膚不毛是
豈有藉於人哉凡以爲道德也士君子固
非能遺人倫逃宇宙也非能鳥獸之爲羣
而草木之與同朽也食不求飽而未嘗不
===
食居不求安而未嘗不居功名富貴不以
爲吾性累而非能外功名富貴以爲性是
皆生民之不可一日無者也無之是無人
類也譬之雲飛川流唐虞事業孔孟述作
吾無容心焉耳矣伊尹之幡然而出也堯
舜君民以先知覺後知以先覺覺後覺也
雖五就湯五就桀而不以爲煩論者曰是
固一介不取與之伊尹也柳士師三黜不
去油油然與之偕齒於後世以爲不恭富
punctuated: 不反，所以厚養也。不特此耳，飽仁義以爲膏粱，而蒿目怵中，常有當世之憂；令聞廣譽以爲文繡，而側身常若不及。師友義皇，蜉蝣宇宙，一琴一瑟足以自樂，而必於轍環天下，席不暇煖；巖居川觀，侶烟霞而友泉石，足以自適，而必於胝無胈、膚不毛。是豈有藉於人哉？凡以爲道德也。士君子固非能遺人倫、逃宇宙也，非能鳥獸之爲羣、而草木之與同朽也。食不求飽，而未嘗不食；居不求安，而未嘗不居。功名富貴不以爲吾性累，而非能外功名富貴以爲性。是皆生民之不可一日無者也，無之是無人類也。譬之雲飛川流，唐虞事業，孔孟述作，吾無容心焉耳矣。伊尹之幡然而出也，堯舜君民，以先知覺後知，以先覺覺後覺也；雖五就湯、五就桀而不以爲煩。論者曰：是固一介不取與之伊尹也。柳士師三黜不去，油油然與之偕，齒於後世以爲不恭富…
translation_en: … without wavering—this is how one enriches one's cultivation. Not only this: though one feasts on benevolence and righteousness as if they were fine meats and grain, one's eyes remain troubled and one's heart anxious, constantly harboring concern for the present age; though one wears a good reputation and wide renown as if they were embroidered robes, one conducts oneself with apprehension as if never doing enough. Taking Fuxi [義皇 for 羲皇] as teacher and friend, viewing the cosmos as ephemera, a single zither and harp would suffice for self-delight—yet one insists on traveling in circuits around the world, one's mat never staying warm. Dwelling among crags and contemplating streams, taking mist and clouds as companions and springs and rocks as friends, would suffice for self-contentment—yet one insists on toiling until one's calluses have no fine hair and one's skin is worn bare. Does this rely on anything from others? All of it is done for the sake of the Way and its Virtue. Indeed, a scholar and gentleman cannot abandon human relationships or flee the universe; he cannot flock together with birds and beasts or rot away alongside grass and trees. In eating he does not seek satiety, yet he never ceases to eat; in dwelling he does not seek comfort, yet he never ceases to dwell. Meritorious achievement, fame, wealth, and honor are not allowed to encumber our human nature, yet we cannot exclude achievement, fame, wealth, and honor in order to constitute our nature. These are all things that the living people cannot do without for a single day; to be without them would mean the end of humanity. It is like the flying of clouds and the flowing of streams: whether it is the grand enterprises of Yao and Shun (Tang and Yu) or the writings and transmissions of Confucius and Mencius, we harbor no ulterior deliberation in them at all. When Yi Yin 尹伊 changed course and stepped forth into service, it was to make his ruler and people like Yao and Shun, using his prior knowledge to awaken those slow to know, and his prior awareness to awaken those slow to be aware; even going five times to Tang and five times to Jie, he did not consider it troublesome. Commentators say: this was indeed the very same Yi Yin who would neither take nor give a single straw improperly. When Liuxia Hui, as Chief Criminal Judge (柳士師), was dismissed three times without leaving, he remained cheerfully at ease alongside others; had he been judged in a later age, he would have been regarded merely as someone irreverent and attached to wealth and…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
貴之人耳孟子乃稱其不以三公易介而
斯以談功名富貴亦何必岐道德而二之
哉嗟夫依乎中庸君子爲難而紛華靡麗
常情易動求士於三代之下何容易哉上
之人縣富貴以待之恐恐然惟懼其不稱
也毋論道德即功名不敢以信士下之人
望富貴而企之恐恐然惟懼其不得也毋
論道德即功名不敢以自信父以詔子兄
以詔弟自非卓然自信鮮不駸駸入之矣
===
至謂今之道德即古之功名今之功名即
古之富貴不幾于輕天下士而視道德爲
殊絶耶然則士宜何如曰志伊尹之所志
又曰先天下之憂而憂後天下之樂而樂
噫微斯人吾誰與歸
punctuated: 貴之人耳，孟子乃稱其「不以三公易介」。而斯以談，功名富貴亦何必岐道德而二之哉？嗟夫！依乎中庸，君子爲難，而紛華靡麗，常情易動，求士於三代之下，何容易哉！上之人縣富貴以待之，恐恐然惟懼其不稱也；毋論道德，即功名不敢以信士。下之人望富貴而企之，恐恐然惟懼其不得也；毋論道德，即功名不敢以自信。父以詔子，兄以詔弟，自非卓然自信，鮮不駸駸入之矣。至謂今之道德即古之功名，今之功名即古之富貴，不幾于輕天下士而視道德爲殊絶耶？然則士宜何如？曰：「志伊尹之所志。」又曰：「先天下之憂而憂，後天下之樂而樂。」噫！微斯人，吾誰與歸！
translation_en: …and honors; yet Mencius praised him for "not exchanging his firm resolution for the rank of the Three Dukes." Viewed in this light, why must merit, fame, wealth, and honors be separated from morality and virtue as two distinct things? Alas! To abide by the Mean is difficult even for the noble man, whereas the ordinary mind is easily stirred by華麗 splendor and extravagance; how could it be easy to seek true scholars after the Three Dynasties! Those above dangle wealth and honors to await them, anxiously fearing only that they will not measure up; to say nothing of morality and virtue, they do not even dare to trust scholars with regard to merit and fame. Those below gaze upon wealth and honors and tiptoe after them, anxiously fearing only that they will not obtain them; to say nothing of morality and virtue, they do not even dare to have confidence in themselves with regard to merit and fame. Fathers instruct their sons in this, and elder brothers instruct their younger brothers; unless one is of towering self-confidence, few do not gradually sink deep into it. As for the saying that today's morality and virtue are merely antiquity's merit and fame, and today's merit and fame are merely antiquity's wealth and honors, does this not come close to belittling the scholars of the world and regarding morality and virtue as utterly beyond reach? How, then, ought a scholar to conduct himself? It is said: "Set your ambition on what Yi Yin 伊尹 set his ambition on." And it is also said: "Be the first to worry about the world's worries, and the last to enjoy the world's joys." Ah! Without such a person, with whom would I keep company?

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
河南鄉試錄後序
今皇帝臨御天下甫四年而天下
郡國鄉貢士再舉矣頃中州
之役御史趙〔煥〕寔奉
明命臨之業已按故實申約束其
自藩臬長貳以及庶官百執
事罔不夙夜寅恭翌襄
盛典已得士成賢能書〔應星〕當
===
屬一言其後昔梅福慨選舉
之法不足以得當世士鄉疑
以爲然今乃知其無當福漢
人也狹小漢制有激乎其言
之耳我
國家三歲一比士昉于周官而
punctuated:
河南鄉試錄後序

今皇帝臨御天下，甫四年而天下郡國鄉貢士再舉矣。頃中州之役，御史趙〔煥〕寔奉明命臨之，業已按故實、申約束，其自藩臬長貳以及庶官百執事，罔不夙夜寅恭，翌襄盛典。已得士，成賢能書，〔應星〕當屬一言其後。昔梅福慨選舉之法不足以得當世士，鄉疑以爲然，今乃知其無當。福，漢人也，狹小漢制，有激乎其言之耳。我國家三歲一比士，昉于《周官》，而
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Henan Provincial Examination

Our reigning Emperor has ruled the realm for barely four years, and already the tribute scholars from the commanderies and principalities across the empire have been selected for the second time in the Provincial Examinations. For this recent undertaking in the Central Plain [Henan], Investigating Censor Zhao [Huan 趙煥] truly received the illustrious mandate to supervise it. After he had examined the precedents and reiterated the regulations, everyone from the chiefs and deputies of the Provincial Administration Commission and Surveillance Commission down to the various officials and hundred functionaries worked withreverent diligence day and night to assist in this grand ceremony. Now that the scholars have been selected and the register of the worthy and capable has been completed, it falls to me, [Yingxing 應星], to append a few words at the end.

In the past, Mei Fu 梅福 lamented that the methods of selection and recommendation were inadequate for obtaining the scholars of the age. Formerly I was inclined to think this was so, but now I know his view to be unfounded. Fu was a man of the Han dynasty; he belittled the Han system and spoke out of indignation. Our dynasty examines and compares scholars once every three years, a practice originating in the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), and…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
以三日竭其兼才則劉邵有
之彼所爲一論道德一論法
制一論策術蓋秩秩今日事
而與書德行道藝獻天府者
其旨固同然則士患其負所
舉耳舉何負於士哉乃中州
之士則有舉之不能盡者才
===
以地傑亦以時盛也夫戳沙
磧而不窺玉淵者不知驪龍
之所蟠也習邑屋而不覩上
邦者不知豪傑之所躔也中
州中天地而和氣萃焉其人
龍之淵乎按五嶽而嵩高鎮
其中九州而豫冀聯其二十
punctuated: 以三日竭其兼才，則劉邵有之。彼所爲一論道德、一論法制、一論策術，蓋秩秩今日事，而與書德行、道藝獻天府者，其旨固同。然則士患其負所舉耳，舉何負於士哉？乃中州之士，則有舉之不能盡者，才以地傑，亦以時盛也。夫戳沙磧而不窺玉淵者，不知驪龍之所蟠也；習邑屋而不覩上邦者，不知豪傑之所躔也。中州中天地而和氣萃焉，其人龍之淵乎？按五嶽而嵩高鎮其一，九州而豫、冀聯其二，十
translation_en: … taking three days to exhaust their comprehensive talents is something already found in Liu Shao 劉邵. What he described—first discussing morality and virtue, second discussing laws and institutions, and third discussing policy and statecraft—corresponds in an orderly manner to the practice of today, and its underlying principle is indeed identical with the ancient practice of recording moral conduct and expertise in the Way and the arts and presenting them to the Sacred Repository. If that is so, then scholars should only worry about failing to live up to the examination that selects them; how does the selection system ever fail the scholars? Yet among the scholars of the Central Region (Henan), there are more talents than the examinations can fully encompass, for talent excels by virtue of the land and also flourishes by virtue of the times. Truly, one who pokes into sandy wastes without peering into a jade-filled abyss does not know where the black dragon coils; one who is accustomed only to village dwellings without beholding the great states does not know where heroes and outstanding men tread. The Central Region stands at the center of Heaven and Earth, where harmonious vital energy gathers—is it not the very abyss of human dragons? Consider the Five Sacred Peaks: Mount Song 嵩高 presides over it; of the Nine Provinces, Yu 豫 and Ji 冀 are joined within it as two; of the Fifteen…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
五國風而二南以下居其九
茲豈獨以形勝甲天下卽帝
王故都聖賢遺蹟披圖不可
勝攬而龍圖龜書神筴寶鼎
之類則又異靈所鍾杳妙莫
測天之開斯文也千古其一
日乎我
===
國家都燕撫有萬國中州首當
其南面承瓴水之勢而爲天
下職貢先雖班固頌明堂張
衡擬天府未盡也以故鴻儒
碩輔忠臣烈士類多代與其
鄉風業光美先後爲
國家重
punctuated: 五國風而二南以下居其九。茲豈獨以形勝甲天下？卽帝王故都、聖賢遺蹟，披圖不可勝攬；而龍圖、龜書、神筴、寶鼎之類，則又異靈所鍾，杳妙莫測。天之開斯文也，千古其一日乎！我國家都燕，撫有萬國，中州首當其南面，承瓴水之勢，而爲天下職貢先，雖班固頌明堂、張衡擬天府，未盡也。以故鴻儒碩輔、忠臣烈士，類多代與，其鄉風業光美，先後爲國家重。
translation_en:
… of the Airs of the Fifteen States (Shiwu Guofeng), from the Two Nan (Er Nan) on down, it accounts for nine. How is this merely because its strategic topography is first under Heaven? Even as for the former capitals of emperors and kings and the remaining traces of sages and worthies, if one unrolls the maps, they are too numerous to take in all at once; while such things as the Dragon Chart, the Tortoise Writing, the Divine Milfoil Stalks, and the Precious Tripods are furthermore where extraordinary numinous forces have concentrated, abstruse and unfathomable. In Heaven's opening up of This Culture (siwen), are not a thousand ages just like a single day?

Our dynasty has established its capital at Yan [Beijing] and holds sway over the myriad states. The Central Prefectures (Zhongzhou, i.e., Henan) are the very first to face it to the south, receiving the momentum of water poured from a rooftop pitcher, and standing at the forefront of tribute and service from all under Heaven; even Ban Gu 班固 praising the Hall of Light (Mingtang) or Zhang Heng 張衡 comparing it to the Storehouses of Heaven (Tianfu) could not exhaustedly describe it. For this reason, great Confucians and eminent chief ministers, loyal officials and heroic gentlemen have mostly arisen here from generation to generation [reading 代興 for 代與]; the local customs and achievements are glorious and admirable, and one after another they have been of great weight to the state.

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
今皇帝又以
神聖之資履
熈洽之運稽古敬學明目達聰
日親師保大臣脩舉
祖宗朝實政
明詔屢下側席天下真才與之分
猷共理諸士褎然起中州雲
===
蒸霧合嚮用
聖明之世其視四方之選爲盛豈
偶然哉然予猶謂舉士於中
州誠易而士不負所舉則中
州爲獨難盖中州造自羲禹
湯文而伊傅周召所當經營
者也其道不泯故其風足以
punctuated: 今皇帝又以神聖之資，履熈洽之運，稽古敬學，明目達聰，日親師保大臣，脩舉祖宗朝實政。明詔屢下，側席天下真才，與之分猷共理。諸士褎然起中州，雲蒸霧合，嚮用聖明之世，其視四方之選爲盛，豈偶然哉？然予猶謂舉士於中州誠易，而士不負所舉，則中州爲獨難。盖中州造自羲、禹、湯、文，而伊、傅、周、召所當經營者也。其道不泯，故其風足以
translation_en: Now, His Majesty the Emperor, moreover endowed with divine and sage qualities and treading upon an era of prosperous harmony, examines antiquity and reveres learning, keeps his eyes clear and his hearing acute, daily draws close to his Grand Preceptors, Grand Guardians, and great ministers, and revives and implements the substantive governance of the ancestral reigns. Bright edicts have repeatedly been handed down as he eagerly awaits true talents from across the realm to share in his counsels and govern together with him. That all of you scholars have risen preeminently from the Central Plain, gathering like rising clouds and converging mists to answer the call of service in an age of sage enlightenment, flourishing even more than those selected from the four quarters—how could this be mere coincidence? Yet I would still say that while selecting scholars in the Central Plain is truly easy, for those scholars not to fail the expectations of their selection is uniquely difficult in the Central Plain. For the Central Plain was founded by Fuxi 伏羲, Yu 禹, Tang 湯, and King Wen 文王, and was the very realm administered by Yi Yin 伊尹, Fu Yue 傅說, the Duke of Zhou 周公, and the Duke of Shao 召公. Their Way has not perished, and therefore their ethos suffices to…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
興人於千百世後無論見知
聞知即有待而興亦豪傑之
徒也猶之粤無鎛夫人而能
爲鎛也燕無函夫人而能爲
函也爲中州士者不已難乎
今數聖人遐不可望矣士有
賢如仲山甫國僑蘧瑗其人
===
者乎得一二輩以應
皇上側席之求固無異圖書再出
而鼎彛朝暮見也才難不其
然乎且士有先資必有成信
用士有敷言必有試功尚父
不曰有馬其狀如驥天下之
至良也然驅之不前却之不
punctuated: 興人於千百世後。無論見知、聞知，即有待而興，亦豪傑之徒也。猶之粤無鎛，夫人而能爲鎛也；燕無函，夫人而能爲函也。爲中州士者，不已難乎？今數聖人遐不可望矣，士有賢如仲山甫、國僑、蘧瑗其人者乎？得一二輩以應皇上側席之求，固無異圖書再出而鼎彛朝暮見也。「才難」，不其然乎？且士有先資，必有成信；用士有敷言，必有試功。尚父不曰：「有馬其狀如驥，天下之至良也，然驅之不前，却之不…
translation_en: …inspire people hundreds and thousands of generations later. Not to mention those who knew the Way by seeing it or knew it by hearing of it—even those who await such models in order to rise up are men of heroic caliber. It is just as the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) says: "In Yue there are no specialized hoe-smiths, because everyone is able to make hoes; in Yan there are no specialized armorers, because everyone is able to make armor." To be a scholar of the Central Plain—is that not especially difficult? Nowadays those several sages are distant and beyond reach, yet are there among the scholars men as worthy as Zhong Shanfu 仲山甫, Guo Qiao 國僑 (Zichan 子產), and Qu Yuan 蘧瑗 (Qu Boyu 蘧伯玉)? To obtain one or two such men to answer His Majesty's eager search for talent—waiting on the edge of his mat—would indeed be no different from the River Chart and Luo Writing appearing once again, or the sacred tripods and ritual vessels being seen morning and evening. "Talent is difficult to find"—is it not truly so? Moreover, when a scholar presents his initial pledge of service, he must substantiate it with proven trustworthiness; when employing scholars, if they set forth their words, they must be tested by their achievements. Did not Grand Father (Shangfu 尚父, i.e.吕尚 Lü Shang) say: "Suppose there is a horse whose appearance is like that of a thoroughbred steed (ji 驥)—the finest in the world; yet when driven forward it does not advance, when reined back it does not…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
止左之不左右之不右則臧
獲雖賤不托其足夫馬不能
欺人以駑良而士之名實可
知已今士以文遇有司有司
亦即以文之名遇士一日受
事則
朝廷之所委者實政而其所急
===
者眞才也士自度苟非其眞
雖日口實數聖人爲名高而
其究曽樊侯鄭衞二大夫不
逮焉其下者干澤自潤無所
賴於公家行文罔而已安在
其爲中州士乎故圜丘之器
不玉明堂之木不琱貴其質
punctuated: 止，左之不左，右之不右，則臧獲雖賤，不托其足。夫馬不能欺人以駑良，而士之名實可知已。今士以文遇有司，有司亦即以文之名遇士。一日受事，則朝廷之所委者實政，而其所急者眞才也。士自度苟非其眞，雖日口實數聖人爲名高，而其究曽樊侯、鄭、衞二大夫不逮焉；其下者干澤自潤，無所賴於公家，行文罔而已。安在其爲中州士乎？故圜丘之器不玉，明堂之木不琱，貴其質
translation_en: …stop; turn it left and it does not go left; turn it right and it does not go right—then even lowly bondservants would not entrust their feet to it. Now, if a horse cannot deceive people as to whether it is a nag or a thoroughbred, then how it stands with the reputation and reality of scholars can readily be known! Today, scholars meet the authorities through their literary compositions, and the authorities likewise meet scholars on the basis of their literary reputation. Yet once they take up office, what the Court entrusts to them is substantive governance, and what it urgently requires is genuine talent. If a scholar examines himself and lacks that genuine substance, then even if he daily cites several sages to elevate his reputation, in the end he will not even measure up to the Marquis of Fan [Zhong Shanfu 仲山甫] or the two grandees of Zheng [Guoqiao 國僑] and Wei [Qu Yuan 蘧瑗]. Those who are worse still seek official favor to enrich themselves, offering nothing of benefit to the state and merely practicing literary deception. Wherein, then, lies their character as scholars of the Central Plains [Henan]? Therefore, the vessels of the Round Mound altar are not made of jade, and the timber of the Hall of Light is left uncarved, because what is valued is that their substance…

title: 萬曆四年河南鄉試錄
text:
而有用也石田千里不可耕
象人百萬不可使聦其多而
無用也夫士許
國在今日而自許乃身亦在今
日故敢以名實之義申告之
直隷鎮江府丹陽縣儒學敎
諭俞〔應星〕謹序
punctuated:
而有用也。石田千里，不可耕；象人百萬，不可使；聦其多而無用也。夫士許國在今日，而自許乃身亦在今日，故敢以名實之義申告之。

直隷鎮江府丹陽縣儒學敎諭俞〔應星〕謹序。
translation_en:
… and are useful. A thousand li of stony fields cannot be plowed; a million effigies of men cannot be employed—they are despised [?] for being numerous yet useless. Now, a scholar's pledging himself to the state begins today, and his expectations for his own person also begin today; therefore I have ventured to repeatedly admonish them with the principle of name and reality.

Respectfully prefaced by Yu [Yingxing], Instructor of the Confucian School of Danyang County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Area (Zhili).
